segs.p: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.1
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.1

segs.p: 1. Āhuneyyavagga
segs.e: 1. Worthy of Offerings

segs.p: Paṭhamaāhuneyyasutta
segs.e: Worthy of Offerings (1st)

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: “bhikkhavo”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants!”

segs.p: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who, when they see a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

segs.p: Sotena saddaṁ sutvā …
segs.e: When they hear a sound with their ears …

segs.p: ghānena gandhaṁ ghāyitvā …
segs.e: When they smell an odor with their nose …

segs.p: jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā …
segs.e: When they taste a flavor with their tongue …

segs.p: kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṁ phusitvā …
segs.e: When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

segs.p: Idamavoca bhagavā.
segs.e: That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.2
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.2

segs.p: 1. Āhuneyyavagga
segs.e: 1. Worthy of Offerings

segs.p: Dutiyaāhuneyyasutta
segs.e: Worthy of Offerings (2nd)

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhoti—ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṁ tirobhāvaṁ; tirokuṭṭaṁ tiropākāraṁ tiropabbataṁ asajjamāno gacchati, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karoti, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchati, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamati, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasati parimajjati; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vatteti.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. They control the body as far as the realm of divinity.

segs.p: Dibbāya, sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāti—dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca.
segs.e: With clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

segs.p: Parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.

segs.p: Sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāti,
segs.e: They understand mind with greed as ‘mind with greed’,

segs.p: vītarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: and mind without greed as ‘mind without greed’.

segs.p: sadosaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: They understand mind with hate …

segs.p: vītadosaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind without hate …

segs.p: samohaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind with delusion …

segs.p: vītamohaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind without delusion …

segs.p: saṅkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: constricted mind …

segs.p: vikkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: scattered mind …

segs.p: mahaggataṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: expansive mind …

segs.p: amahaggataṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: unexpansive mind …

segs.p: sauttaraṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind that is not supreme …

segs.p: anuttaraṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind that is supreme …

segs.p: samāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind immersed in samādhi …

segs.p: asamāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind not immersed in samādhi …

segs.p: vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: freed mind …

segs.p: avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand unfreed mind as ‘unfreed mind’.

segs.p: Anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo …pe…. Iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: They recollect many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti: ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds: ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: Āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.

segs.p: Indriyasutta
segs.e: Faculties

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Saddhindriyena, vīriyindriyena, satindriyena, samādhindriyena, paññindriyena, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

segs.p: Paṭhamaājānīyasutta
segs.e: The Thoroughbred (1st)

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅgantveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with six factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño bhadro assājānīyo khamo hoti rūpānaṁ, khamo saddānaṁ, khamo gandhānaṁ, khamo rasānaṁ, khamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ, vaṇṇasampanno ca hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a fine royal thoroughbred can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches. And it’s beautiful.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅgantveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A fine royal thoroughbred with these six factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khamo hoti rūpānaṁ, khamo saddānaṁ, khamo gandhānaṁ, khamo rasānaṁ, khamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ, khamo dhammānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.

segs.p: Anuttariyasutta
segs.e: Unsurpassable

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, anuttariyāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six things are unsurpassable.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ, anussatānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: The unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha anuttariyānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six unsurpassable things.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Anussatiṭṭhānasutta
segs.e: Topics for Recollection

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, anussatiṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these six topics for recollection.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Buddhānussati, dhammānussati, saṅghānussati, sīlānussati, cāgānussati, devatānussati.
segs.e: The recollection of the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, ethics, generosity, and the deities.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six topics for recollection.”

segs.p: Mahānāmasutta
segs.e: With Mahānāma

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno, kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “yo so, bhante, ariyasāvako āgataphalo viññātasāsano, so katamena vihārena bahulaṁ viharatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, when a noble disciple has reached the fruit and understood the instructions, what kind of meditation do they frequently practice?”

segs.p: “Yo so, mahānāma, ariyasāvako āgataphalo viññātasāsano, so iminā vihārena bahulaṁ viharati.
segs.e: “Mahānāma, when a noble disciple has reached the fruit and understood the instructions they frequently practice this kind of meditation.

segs.p: Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako tathāgataṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple recollects the Realized One:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako tathāgataṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the Realized One their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti tathāgataṁ ārabbha.
segs.e: At that time their mind is quite unswerving, based on the Realized One.

segs.p: Ujugatacitto kho pana, mahānāma, ariyasāvako labhati atthavedaṁ, labhati dhammavedaṁ, labhati dhammūpasaṁhitaṁ pāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: A noble disciple whose mind is unswerving finds inspiration in the meaning and the teaching, and finds joy connected with the teaching.

segs.p: Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
segs.e: When they’re joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss. And when they’re blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, mahānāma:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako visamagatāya pajāya samappatto viharati, sabyāpajjāya pajāya abyāpajjo viharati, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno buddhānussatiṁ bhāveti’.
segs.e: a noble disciple who lives in balance among people who are unbalanced, and lives untroubled among people who are troubled. They’ve entered the stream of the teaching and develop the recollection of the Buddha.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, mahānāma, ariyasāvako dhammaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako dhammaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the teaching their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti dhammaṁ ārabbha.
Ujugatacitto kho pana, mahānāma, ariyasāvako labhati atthavedaṁ, labhati dhammavedaṁ, labhati dhammūpasaṁhitaṁ pāmojjaṁ.
Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
Ayaṁ vuccati, mahānāma:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako visamagatāya pajāya samappatto viharati, sabyāpajjāya pajāya abyāpajjo viharati, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno dhammānussatiṁ bhāveti’.
segs.e: a noble disciple who lives in balance among people who are unbalanced, and lives untroubled among people who are troubled. They’ve entered the stream of the teaching and develop the recollection of the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, mahānāma, ariyasāvako saṅghaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako saṅghaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti saṅghaṁ ārabbha.
Ujugatacitto kho pana, mahānāma, ariyasāvako labhati atthavedaṁ, labhati dhammavedaṁ, labhati dhammūpasaṁhitaṁ pāmojjaṁ.
Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
Ayaṁ vuccati, mahānāma:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako visamagatāya pajāya samappatto viharati, sabyāpajjāya pajāya abyāpajjo viharati, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno saṅghānussatiṁ bhāveti’.
segs.e: a noble disciple who lives in balance among people who are unbalanced, and lives untroubled among people who are troubled. They’ve entered the stream of the teaching and develop the recollection of the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, mahānāma, ariyasāvako attano sīlāni anussarati akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects their own ethical precepts, which are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako sīlaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects their ethical precepts their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti sīlaṁ ārabbha.
Ujugatacitto kho pana, mahānāma, ariyasāvako labhati atthavedaṁ, labhati dhammavedaṁ, labhati dhammūpasaṁhitaṁ pāmojjaṁ.
Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
Ayaṁ vuccati, mahānāma:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako visamagatāya pajāya samappatto viharati, sabyāpajjāya pajāya abyāpajjo viharati, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno sīlānussatiṁ bhāveti’.
segs.e: a noble disciple who lives in balance among people who are unbalanced, and lives untroubled among people who are troubled. They’ve entered the stream of the teaching and develop the recollection of ethics.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, mahānāma, ariyasāvako attano cāgaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects their generosity:

segs.p: ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me.
segs.e: ‘I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate!

segs.p: Yohaṁ maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitāya pajāya vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasāmi muttacāgo payatapāṇi vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato’ti.
segs.e: Among people full of the stain of stinginess I live at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako cāgaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects their generosity their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti cāgaṁ ārabbha.
Ujugatacitto kho pana, mahānāma, ariyasāvako labhati atthavedaṁ, labhati dhammavedaṁ, labhati dhammūpasaṁhitaṁ pāmojjaṁ.
Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
Ayaṁ vuccati, mahānāma:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako visamagatāya pajāya samappatto viharati, sabyāpajjāya pajāya abyāpajjo viharati, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno cāgānussatiṁ bhāveti’.
segs.e: a noble disciple who lives in balance among people who are unbalanced, and lives untroubled among people who are troubled. They’ve entered the stream of the teaching and develop the recollection of generosity.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, mahānāma, ariyasāvako devatānussatiṁ bhāveti:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the deities:

segs.p: ‘santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā tāvatiṁsā, santi devā yāmā, santi devā tusitā, santi devā nimmānaratino, santi devā paranimmitavasavattino, santi devā brahmakāyikā, santi devā tatuttari.
segs.e: ‘There are the gods of the four great kings, the gods of the thirty-three, the gods of Yama, the joyful gods, the gods who love to create, the gods who control what is created by others, the gods of the Divinity’s host, and gods even higher than these.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṁvijjati.
segs.e: When those deities passed away from here, they were reborn there because of their faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. I, too, have the same kind of faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.’

segs.p: Yathārūpena sīlena samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpaṁ sīlaṁ saṁvijjati.
Yathārūpena sutena samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpaṁ sutaṁ saṁvijjati.
Yathārūpena cāgena samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpo cāgo saṁvijjati.
Yathārūpāya paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṁvijjatī’ti.

Yasmiṁ, mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako attano ca tāsañca devatānaṁ saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom of both themselves and the deities their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti tā devatā ārabbha.
segs.e: At that time their mind is quite unswerving, based on the deities.

segs.p: Ujugatacitto kho pana, mahānāma, ariyasāvako labhati atthavedaṁ, labhati dhammavedaṁ, labhati dhammūpasaṁhitaṁ pāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: A noble disciple whose mind is unswerving finds inspiration in the meaning and the teaching, and finds joy connected with the teaching.

segs.p: Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
segs.e: When you’re joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, you feel bliss. And when you’re blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, mahānāma:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako visamagatāya pajāya samappatto viharati, sabyāpajjāya pajāya abyāpajjo viharati, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno devatānussatiṁ bhāveti’.
segs.e: a noble disciple who lives in balance among people who are unbalanced, and lives untroubled among people who are troubled. They’ve entered the stream of the teaching and develop the recollection of the deities.

segs.p: Yo so, mahānāma, ariyasāvako āgataphalo viññātasāsano, so iminā vihārena bahulaṁ viharatī”ti.
segs.e: When a noble disciple has reached the fruit and understood the instructions this is the kind of meditation they frequently practice.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Āhuneyyavaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Dve āhuneyyā indriya,
balāni tayo ājānīyā;
Anuttariya anussatī,
mahānāmena te dasāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.11
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.11

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Paṭhamasāraṇīyasutta
segs.e: Warm-hearted (1st)

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sāraṇīyā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these six warm-hearted qualities.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private. This is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness, both in public and in private. This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ manokammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī hoti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions. This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni tathārūpehi sīlehi sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion. This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāyaṁ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering. This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhammā sāraṇīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the six warm-hearted qualities.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.12
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.12

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Dutiyasāraṇīyasutta
segs.e: Warm-hearted (2nd)

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sāraṇīyā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six warm-hearted qualities make for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without dispute.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca,
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private.

segs.p: ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without dispute.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti …pe….
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness …

segs.p: Mettaṁ manokammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī hoti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions. This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni tathārūpehi sīlehi sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion. This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāyaṁ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca,
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without dispute.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhammā sāraṇīyā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These six warm-hearted qualities make for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.13
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.13

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Nissāraṇīyasutta
segs.e: Elements of Escape

segs.p: “Chayimā, bhikkhave, nissāraṇīyā dhātuyo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these six elements of escape.

segs.p: Katamā cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take a mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘mettā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā;
segs.e: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by love. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segs.p: atha ca pana me byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
segs.e: Yet somehow ill will still occupies my mind.’

segs.p: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo: ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca; mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
segs.e: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ mettāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya;
segs.e: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the heart’s release by love has been developed and properly implemented,

segs.p: atha ca panassa byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: yet somehow ill will still occupies the mind.

segs.p: Nissaraṇañhetaṁ, āvuso, byāpādassa yadidaṁ mettācetovimuttī’ti.
segs.e: For it is the heart’s release by love that is the escape from ill will.’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘karuṇā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā;
segs.e: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by compassion. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segs.p: atha ca pana me vihesā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
segs.e: Yet somehow the thought of harming still occupies my mind.’

segs.p: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo: ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca; mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
segs.e: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ karuṇāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya;
atha ca panassa vihesā cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇañhetaṁ, āvuso, vihesāya yadidaṁ karuṇācetovimuttī’ti.
segs.e: For it is the heart’s release by compassion that is the escape from thoughts of harming.’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘muditā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā;
segs.e: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by rejoicing. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segs.p: atha ca pana me arati cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
segs.e: Yet somehow discontent still occupies my mind.’

segs.p: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo: ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca; mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
segs.e: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ muditāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya;
atha ca panassa arati cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇañhetaṁ, āvuso, aratiyā yadidaṁ muditācetovimuttī’ti.
segs.e: For it is the heart’s release by rejoicing that is the escape from discontent.’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘upekkhā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā;
segs.e: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by equanimity. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segs.p: atha ca pana me rāgo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
segs.e: Yet somehow desire still occupies my mind.’

segs.p: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo: ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca; mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
segs.e: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ upekkhāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya;
atha ca panassa rāgo cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇañhetaṁ, āvuso, rāgassa yadidaṁ upekkhācetovimuttī’ti.
segs.e: For it is the heart’s release by equanimity that is the escape from desire.’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘animittā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā;
segs.e: ‘I’ve developed the signless release of the heart. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segs.p: atha ca pana me nimittānusāri viññāṇaṁ hotī’ti.
segs.e: Yet somehow my consciousness still follows after signs.’

segs.p: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo: ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca; mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
segs.e: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ animittāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya;
atha ca panassa nimittānusāri viññāṇaṁ bhavissati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇañhetaṁ, āvuso, sabbanimittānaṁ yadidaṁ animittācetovimuttī’ti.
segs.e: For it is the signless release of the heart that is the escape from all signs.’

segs.p: Idha pana bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘asmīti kho me vigataṁ, ayamahamasmīti ca na samanupassāmi;
segs.e: ‘I’m rid of the conceit “I am”. And I don’t regard anything as “I am this”.

segs.p: atha ca pana me vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.
segs.e: Yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupies my mind.’

segs.p: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo: ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca; mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.
segs.e: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso yaṁ asmīti vigate ayamahamasmīti ca na samanupassato;
segs.e: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the conceit “I am” has been done away with, and nothing is regarded as “I am this”,

segs.p: atha ca panassa vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupies the mind.

segs.p: Nissaraṇañhetaṁ, āvuso, vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallassa yadidaṁ asmīti mānasamugghāto’ti.
segs.e: For it is the uprooting of the conceit “I am” that is the escape from the dart of doubt and indecision.’

segs.p: Imā kho, bhikkhave, cha nissāraṇīyā dhātuyo”ti.
segs.e: These are the six elements of escape.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.14
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.14

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Bhaddakasutta
segs.e: A Good Death

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “āvuso bhikkhave”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
segs.e: Sāriputta said this:

segs.p: “Tathā tathā, āvuso, bhikkhu vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato na bhaddakaṁ maraṇaṁ hoti, na bhaddikā kālakiriyā.
segs.e: “A mendicant lives life so as to not have a good death.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato na bhaddakaṁ maraṇaṁ hoti, na bhaddikā kālakiriyā?
segs.e: And how do they live life so as to not have a good death?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kammārāmo hoti kammarato kammārāmataṁ anuyutto, bhassārāmo hoti bhassarato bhassārāmataṁ anuyutto, niddārāmo hoti niddārato niddārāmataṁ anuyutto, saṅgaṇikārāmo hoti saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ anuyutto, saṁsaggārāmo hoti saṁsaggarato saṁsaggārāmataṁ anuyutto, papañcārāmo hoti papañcarato papañcārāmataṁ anuyutto.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who relishes work, talk, sleep, company, closeness, and proliferation. They love these things and like to relish them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato na bhaddakaṁ maraṇaṁ hoti, na bhaddikā kālakiriyā.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives life like this does not have a good death.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu sakkāyābhirato nappajahāsi sakkāyaṁ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāya’.
segs.e: a mendicant who enjoys substantial reality, who hasn’t given up substantial reality to rightly make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Tathā tathāvuso, bhikkhu vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato bhaddakaṁ maraṇaṁ hoti, bhaddikā kālakiriyā.
segs.e: A mendicant lives life so as to have a good death.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato bhaddakaṁ maraṇaṁ hoti, bhaddikā kālakiriyā?
segs.e: And how do they live life so as to have a good death?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu na kammārāmo hoti na kammarato na kammārāmataṁ anuyutto, na bhassārāmo hoti na bhassarato na bhassārāmataṁ anuyutto, na niddārāmo hoti na niddārato na niddārāmataṁ anuyutto, na saṅgaṇikārāmo hoti na saṅgaṇikarato na saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ anuyutto, na saṁsaggārāmo hoti na saṁsaggarato na saṁsaggārāmataṁ anuyutto, na papañcārāmo hoti na papañcarato na papañcārāmataṁ anuyutto.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who doesn’t relish work, talk, sleep, company, closeness, and proliferation. They don’t love these things or like to relish them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato bhaddakaṁ maraṇaṁ hoti, bhaddikā kālakiriyā.
segs.e: A mendicant who lives life like this has a good death.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu nibbānābhirato pajahāsi sakkāyaṁ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: a mendicant who delights in extinguishment, who has given up substantial reality to rightly make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Yo papañcamanuyutto,
segs.e: A beast who likes to proliferate,

segs.p: papañcābhirato mago;
segs.e: enjoying proliferation,

segs.p: Virādhayī so nibbānaṁ,
segs.e: fails to win extinguishment,

segs.p: yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.
segs.e: the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Yo ca papañcaṁ hitvāna,
segs.e: But one who gives up proliferation,

segs.p: nippapañcapade rato;
segs.e: enjoying the state of non-proliferation,

segs.p: Ārādhayī so nibbānaṁ,
segs.e: wins extinguishment,

segs.p: yogakkhemaṁ anuttaran”ti.
segs.e: the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.15
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.15

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Anutappiyasutta
segs.e: Regret

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “tathā tathāvuso, bhikkhu vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato kālakiriyā anutappā hoti.
segs.e: “As a mendicant makes their bed, so they must lie in it, and die tormented by regrets.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato kālakiriyā anutappā hoti?
segs.e: And how do they die tormented by regrets?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kammārāmo hoti kammarato kammārāmataṁ anuyutto, bhassārāmo hoti …
segs.e: Take a mendicant who relishes work, talk, sleep, company, closeness, and proliferation. They love these things and like to relish them.

segs.p: niddārāmo hoti …
saṅgaṇikārāmo hoti …
saṁsaggārāmo hoti …
papañcārāmo hoti papañcarato papañcārāmataṁ anuyutto.
Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato kālakiriyā anutappā hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant who makes their bed like this must lie in it, and die tormented by regrets.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu sakkāyābhirato nappajahāsi sakkāyaṁ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāya’.
segs.e: a mendicant who enjoys substantial reality, who hasn’t given up substantial reality to rightly make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Tathā tathāvuso, bhikkhu vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato kālakiriyā ananutappā hoti.
segs.e: As a mendicant makes their bed, so they must lie in it, and die free of regrets.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato kālakiriyā ananutappā hoti?
segs.e: And how do they die free of regrets?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu na kammārāmo hoti na kammarato na kammārāmataṁ anuyutto, na bhassārāmo hoti …
segs.e: Take a mendicant who doesn’t relish work, talk, sleep, company, closeness, and proliferation. They don’t love these things or like to relish them.

segs.p: na niddārāmo hoti …
na saṅgaṇikārāmo hoti …
na saṁsaggārāmo hoti …
na papañcārāmo hoti na papañcarato na papañcārāmataṁ anuyutto.
Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu tathā tathā vihāraṁ kappeti yathā yathāssa vihāraṁ kappayato kālakiriyā ananutappā hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant who makes their bed like this must lie in it, and die free of regrets.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso:
segs.e: This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu nibbānābhirato pajahāsi sakkāyaṁ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: a mendicant who delights in extinguishment, who has given up substantial reality to rightly make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Yo papañcamanuyutto,
segs.e: A beast who likes to proliferate,

segs.p: papañcābhirato mago;
segs.e: enjoying proliferation,

segs.p: Virādhayī so nibbānaṁ,
segs.e: fails to win extinguishment,

segs.p: yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.
segs.e: the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Yo ca papañcaṁ hitvāna,
segs.e: But one who gives up proliferation,

segs.p: nippapañcapade rato;
segs.e: enjoying the state of non-proliferation,

segs.p: Ārādhayī so nibbānaṁ,
segs.e: wins extinguishment,

segs.p: yogakkhemaṁ anuttaran”ti.
segs.e: the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.16
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.16

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Nakulapitusutta
segs.e: Nakula’s Father

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena nakulapitā gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time the householder Nakula’s father was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho nakulamātā gahapatānī nakulapitaraṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the housewife Nakula’s mother said to him:

segs.p: “Mā kho tvaṁ, gahapati, sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: “Householder, don’t pass away with concerns.

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
segs.e: Such concern is suffering,

segs.p: garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā.
segs.e: and it’s criticized by the Buddha.

segs.p: Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘na nakulamātā gahapatānī mamaccayena sakkhissati dārake posetuṁ, gharāvāsaṁ santharitun’ti.
segs.e: ‘When I’ve gone, the housewife Nakula’s mother won’t be able to provide for the children and keep up the household carpets.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Kusalāhaṁ, gahapati, kappāsaṁ kantituṁ veṇiṁ olikhituṁ.
segs.e: I’m skilled at spinning cotton and carding wool.

segs.p: Sakkomahaṁ, gahapati, tavaccayena dārake posetuṁ, gharāvāsaṁ santharituṁ.
segs.e: I’m able to provide for the children and keep up the household carpets.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, gahapati, mā sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: So householder, don’t pass away with concerns …

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā.
Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘nakulamātā gahapatānī mamaccayena aññaṁ gharaṁ gamissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘When I’ve gone, the housewife Nakula’s mother will take another husband.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Tvañceva kho, gahapati, jānāsi ahañca, yaṁ no soḷasavassāni gahaṭṭhakaṁ brahmacariyaṁ samāciṇṇaṁ.
segs.e: Both you and I know that we have remained chaste while at home for the past sixteen years.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, gahapati, mā sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: So householder, don’t pass away with concerns …

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā.
Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘nakulamātā gahapatānī mamaccayena na dassanakāmā bhavissati bhagavato na dassanakāmā bhikkhusaṅghassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘When I’ve gone, the housewife Nakula’s mother won’t want to see the Buddha and his Saṅgha of mendicants.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Ahañhi, gahapati, tavaccayena dassanakāmatarā ceva bhavissāmi bhagavato, dassanakāmatarā ca bhikkhusaṅghassa.
segs.e: When you’ve gone, I’ll want to see the Buddha and his mendicant Saṅgha even more.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, gahapati, mā sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: So householder, don’t pass away with concerns …

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā.
Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘na nakulamātā gahapatānī mamaccayena sīlesu paripūrakārinī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The housewife Nakula’s mother won’t fulfill ethics.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, gahapati, tassa bhagavato sāvikā gihī odātavasanā sīlesu paripūrakāriniyo, ahaṁ tāsaṁ aññatarā.
segs.e: I am one of those white-robed disciples of the Buddha who fulfills their ethics.

segs.p: Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā—ayaṁ so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye—taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā pucchatu.
segs.e: For whoever doubts this, that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha is staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood. Let them approach him and ask.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, gahapati, mā sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: So householder, don’t pass away with concerns …

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā.
Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘na nakulamātā gahapatānī lābhinī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The housewife Nakula’s mother doesn’t have internal serenity of heart.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, gahapati, tassa bhagavato sāvikā gihī odātavasanā lābhiniyo ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, ahaṁ tāsaṁ aññatarā.
segs.e: I am one of those white-robed disciples of the Buddha who has internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā—ayaṁ so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye—taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā pucchatu.
segs.e: For whoever doubts this, that Blessed One is staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood. Let them approach him and ask.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, gahapati, mā sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: So householder, don’t pass away with concerns …

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā.
Siyā kho pana te, gahapati, evamassa:
segs.e: Householder, you might think:

segs.p: ‘na nakulamātā gahapatānī imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ogādhappattā patigādhappattā assāsappattā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṅkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The housewife Nakula’s mother has not found a footing, a firm footing, and solace in this teaching and training. She has not gone beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and gained assurance. And she’s not independent of others in the Teacher’s instructions.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, gahapati, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, gahapati, tassa bhagavato sāvikā gihī odātavasanā imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ogādhappattā patigādhappattā assāsappattā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṅkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharanti, ahaṁ tāsaṁ aññatarā.
segs.e: I am one of those white-robed disciples of the Buddha who has found a footing, a firm footing, and solace in this teaching and training. I have gone beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and gained assurance. And I am independent of others in the Teacher’s instructions.

segs.p: Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā—ayaṁ so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye—taṁ bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamitvā pucchatu.
segs.e: For whoever doubts this, that Blessed One is staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood. Let them approach him and ask.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, gahapati, mā sāpekkho kālamakāsi.
segs.e: So householder, don’t pass away with concerns.

segs.p: Dukkhā, gahapati, sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā;
segs.e: Such concern is suffering,

segs.p: garahitā ca bhagavatā sāpekkhassa kālakiriyā”ti.
segs.e: and it’s criticized by the Buddha.”

segs.p: Atha kho nakulapituno gahapatissa nakulamātarā gahapatāniyā iminā ovādena ovadiyamānassa so ābādho ṭhānaso paṭippassambhi.
segs.e: And then, as Nakula’s mother was giving this advice to Nakula’s father, his illness died down on the spot.

segs.p: Vuṭṭhahi ca nakulapitā gahapati tamhā ābādhā;
segs.e: And that’s how Nakula’s father recovered from that illness.

segs.p: tathā pahīno ca pana nakulapituno gahapatissa so ābādho ahosi.

Atha kho nakulapitā gahapati gilānā vuṭṭhito aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā daṇḍamolubbha yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho nakulapitaraṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Soon after recovering, leaning on a staff he went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṁ te, gahapati.
segs.e: “You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate,

segs.p: Yassa te nakulamātā gahapatānī anukampikā atthakāmā ovādikā anusāsikā.
segs.e: to have the housewife Nakula’s mother advise and instruct you out of kindness and sympathy.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, gahapati, mama sāvikā gihī odātavasanā sīlesu paripūrakāriniyo, nakulamātā gahapatānī tāsaṁ aññatarā.
segs.e: She is one of those white-robed disciples of the Buddha who fulfills their ethics.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, gahapati, mama sāvikā gihī odātavasanā lābhiniyo ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, nakulamātā gahapatānī tāsaṁ aññatarā.
segs.e: She is one of those white-robed disciples of the Buddha who has internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho, gahapati, mama sāvikā gihī odātavasanā imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ogādhappattā patigādhappattā assāsappattā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṅkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharanti, nakulamātā gahapatānī tāsaṁ aññatarā.
segs.e: She is one of those white-robed disciples of the Buddha who has found a footing, a firm footing, and solace in this teaching and training. She has gone beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and gained assurance. And she is independent of others in the Teacher’s instructions.

segs.p: Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṁ te, gahapati.
segs.e: You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate,

segs.p: Yassa te nakulamātā gahapatānī anukampikā atthakāmā ovādikā anusāsikā”ti.
segs.e: to have the housewife Nakula’s mother advise and instruct you out of kindness and sympathy.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.17
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.17

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Soppasutta
segs.e: Sleep

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat, went to the assembly hall, and sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Āyasmāpi kho sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Venerable Sāriputta also came out of retreat, went to the assembly hall, bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Āyasmāpi kho mahāmoggallāno …
segs.e: Venerables Mahāmoggallāna,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho mahākassapo …
segs.e: Mahākassapa,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho mahākaccāno …
segs.e: Mahākaccāna,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho mahākoṭṭhiko …
segs.e: Mahākoṭṭhita,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho mahācundo …
segs.e: Mahācunda,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho mahākappino …
segs.e: Mahākappina,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho anuruddho …
segs.e: Anuruddha,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho revato …
segs.e: Revata,

segs.p: āyasmāpi kho ānando sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: and Ānanda did the same.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā bahudeva rattiṁ nisajjāya vītināmetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: The Buddha spent much of the night sitting in meditation, then rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Tepi kho āyasmanto acirapakkantassa bhagavato uṭṭhāyāsanā yathāvihāraṁ agamaṁsu.
segs.e: And soon after the Buddha left those venerables each went to their own dwelling.

segs.p: Ye pana tattha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ te yāva sūriyuggamanā kākacchamānā supiṁsu.
segs.e: But those mendicants who were junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training slept until the sun came up, snoring.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena te bhikkhū yāva sūriyuggamanā kākacchamāne supante.
segs.e: The Buddha saw them doing this, with his clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman.

segs.p: Disvā yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: He went to the assembly hall, sat down on the seat spread out,

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: and addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “Kahaṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sāriputto?
segs.e: “Mendicants, where is Sāriputta?

segs.p: Kahaṁ mahāmoggallāno?
segs.e: Where are Mahāmoggallāna,

segs.p: Kahaṁ mahākassapo?
segs.e: Mahākassapa,

segs.p: Kahaṁ mahākaccāno?
segs.e: Mahākaccāna,

segs.p: Kahaṁ mahākoṭṭhiko?
segs.e: Mahākoṭṭhita,

segs.p: Kahaṁ mahācundo?
segs.e: Mahācunda,

segs.p: Kahaṁ mahākappino?
segs.e: Mahākappina,

segs.p: Kahaṁ anuruddho?
segs.e: Anuruddha,

segs.p: Kahaṁ revato?
segs.e: Revata,

segs.p: Kahaṁ ānando?
segs.e: and Ānanda?

segs.p: Kahaṁ nu kho te, bhikkhave, therā sāvakā gatā”ti?
segs.e: Where have these senior disciples gone?”

segs.p: “Tepi kho, bhante, āyasmanto acirapakkantassa bhagavato uṭṭhāyāsanā yathāvihāraṁ agamaṁsū”ti.
segs.e: “Soon after the Buddha left those venerables each went to their own dwelling.”

segs.p: “Tena no tumhe, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū nāgatāti yāva sūriyuggamanā kākacchamānā supatha?
segs.e: “So, mendicants, when the senior mendicants left, why did you sleep until the sun came up, snoring?

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard

segs.p: ‘rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto yāvadatthaṁ seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharanto yāvajīvaṁ rajjaṁ kārento janapadassa vā piyo manāpo’”ti?
segs.e: of an anointed aristocratic king who rules his whole life, dear and beloved to the country, while indulging in the pleasures of sleeping, lying down, and drowsing as much as he likes?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave.
segs.e: “Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: ‘rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto yāvadatthaṁ seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharanto yāvajīvaṁ rajjaṁ kārento janapadassa vā piyo manāpo’ti.
Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard

segs.p: ‘raṭṭhiko …pe…
segs.e: of an appointed official …

segs.p: pettaṇiko …
segs.e: a hereditary official …

segs.p: senāpatiko …
segs.e: a general …

segs.p: gāmagāmaṇiko …
segs.e: a village chief …

segs.p: pūgagāmaṇiko yāvadatthaṁ seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharanto yāvajīvaṁ pūgagāmaṇikattaṁ kārento pūgassa vā piyo manāpo’”ti?
segs.e: or a guild head who runs the guild his whole life, dear and beloved to the guild, while indulging in the pleasures of sleeping, lying down, and drowsing as much as he likes?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave.
segs.e: “Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: ‘pūgagāmaṇiko yāvadatthaṁ seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharanto yāvajīvaṁ pūgagāmaṇikattaṁ vā kārento pūgassa vā piyo manāpo’ti.
Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard

segs.p: ‘samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yāvadatthaṁ seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto indriyesu aguttadvāro bhojane amattaññū jāgariyaṁ ananuyutto avipassako kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogaṁ ananuyutto āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanto’”ti?
segs.e: of an ascetic or brahmin who indulges in the pleasures of sleeping, lying down, and drowsing as much as they like? Their sense doors are unguarded, they eat too much, they’re not dedicated to wakefulness, they’re unable to discern skillful qualities, and they don’t pursue the development of the qualities on the side of awakening in the evening and toward dawn. Yet they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave.
segs.e: “Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: ‘samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yāvadatthaṁ seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto indriyesu aguttadvāro bhojane amattaññū jāgariyaṁ ananuyutto avipassako kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogaṁ ananuyutto āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanto’ti.
Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘indriyesu guttadvārā bhavissāma, bhojane mattaññuno, jāgariyaṁ anuyuttā, vipassakā kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ, pubbarattāpararattaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ, bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will guard our sense doors, eat in moderation, be dedicated to wakefulness, discern skillful qualities, and pursue the development of the qualities on the side of awakening in the evening and toward dawn.’

segs.p: Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabban”ti.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.18
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.18

segs.p: 2. Sāraṇīyavagga
segs.e: 2. Warm-hearted

segs.p: Macchabandhasutta
segs.e: A Fish Dealer

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā addhānamaggappaṭipanno aññatarasmiṁ padese macchikaṁ macchabandhaṁ macche vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamānaṁ.
segs.e: While walking along the road he saw a fish dealer in a certain spot selling fish that he had killed himself.

segs.p: Disvā maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Seeing this he left the road, sat at the root of a tree on the seat spread out,

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: and addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, amuṁ macchikaṁ macchabandhaṁ macche vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamānan”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, do you see that fish dealer selling fish that he killed himself?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: “What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard

segs.p: ‘macchiko macchabandho macche vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamāno tena kammena tena ājīvena hatthiyāyī vā assayāyī vā rathayāyī vā yānayāyī vā bhogabhogī vā mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasanto’”ti?
segs.e: of a fish dealer selling fish that he killed himself who, by means of that work and livelihood, got to travel by elephant, horse, chariot, or vehicle, or to enjoy wealth, or to live off a large fortune?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave.
segs.e: “Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: ‘macchiko macchabandho macche vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamāno tena kammena tena ājīvena hatthiyāyī vā assayāyī vā rathayāyī vā yānayāyī vā bhogabhogī vā mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasanto’ti.
Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Te hi so, bhikkhave, macche vajjhe vadhāyupanīte pāpakena manasānupekkhati, tasmā so neva hatthiyāyī hoti na assayāyī na rathayāyī na yānayāyī na bhogabhogī, na mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: Because when the fish are led to the slaughter he regards them with bad intentions.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard

segs.p: ‘goghātako gāvo vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamāno tena kammena tena ājīvena hatthiyāyī vā assayāyī vā rathayāyī vā yānayāyī vā bhogabhogī vā mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasanto’”ti?
segs.e: of a butcher of cattle selling cattle that he killed himself who, by means of that work and livelihood, got to travel by elephant, horse, chariot, or vehicle, or to enjoy wealth, or to live off a large fortune?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave.
segs.e: “Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: ‘goghātako gāvo vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamāno tena kammena tena ājīvena hatthiyāyī vā assayāyī vā rathayāyī vā yānayāyī vā bhogabhogī vā mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasanto’ti.
Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Te hi so, bhikkhave, gāvo vajjhe vadhāyupanīte pāpakena manasānupekkhati, tasmā so neva hatthiyāyī hoti na assayāyī na rathayāyī na yānayāyī na bhogabhogī, na mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: Because when the cattle are led to the slaughter he regards them with bad intentions.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard

segs.p: ‘orabbhiko …pe…
segs.e: of a butcher of sheep …

segs.p: sūkariko …pe…
segs.e: a butcher of pigs …

segs.p: sākuṇiko …pe…
segs.e: a butcher of poultry …

segs.p: māgaviko mage vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamāno tena kammena tena ājīvena hatthiyāyī vā assayāyī vā rathayāyī vā yānayāyī vā bhogabhogī vā mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasanto’”ti?
segs.e: or a deer-hunter selling deer which he killed himself who, by means of that work and livelihood, got to travel by elephant, horse, chariot, or vehicle, or to enjoy wealth, or to live off a large fortune?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave.
segs.e: “Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: ‘māgaviko mage vadhitvā vadhitvā vikkiṇamāno tena kammena tena ājīvena hatthiyāyī vā assayāyī vā rathayāyī vā yānayāyī vā bhogabhogī vā mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasanto’ti.
Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Te hi so, bhikkhave, mage vajjhe vadhāyupanīte pāpakena manasānupekkhati, tasmā so neva hatthiyāyī hoti na assayāyī na rathayāyī na yānayāyī na bhogabhogī, na mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: Because when the deer are led to the slaughter he regards them with bad intentions.

segs.p: Te hi nāma so, bhikkhave, tiracchānagate pāṇe vajjhe vadhāyupanīte pāpakena manasānupekkhamāno neva hatthiyāyī bhavissati na assayāyī na rathayāyī na yānayāyī na bhogabhogī, na mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ ajjhāvasissati.
segs.e: By regarding even animals led to the slaughter with bad intentions he did not get to travel by elephant, horse, chariot, or vehicle, or to enjoy wealth, or to live off a large fortune.

segs.p: Ko pana vādo yaṁ manussabhūtaṁ vajjhaṁ vadhāyupanītaṁ pāpakena manasānupekkhati.
segs.e: How much worse is someone who regards human beings brought to the slaughter with bad intentions!

segs.p: Tañhi tassa, bhikkhave, hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
segs.e: This will be for their lasting harm and suffering.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjatī”ti.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Paṭhamamaraṇassatisutta
segs.e: Mindfulness of Death (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: “bhikkhavo”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants!”

segs.p: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “maraṇassati, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when mindfulness of death is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. It has freedom from death as its objective and culmination.

segs.p: Bhāvetha no tumhe, bhikkhave, maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: But do you develop mindfulness of death?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahaṁ kho, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, bhāvesi maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you develop it?”

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “In this case, sir, I think:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ rattindivaṁ jīveyyaṁ, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, if I’d only live for another day and night, I’d focus on the Buddha’s instructions and I could really achieve a lot.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another mendicant said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahampi kho, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I too develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, bhāvesi maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you develop it?”

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “In this case, sir, I think:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ divasaṁ jīveyyaṁ, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, if I’d only live for another day, I’d focus on the Buddha’s instructions and I could really achieve a lot.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another mendicant said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahampi kho, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I too develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, bhāvesi maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you develop it?”

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “In this case, sir, I think:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ ekapiṇḍapātaṁ bhuñjāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, if I’d only live as long as it takes to eat a meal of almsfood, I’d focus on the Buddha’s instructions and I could really achieve a lot.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another mendicant said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahampi kho, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I too develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, bhāvesi maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you develop it?”

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “In this case, sir, I think:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ cattāro pañca ālope saṅkhāditvā ajjhoharāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, if I’d only live as long as it takes to chew and swallow four or five mouthfuls, I’d focus on the Buddha’s instructions and I could really achieve a lot.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another mendicant said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahampi kho, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I too develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, bhāvesi maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you develop it?”

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “In this case, sir, I think:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ ekaṁ ālopaṁ saṅkhāditvā ajjhoharāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, if I’d only live as long as it takes to chew and swallow a single mouthful, I’d focus on the Buddha’s instructions and I could really achieve a lot.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another mendicant said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ahampi kho, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I too develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, bhāvesi maraṇassatin”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you develop it?”

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “In this case, sir, I think:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ assasitvā vā passasāmi passasitvā vā assasāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, if I’d only live as long as it takes to breathe out after breathing in, or to breathe in after breathing out, I’d focus on the Buddha’s instructions and I could really achieve a lot.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhāvemi maraṇassatin”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I develop mindfulness of death.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, the Buddha said to those mendicants:

segs.p: “yo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāveti:
segs.e: “As to the mendicants who develop mindfulness of death by wishing

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ rattindivaṁ jīveyyaṁ, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: to live for a day and night …

segs.p: Yo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāveti:
‘aho vatāhaṁ divasaṁ jīveyyaṁ, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: or to live for a day …

segs.p: Yo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāveti:
‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ ekapiṇḍapātaṁ bhuñjāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: or to live as long as it takes to eat a meal of almsfood …

segs.p: Yo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāveti:
‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ cattāro pañca ālope saṅkhāditvā ajjhoharāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: or to live as long as it takes to chew and swallow four or five mouthfuls—

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, bhikkhū pamattā viharanti dandhaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāventi āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: these are called mendicants who live negligently. They slackly develop mindfulness of death for the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Yo ca khvāyaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāveti:
segs.e: But as to the mendicants who develop mindfulness of death by wishing

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ ekaṁ ālopaṁ saṅkhāditvā ajjhoharāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: to live as long as it takes to chew and swallow a single mouthful …

segs.p: Yo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāveti:
‘aho vatāhaṁ tadantaraṁ jīveyyaṁ yadantaraṁ assasitvā vā passasāmi passasitvā vā assasāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṁ manasi kareyyaṁ, bahu vata me kataṁ assā’ti.
segs.e: or to live as long as it takes to breathe out after breathing in, or to breathe in after breathing out—

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, bhikkhū appamattā viharanti tikkhaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāventi āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: these are called mendicants who live diligently. They keenly develop mindfulness of death for the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘appamattā viharissāma, tikkhaṁ maraṇassatiṁ bhāvessāma āsavānaṁ khayāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will live diligently. We will keenly develop mindfulness of death for the ending of defilements.’

segs.p: Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabban”ti.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.

segs.p: Dutiyamaraṇassatisutta
segs.e: Mindfulness of Death (2nd)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “maraṇassati, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when mindfulness of death is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. It has freedom from death as its objective and culmination.

segs.p: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, maraṇassati kathaṁ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā?
segs.e: And how is mindfulness of death developed and cultivated to be very fruitful and beneficial, with freedom from death as its objective and culmination?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu divase nikkhante rattiyā patihitāya iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: As day passes by and night draws close, a mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘bahukā kho me paccayā maraṇassa—
segs.e: ‘I might die of many causes.

segs.p: ahi vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya, vicchiko vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya, satapadī vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya;
