segs.e: A snake might bite me, or a scorpion or centipede might sting me.

segs.p: tena me assa kālakiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo.
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: Upakkhalitvā vā papateyyaṁ, bhattaṁ vā me bhuttaṁ byāpajjeyya, pittaṁ vā me kuppeyya, semhaṁ vā me kuppeyya, satthakā vā me vātā kuppeyyuṁ;
segs.e: Or I might stumble off a cliff, or get food poisoning, or suffer a disturbance of bile, phlegm, or piercing winds.

segs.p: tena me assa kālakiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo’ti.
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.’

segs.p: Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: That mendicant should reflect:

segs.p: ‘atthi nu kho me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīnā, ye me assu rattiṁ kālaṁ karontassa antarāyāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Are there any bad, unskillful qualities that I haven’t given up, which might be an obstacle to my progress if I die tonight?’

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows that

segs.p: ‘atthi me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīnā, ye me assu rattiṁ kālaṁ karontassa antarāyāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṁyeva pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: there are such bad, unskillful qualities. Then in order to give them up they should apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṁ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya;
segs.e: Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tena bhikkhunā tesaṁyeva pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, in order to give up those bad, unskillful qualities, that mendicant should apply extraordinary enthusiasm …

segs.p: Sace pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: But suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows that

segs.p: ‘natthi me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīnā, ye me assu rattiṁ kālaṁ karontassa antarāyāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṁ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: there are no such bad, unskillful qualities. Then that mendicant should meditate with rapture and joy, training day and night in skillful qualities.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rattiyā nikkhantāya divase patihite iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Or else, as night passes by and day draws close, a mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘bahukā kho me paccayā maraṇassa—
segs.e: ‘I might die of many causes.

segs.p: ahi vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya, vicchiko vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya, satapadī vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya;
segs.e: A snake might bite me, or a scorpion or centipede might sting me.

segs.p: tena me assa kālakiriyā so mamassa antarāyo.
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: Upakkhalitvā vā papateyyaṁ, bhattaṁ vā me bhuttaṁ byāpajjeyya, pittaṁ vā me kuppeyya, semhaṁ vā me kuppeyya, satthakā vā me vātā kuppeyyuṁ;
segs.e: Or I might stumble off a cliff, or get food poisoning, or suffer a disturbance of bile, phlegm, or piercing winds.

segs.p: tena me assa kālakiriyā so mamassa antarāyo’ti.
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.’

segs.p: Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: That mendicant should reflect:

segs.p: ‘atthi nu kho me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīnā, ye me assu divā kālaṁ karontassa antarāyāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Are there any bad, unskillful qualities that I haven’t given up, which might be an obstacle to my progress if I die today?’

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows that

segs.p: ‘atthi me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīnā, ye me assu divā kālaṁ karontassa antarāyāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṁyeva pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: there are such bad, unskillful qualities. Then in order to give them up they should apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṁ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya;
segs.e: Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tena bhikkhunā tesaṁyeva pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, in order to give up those bad, unskillful qualities, that mendicant should apply extraordinary enthusiasm …

segs.p: Sace pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: But suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows that

segs.p: ‘natthi me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīnā, ye me assu divā kālaṁ karontassa antarāyāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṁ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: there are no such bad, unskillful qualities. Then that mendicant should meditate with rapture and joy, training day and night in skillful qualities.

segs.p: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, maraṇassati evaṁ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṁsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: Mindfulness of death, when developed and cultivated in this way, is very fruitful and beneficial. It has freedom from death as its objective and culmination.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Sāraṇīyavaggo dutiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Dve sāraṇī nisāraṇīyaṁ,
bhaddakaṁ anutappiyaṁ;
Nakulaṁ soppamacchā ca,
dve honti maraṇassatīti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.21
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.21

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Sāmakasutta
segs.e: At Sāma Village

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati sāmagāmake pokkharaṇiyāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans near the little village of Sāma, by a lotus pond.

segs.p: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ pokkharaṇiyaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire lotus pond, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “Tayome, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Sir, three qualities lead to the decline of a mendicant.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā—
segs.e: Relishing work, talk, and sleep.

segs.p: ime kho, bhante, tayo dhammā bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These three qualities lead to the decline of a mendicant.”

segs.p: Idamavoca sā devatā.
segs.e: That is what that deity said,

segs.p: Samanuñño satthā ahosi.
segs.e: and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho sā devatā “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then that deity, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened, adding:

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ pokkharaṇiyaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
‘tayome, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
Katame tayo?
Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā—
ime kho, bhante, tayo dhammā bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
Idamavoca, bhikkhave, sā devatā.
Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
Tesaṁ vo, bhikkhave, alābhā tesaṁ dulladdhaṁ, ye vo devatāpi jānanti kusalehi dhammehi parihāyamāne.
segs.e: “It’s unfortunate for those of you who even the deities know are declining in skillful qualities.

segs.p: Aparepi, bhikkhave, tayo parihāniye dhamme desessāmi.
segs.e: I will teach you three more qualities that lead to decline.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo parihāniyā dhammā?
segs.e: “And what, mendicants, are three qualities that lead to decline?

segs.p: Saṅgaṇikārāmatā, dovacassatā, pāpamittatā—
segs.e: Enjoyment of company, being hard to admonish, and having bad friends.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo parihāniyā dhammā.
segs.e: These three qualities lead to decline.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṁ parihāyiṁsu kusalehi dhammehi, sabbete imeheva chahi dhammehi parihāyiṁsu kusalehi dhammehi.
segs.e: Whether in the past, future, or present, all those who decline in skillful qualities do so because of these six qualities.”

segs.p: Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṁ parihāyissanti kusalehi dhammehi, sabbete imeheva chahi dhammehi parihāyissanti kusalehi dhammehi.
Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi parihāyanti kusalehi dhammehi, sabbete imeheva chahi dhammehi parihāyanti kusalehi dhammehī”ti.
Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.22
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.22

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Aparihāniyasutta
segs.e: Non-decline

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṁ suṇātha …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you these six principles that prevent decline. …

segs.p: katame ca, bhikkhave, cha aparihāniyā dhammā?
segs.e: And what, mendicants, are the six principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Na kammārāmatā, na bhassārāmatā, na niddārāmatā, na saṅgaṇikārāmatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā—
segs.e: Not relishing work, talk, sleep, and company, being easy to admonish, and having good friends.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha aparihāniyā dhammā.
segs.e: These six qualities prevent decline.

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṁ na parihāyiṁsu kusalehi dhammehi, sabbete imeheva chahi dhammehi na parihāyiṁsu kusalehi dhammehi.
segs.e: Whether in the past, future, or present, all those who have not declined in skillful qualities do so because of these six qualities.”

segs.p: Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṁ na parihāyissanti kusalehi dhammehi, sabbete imeheva chahi dhammehi na parihāyissanti kusalehi dhammehi.
Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi na parihāyanti kusalehi dhammehi, sabbete imeheva chahi dhammehi na parihāyanti kusalehi dhammehī”ti.
Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.23
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.23

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Bhayasutta
segs.e: Dangers

segs.p: “‘Bhayan’ti, bhikkhave, kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ;
segs.e: “‘Danger’, mendicants, is a term for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: ‘dukkhan’ti, bhikkhave, kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ;
segs.e: ‘Suffering’,

segs.p: ‘rogo’ti, bhikkhave, kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ;
segs.e: ‘disease’,

segs.p: ‘gaṇḍo’ti, bhikkhave, kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ;
segs.e: ‘boil’,

segs.p: ‘saṅgo’ti, bhikkhave, kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ;
segs.e: ‘chain’,

segs.p: ‘paṅko’ti, bhikkhave, kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: and ‘bog’ are terms for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, ‘bhayan’ti kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ?
segs.e: And why is ‘danger’ a term for sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Kāmarāgarattāyaṁ, bhikkhave, chandarāgavinibaddho diṭṭhadhammikāpi bhayā na parimuccati, samparāyikāpi bhayā na parimuccati, tasmā ‘bhayan’ti kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: Someone who is besotted by sensual greed and shackled by lustful desire is not freed from dangers in this life or in lives to come. That is why ‘danger’ is a term for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, dukkhanti …pe…
segs.e: And why are ‘suffering’,

segs.p: rogoti …
segs.e: ‘disease’,

segs.p: gaṇḍoti …
segs.e: ‘boil’,

segs.p: saṅgoti …
segs.e: ‘chain’,

segs.p: paṅkoti kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ?
segs.e: and ‘bog’ terms for sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Kāmarāgarattāyaṁ, bhikkhave, chandarāgavinibaddho diṭṭhadhammikāpi paṅkā na parimuccati, samparāyikāpi paṅkā na parimuccati, tasmā ‘paṅko’ti kāmānametaṁ adhivacananti.
segs.e: Someone who is besotted by sensual greed and shackled by lustful desire is not freed from suffering, disease, boils, chains, or bogs in this life or in lives to come. That is why these are terms for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Bhayaṁ dukkhaṁ rogo gaṇḍo,
segs.e: Danger, suffering, disease, boils,

segs.p: saṅgo paṅko ca ubhayaṁ;
segs.e: and chains and bogs both.

segs.p: Ete kāmā pavuccanti,
segs.e: These describe the sensual pleasures

segs.p: yattha satto puthujjano.
segs.e: to which ordinary people are attached.

segs.p: Upādāne bhayaṁ disvā,
segs.e: Seeing the danger in grasping,

segs.p: jātimaraṇasambhave;
segs.e: the origin of birth and death,

segs.p: Anupādā vimuccanti,
segs.e: the unattached are freed

segs.p: jātimaraṇasaṅkhaye.
segs.e: with the ending of birth and death.

segs.p: Te khemappattā sukhino,
segs.e: Happy, they’ve come to a safe place,

segs.p: diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā;
segs.e: quenched in this very life.

segs.p: Sabbaverabhayātītā,
segs.e: They’ve gone beyond all enmities and fears,

segs.p: sabbadukkhaṁ upaccagun”ti.
segs.e: and risen above all suffering.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.24
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.24

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Himavantasutta
segs.e: The Himalaya

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu himavantaṁ pabbatarājaṁ padāleyya, ko pana vādo chavāya avijjāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has six qualities could shatter Himalaya, the king of mountains, let alone this wretched ignorance!

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samādhissa samāpattikusalo hoti, samādhissa ṭhitikusalo hoti, samādhissa vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, samādhissa kallitakusalo hoti, samādhissa gocarakusalo hoti, samādhissa abhinīhārakusalo hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is skilled in entering immersion, skilled in remaining in immersion, skilled in emerging from immersion, skilled in positivity for immersion, skilled in the territory of immersion, and skilled in projecting the mind purified by immersion.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu himavantaṁ pabbatarājaṁ padāleyya, ko pana vādo chavāya avijjāyā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these six qualities could shatter Himalaya, the king of mountains, let alone this wretched ignorance!”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.25
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.25

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Anussatiṭṭhānasutta
segs.e: Topics for Recollection

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, anussatiṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these six topics for recollection.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako tathāgataṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple recollects the Realized One:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako tathāgataṁ anussarati, nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the Realized One their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
segs.e: At that time their mind is quite unswerving. They’ve left behind greed; they’re free of it and have risen above it.

segs.p: ‘Gedho’ti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Greed’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Idampi kho, bhikkhave, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visujjhanti.
segs.e: Relying on this, some sentient beings are purified in this way.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhammaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo …pe… paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako dhammaṁ anussarati, nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the teaching their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Idampi kho, bhikkhave, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visujjhanti.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako saṅghaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako saṅghaṁ anussarati, nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Idampi kho, bhikkhave, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visujjhanti.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako attano sīlāni anussarati akhaṇḍāni …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikāni.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects their own ethical precepts, which are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako sīlaṁ anussarati, nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects their ethical precepts their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Idampi kho, bhikkhave, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visujjhanti.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako attano cāgaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects their generosity:

segs.p: ‘lābhā vata me. Suladdhaṁ vata me …pe…
segs.e: ‘I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate!

segs.p: yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato’ti.
segs.e: Among people full of the stain of stinginess I live at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.’

segs.p: …pe…
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects their generosity their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: Evam’idhekacce sattā visujjhanti.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako devatā anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the deities:

segs.p: ‘santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā tāvatiṁsā, santi devā yāmā, santi devā tusitā, santi devā nimmānaratino, santi devā paranimmitavasavattino, santi devā brahmakāyikā, santi devā tatuttari.
segs.e: ‘There are the gods of the four great kings, the gods of the thirty-three, the gods of Yama, the joyful gods, the gods who love to create, the gods who control what is created by others, the gods of the Divinity’s host, and gods even higher than these.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā; mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṁvijjati.
segs.e: When those deities passed away from here, they were reborn there because of their faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. I, too, have the same kind of faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.’

segs.p: Yathārūpena sīlena …
sutena …
cāgena …
paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā; mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṁvijjatī’ti.

Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako attano ca tāsañca devatānaṁ saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom of both themselves and the deities their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
segs.e: At that time their mind is quite unswerving. They’ve left behind greed; they’re free of it and have risen above it.

segs.p: ‘Gedho’ti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Greed’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Idampi kho, bhikkhave, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visujjhanti.
segs.e: Relying on this, some sentient beings are purified in this way.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six topics for recollection.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.26
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.26

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Mahākaccānasutta
segs.e: With Mahākaccāna

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā mahākaccāno bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Mahākaccāna addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “āvuso bhikkhave”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Āyasmā mahākaccāno etadavoca:
segs.e: Venerable Mahākaccāna said this:

segs.p: “acchariyaṁ, āvuso;
segs.e: “It’s incredible, reverends,

segs.p: abbhutaṁ, āvuso.
segs.e: it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sambādhe okāsādhigamo anubuddho sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ cha anussatiṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: How this Blessed One who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, has found an opening amid confinement; that is, the six topics for recollection. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, ariyasāvako tathāgataṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple recollects the Realized One:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye ariyasāvako tathāgataṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the Realized One their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
segs.e: At that time their mind is quite unswerving. They’ve left behind greed; they’re free of it and have risen above it.

segs.p: ‘Gedho’ti kho, āvuso, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Greed’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Sa kho so, āvuso, ariyasāvako sabbaso ākāsasamena cetasā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: That noble disciple meditates with a heart just like space, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Idampi kho, āvuso, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visuddhidhammā bhavanti.
segs.e: Relying on this, some sentient beings become pure in this way.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, ariyasāvako dhammaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo …pe… paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye ariyasāvako dhammaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the teaching their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, āvuso, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Sa kho so, āvuso, ariyasāvako sabbaso ākāsasamena cetasā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
Idampi kho, āvuso, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visuddhidhammā bhavanti.
Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, ariyasāvako saṅghaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye ariyasāvako saṅghaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, āvuso, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Sa kho so, āvuso, ariyasāvako sabbaso ākāsasamena cetasā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
Idampi kho, āvuso, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visuddhidhammā bhavanti.
Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, ariyasāvako attano sīlāni anussarati akhaṇḍāni …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikāni.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects their own ethical precepts, which are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye ariyasāvako attano sīlaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects their ethical precepts their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, āvuso, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Sa kho so, āvuso, ariyasāvako sabbaso ākāsasamena cetasā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
Idampi kho, āvuso, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visuddhidhammā bhavanti.
Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, ariyasāvako attano cāgaṁ anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects their generosity:

segs.p: ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me …pe…
segs.e: ‘I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate!

segs.p: yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato’ti.
segs.e: Among people full of the stain of stinginess I live at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye ariyasāvako attano cāgaṁ anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects their generosity their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion. …

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
‘Gedho’ti kho, āvuso, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
Sa kho so, āvuso, ariyasāvako sabbaso ākāsasamena cetasā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
Idampi kho, āvuso, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visuddhidhammā bhavanti.
Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, ariyasāvako devatā anussarati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple recollects the deities:

segs.p: ‘santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā …pe… tatuttari.
segs.e: ‘There are the gods of the four great kings, the gods of the thirty-three, the gods of Yama, the joyful gods, the gods who love to create, the gods who control what is created by others, the gods of the Divinity’s host, and gods even higher than these.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā; mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṁvijjati.
segs.e: When those deities passed away from here, they were reborn there because of their faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. I, too, have the same kind of faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.’

segs.p: Yathārūpena sīlena …
sutena …
cāgena …
paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tattha upapannā; mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṁvijjatī’ti.

Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye ariyasāvako attano ca tāsañca devatānaṁ saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarati nevassa tasmiṁ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na dosapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti, na mohapariyuṭṭhitaṁ cittaṁ hoti;
segs.e: When a noble disciple recollects the faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom of both themselves and the deities their mind is not full of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: ujugatamevassa tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ hoti, nikkhantaṁ muttaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ gedhamhā.
segs.e: At that time their mind is quite unswerving. They’ve left behind greed; they’re free of it and have risen above it.

segs.p: ‘Gedho’ti kho, āvuso, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Greed’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Sa kho so, āvuso, ariyasāvako sabbaso ākāsasamena cetasā viharati vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena.
segs.e: That noble disciple meditates with a heart just like space, abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Idampi kho, āvuso, ārammaṇaṁ karitvā evam’idhekacce sattā visuddhidhammā bhavanti.
segs.e: Relying on this, some sentient beings become pure in this way.

segs.p: Acchariyaṁ, āvuso, abbhutaṁ, āvuso.
segs.e: It’s incredible, reverends, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sambādhe okāsādhigamo anubuddho sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ cha anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: How this Blessed One who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, has found an opening amid confinement; that is, the six topics for recollection. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.27
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.27

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Paṭhamasamayasutta
segs.e: Proper Occasions (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “kati nu kho, bhante, samayā manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how many occasions are there for going to see an esteemed mendicant?”

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhu, samayā manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicant, there are six occasions for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Firstly, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire, and they don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. On that occasion they should go to an esteemed mendicant and say:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho, āvuso, kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharāmi kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmi.
segs.e: ‘My heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire, and I don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen.

segs.p: Sādhu vata me āyasmā kāmarāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desetū’ti.
segs.e: Venerable, please teach me how to give up sensual desire.’

segs.p: Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu kāmarāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Then that esteemed mendicant teaches them how to give up sensual desire.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, paṭhamo samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the first occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in ill will …

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho, āvuso, byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharāmi byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmi.
Sādhu vata me āyasmā byāpādassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desetū’ti.
Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu byāpādassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, dutiyo samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the second occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness …

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho, āvuso, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharāmi thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmi.
Sādhu vata me āyasmā thinamiddhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desetū’ti.
Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu thinamiddhassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, tatiyo samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the third occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse …

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho, āvuso, uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharāmi uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmi.
Sādhu vata me āyasmā uddhaccakukkuccassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desetū’ti.
Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu uddhaccakukkuccassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, catuttho samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the fourth occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in doubt …

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ, āvuso, vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharāmi vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmi.
Sādhu vata me āyasmā vicikicchāya pahānāya dhammaṁ desetū’ti.
Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu vicikicchāya pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, pañcamo samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the fifth occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu yaṁ nimittaṁ āgamma yaṁ nimittaṁ manasikaroto anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti taṁ nimittaṁ nappajānāti tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant doesn’t understand what kind of meditation they need to focus on in order to end the defilements without delay. On that occasion they should go to an esteemed mendicant and say:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho, āvuso, yaṁ nimittaṁ āgamma yaṁ nimittaṁ manasikaroto anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, taṁ nimittaṁ nappajānāmi.
segs.e: ‘I don’t understand what kind of meditation to focus on in order to end the defilements without delay.

segs.p: Sādhu vata me āyasmā āsavānaṁ khayāya dhammaṁ desetū’ti.
segs.e: Venerable, please teach me how to end the defilements.’

segs.p: Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayāya dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Then that esteemed mendicant teaches them how to end the defilements.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, chaṭṭho samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the sixth occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhu, cha samayā manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti.
segs.e: These are the six occasions for going to see an esteemed mendicant.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.28
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.28

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Dutiyasamayasutta
segs.e: Proper Occasions (2nd)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā therā bhikkhū bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time several senior mendicants were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Then after the meal, on their return from almsround, this discussion came up among them while sitting together in the pavilion.

segs.p: “ko nu kho, āvuso, samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti?
segs.e: “Reverends, how many occasions are there for going to see an esteemed mendicant?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pāde pakkhāletvā nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā, so samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, there’s a time after an esteemed mendicant’s meal when they return from almsround. Having washed their feet they sit down cross-legged, set their body straight, and bring mindfulness to the present. That is the proper occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to that mendicant:

segs.p: “na kho, āvuso, so samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend, that’s not the proper occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pāde pakkhāletvā nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā, cārittakilamathopissa tasmiṁ samaye appaṭippassaddho hoti, bhattakilamathopissa tasmiṁ samaye appaṭippassaddho hoti.
segs.e: For at that time the fatigue from walking and from eating has not faded away.

segs.p: Tasmā so asamayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.

Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito vihārapacchāyāyaṁ nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā, so samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti.
segs.e: There’s a time late in the afternoon when an esteemed mendicant comes out of retreat. They sit cross-legged in the shade of their porch, set their body straight, and bring mindfulness to the present. That is the proper occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to that mendicant:

segs.p: “na kho, āvuso, so samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend, that’s not the proper occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito vihārapacchāyāyaṁ nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā, yadevassa divā samādhinimittaṁ manasikataṁ hoti tadevassa tasmiṁ samaye samudācarati.
segs.e: For at that time they are still practicing the same meditation subject as a basis of immersion that they focused on during the day.

segs.p: Tasmā so asamayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.

Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā, so samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti.
segs.e: There’s a time when an esteemed mendicant has risen at the crack of dawn. They sit down cross-legged, set their body straight, and bring mindfulness to the present. That is the proper occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to that mendicant:

segs.p: “na kho, āvuso, so samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend, that’s not the proper occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā, ojaṭṭhāyissa tasmiṁ samaye kāyo hoti phāsussa hoti buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ.
segs.e: For at that time their body is full of vitality and they find it easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas.”

segs.p: Tasmā so asamayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun”ti.
Evaṁ vutte āyasmā mahākaccāno there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, Venerable Mahākaccāna said to those senior mendicants:

segs.p: “sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverends, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘chayime, bhikkhu, samayā manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: ‘Mendicant, there are six occasions for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Firstly, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire, and they don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. On that occasion they should go to an esteemed mendicant and say:

segs.p: “ahaṁ kho, āvuso, kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharāmi kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāmi.
segs.e: “My heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire, and I don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen.

segs.p: Sādhu vata me āyasmā kāmarāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desetū”ti.
segs.e: Venerable, please teach me how to give up sensual desire.”

segs.p: Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu kāmarāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Then that esteemed mendicant teaches them how to give up sensual desire.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, paṭhamo samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This is the first occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, yasmiṁ samaye bhikkhu byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe….
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant’s heart is overcome and mired in ill will …

segs.p: Thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati ….
segs.e: dullness and drowsiness …

segs.p: Uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati ….
segs.e: restlessness and remorse …

segs.p: Vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati ….
segs.e: doubt …

segs.p: Yaṁ nimittaṁ āgamma yaṁ nimittaṁ manasikaroto anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, taṁ nimittaṁ na jānāti na passati, tasmiṁ samaye manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a time when a mendicant doesn’t understand what kind of meditation they need to focus on in order to end the defilements without delay. On that occasion they should go to an esteemed mendicant and say,

segs.p: “ahaṁ kho, āvuso, yaṁ nimittaṁ āgamma yaṁ nimittaṁ manasikaroto anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti taṁ nimittaṁ na jānāmi na passāmi.
segs.e: “I don’t understand what kind of meditation to focus on in order to end the defilements without delay.

segs.p: Sādhu vata me āyasmā āsavānaṁ khayāya dhammaṁ desetū”ti.
segs.e: Venerable, please teach me how to end the defilements.”

segs.p: Tassa manobhāvanīyo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayāya dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Then that esteemed mendicant teaches them how to end the defilements.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhu, chaṭṭho samayo manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ’.
segs.e: This is the sixth occasion for going to see an esteemed mendicant.’

segs.p: Sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: Reverends, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘ime kho, bhikkhu, cha samayā manobhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno dassanāya upasaṅkamitun’”ti.
segs.e: ‘These are the six occasions for going to see an esteemed mendicant.’”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.29
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.29

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Udāyīsutta
segs.e: With Udāyī

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Udāyī,

segs.p: “kati nu kho, udāyi, anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti?
segs.e: “Udāyī, how many topics for recollection are there?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā udāyī tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: When he said this, Udāyī kept silent.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: And a second time …

segs.p: “kati nu kho, udāyi, anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti?
Dutiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī tuṇhī ahosi.
Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: and a third time, the Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “kati nu kho, udāyi, anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti?
segs.e: “Udāyī, how many topics for recollection are there?”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: And a second time and a third time Udāyī kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda said to Venerable Udāyī,

segs.p: “satthā taṁ, āvuso udāyi, āmantesī”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Udāyī, the Teacher is addressing you.”

segs.p: “Suṇomahaṁ, āvuso ānanda, bhagavato.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, I hear the Buddha.

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati—Seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo …pe…. Iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant recollects many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānan”ti.
segs.e: This is a topic for recollection.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Ānanda:

segs.p: “aññāsiṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda:
segs.e: “Ānanda, I know that

segs.p: ‘nevāyaṁ udāyī moghapuriso adhicittaṁ anuyutto viharatī’ti.
segs.e: this futile man Udāyī is not committed to the higher mind.

segs.p: Kati nu kho, ānanda, anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, how many topics for recollection are there?”

segs.p: “Pañca, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Sir, there are five topics for recollection.

segs.p: Katamāni pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ evaṁ bahulīkataṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: When this topic of recollection is developed and cultivated in this way it leads to blissful meditation in this very life.

segs.p: “Puna caparaṁ, bhante, bhikkhu ālokasaññaṁ manasi karoti, divā saññaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, yathā divā tathā rattiṁ, yathā rattiṁ tathā divā;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant focuses on the perception of light, focusing on the perception of day regardless of whether it’s night or day.

segs.p: iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
segs.e: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ evaṁ bahulīkataṁ ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: When this topic of recollection is developed and cultivated in this way it leads to knowledge and vision.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṁ uddhaṁ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṁ pūraṁ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant examines their own body up from the soles of the feet and down from the tips of the hairs, wrapped in skin and full of many kinds of filth.

segs.p: ‘atthi imasmiṁ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco, maṁsaṁ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṁ vakkaṁ, hadayaṁ yakanaṁ kilomakaṁ pihakaṁ papphāsaṁ, antaṁ antaguṇaṁ udariyaṁ karīsaṁ, pittaṁ semhaṁ pubbo lohitaṁ sedo medo, assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttan’ti.
segs.e: ‘In this body there is head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ evaṁ bahulīkataṁ kāmarāgappahānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: When this topic of recollection is developed and cultivated in this way it leads to giving up sensual desire.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, bhikkhu seyyathāpi passeyya sarīraṁ sivathikāya chaṭṭitaṁ ekāhamataṁ vā dvīhamataṁ vā tīhamataṁ vā uddhumātakaṁ vinīlakaṁ vipubbakajātaṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, suppose a mendicant were to see a corpse thrown in a charnel ground. And it had been dead for one, two, or three days, bloated, livid, and festering.

segs.p: So imameva kāyaṁ evaṁ upasaṁharati:
segs.e: They’d compare it with their own body:

segs.p: ‘ayampi kho kāyo evaṁdhammo evaṁbhāvī evaṁanatīto’ti.
segs.e: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi vā pana passeyya sarīraṁ sīvathikāya chaṭṭitaṁ kākehi vā khajjamānaṁ kulalehi vā khajjamānaṁ gijjhehi vā khajjamānaṁ sunakhehi vā khajjamānaṁ siṅgālehi vā khajjamānaṁ vividhehi vā pāṇakajātehi khajjamānaṁ.
segs.e: Or suppose they were to see a corpse thrown in a charnel ground being devoured by crows, hawks, vultures, hounds, jackals, and many kinds of little creatures.

segs.p: So imameva kāyaṁ evaṁ upasaṁharati:
segs.e: They’d compare it with their own body:

segs.p: ‘ayampi kho kāyo evaṁdhammo evaṁbhāvī evaṁanatīto’ti.
segs.e: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi vā pana passeyya sarīraṁ sīvathikāya chaṭṭitaṁ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ samaṁsalohitaṁ nhārusambandhaṁ …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, suppose they were to see a corpse thrown in a charnel ground, a skeleton with flesh and blood, held together by sinews …

segs.p: aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ nimmaṁsalohitamakkhitaṁ nhārusambandhaṁ …
segs.e: A skeleton without flesh but smeared with blood, and held together by sinews …

segs.p: aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ apagatamaṁsalohitaṁ nhārusambandhaṁ.
segs.e: A skeleton rid of flesh and blood, held together by sinews …

segs.p: Aṭṭhikāni apagatasambandhāni disāvidisāvikkhittāni, aññena hatthaṭṭhikaṁ aññena pādaṭṭhikaṁ aññena jaṅghaṭṭhikaṁ aññena ūruṭṭhikaṁ aññena kaṭiṭṭhikaṁ aññena phāsukaṭṭhikaṁ aññena piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhikaṁ aññena khandhaṭṭhikaṁ aññena gīvaṭṭhikaṁ aññena hanukaṭṭhikaṁ aññena dantakaṭṭhikaṁ aññena sīsakaṭāhaṁ, aṭṭhikāni setāni saṅkhavaṇṇappaṭibhāgāni aṭṭhikāni puñjakitāni terovassikāni aṭṭhikāni pūtīni cuṇṇakajātāni.
segs.e: Bones rid of sinews scattered in every direction. Here a hand-bone, there a foot-bone, here a shin-bone, there a thigh-bone, here a hip-bone, there a rib-bone, here a back-bone, there an arm-bone, here a neck-bone, there a jaw-bone, here a tooth, there the skull … White bones, the color of shells … Decrepit bones, heaped in a pile … Bones rotted and crumbled to powder.

segs.p: So imameva kāyaṁ evaṁ upasaṁharati:
segs.e: They’d compare it with their own body:

segs.p: ‘ayampi kho kāyo evaṁdhammo evaṁbhāvī evaṁanatīto’ti.
segs.e: ‘This body is also of that same nature, that same kind, and cannot go beyond that.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ evaṁ bahulīkataṁ asmimānasamugghātāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: When this topic of recollection is developed and cultivated in this way it leads to uprooting the conceit ‘I am’.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, giving up pleasure and pain, and ending former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ evaṁ bahulīkataṁ anekadhātupaṭivedhāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: When this topic of recollection is developed and cultivated in this way it leads to the penetration of many elements.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhante, pañca anussatiṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the five topics for recollection.”

segs.p: “Sādhu sādhu, ānanda.
segs.e: “Good, good, Ānanda.

segs.p: Tena hi tvaṁ, ānanda, idampi chaṭṭhaṁ anussatiṭṭhānaṁ dhārehi.
segs.e: Well then, Ānanda, you should also remember this sixth topic for recollection.

segs.p: Idhānanda, bhikkhu satova abhikkamati satova paṭikkamati satova tiṭṭhati satova nisīdati satova seyyaṁ kappeti satova kammaṁ adhiṭṭhāti.
segs.e: In this case, a mendicant goes out mindfully, returns mindfully, stands mindfully, sits mindfully, lies down mindfully, and focuses on work mindfully.

segs.p: Idaṁ, ānanda, anussatiṭṭhānaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ evaṁ bahulīkataṁ satisampajaññāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: When this topic of recollection is developed and cultivated in this way it leads to mindfulness and situational awareness.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.30
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.30

segs.p: 3. Anuttariyavagga
segs.e: 3. Unsurpassable

segs.p: Anuttariyasutta
segs.e: Unsurpassable

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, anuttariyāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six things are unsurpassable.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ, anussatānuttariyanti.
segs.e: The unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

segs.p: Katamañca, bhikkhave, dassanānuttariyaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the unsurpassable seeing?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco hatthiratanampi dassanāya gacchati, assaratanampi dassanāya gacchati, maṇiratanampi dassanāya gacchati, uccāvacaṁ vā pana dassanāya gacchati, samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā micchādiṭṭhikaṁ micchāpaṭipannaṁ dassanāya gacchati.
segs.e: Some people go to see an elephant-treasure, a horse-treasure, a jewel-treasure, or a diverse spectrum of sights; or ascetics and brahmins of wrong view and wrong practice.

segs.p: Atthetaṁ, bhikkhave, dassanaṁ; netaṁ natthīti vadāmi.
segs.e: There is such a seeing, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, dassanaṁ hīnaṁ gammaṁ pothujjanikaṁ anariyaṁ anatthasaṁhitaṁ, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: That seeing is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, tathāgataṁ vā tathāgatasāvakaṁ vā dassanāya gacchati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno, etadānuttariyaṁ, bhikkhave, dassanānaṁ sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ tathāgataṁ vā tathāgatasāvakaṁ vā dassanāya gacchati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno.
segs.e: The unsurpassable seeing is when someone with settled faith and fondness, sure and devoted, goes to see a Realized One or their disciple. This is in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dassanānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the unsurpassable seeing.

segs.p: Iti dassanānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: Such is the unsurpassable seeing.

segs.p: Savanānuttariyañca kathaṁ hoti?
segs.e: But what of the unsurpassable hearing?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco bherisaddampi savanāya gacchati, vīṇāsaddampi savanāya gacchati, gītasaddampi savanāya gacchati, uccāvacaṁ vā pana savanāya gacchati, samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā micchādiṭṭhikassa micchāpaṭipannassa dhammassavanāya gacchati.
segs.e: Some people go to hear the sound of drums, arched harps, singing, or a diverse spectrum of sounds; or ascetics and brahmins of wrong view and wrong practice.

segs.p: Atthetaṁ, bhikkhave, savanaṁ; netaṁ natthīti vadāmi.
segs.e: There is such a hearing, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, savanaṁ hīnaṁ gammaṁ pothujjanikaṁ anariyaṁ anatthasaṁhitaṁ, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: That hearing … doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā dhammassavanāya gacchati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno, etadānuttariyaṁ, bhikkhave, savanānaṁ sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā dhammassavanāya gacchati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno.
segs.e: The unsurpassable hearing is when someone with settled faith and fondness, sure and devoted, goes to hear the teaching of a Realized One or one of his disciples. …

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, savanānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the unsurpassable hearing.

segs.p: Iti dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: Such is the unsurpassable seeing and hearing.

segs.p: Lābhānuttariyañca kathaṁ hoti?
segs.e: But what of the unsurpassable acquisition?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puttalābhampi labhati, dāralābhampi labhati, dhanalābhampi labhati, uccāvacaṁ vā pana lābhaṁ labhati, samaṇe vā brāhmaṇe vā micchādiṭṭhike micchāpaṭipanne saddhaṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: Some people acquire a child, a wife, wealth, or a diverse spectrum of things; or they acquire faith in an ascetic or brahmin of wrong view and wrong practice.

segs.p: Attheso, bhikkhave, lābho; neso natthīti vadāmi.
segs.e: There is such an acquisition, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: So ca kho eso, bhikkhave, lābho hīno gammo pothujjaniko anariyo anatthasaṁhito, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: That acquisition … doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, tathāgate vā tathāgatasāvake vā saddhaṁ paṭilabhati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno, etadānuttariyaṁ, bhikkhave, lābhānaṁ sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ tathāgate vā tathāgatasāvake vā saddhaṁ paṭilabhati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno.
segs.e: The unsurpassable acquisition is when someone with settled faith and fondness, sure and devoted, acquires faith in a Realized One or their disciple. …

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, lābhānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the unsurpassable acquisition.

segs.p: Iti dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: Such is the unsurpassable seeing, hearing, and acquisition.

segs.p: Sikkhānuttariyañca kathaṁ hoti?
segs.e: But what of the unsurpassable training?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco hatthismimpi sikkhati, assasmimpi sikkhati, rathasmimpi sikkhati, dhanusmimpi sikkhati, tharusmimpi sikkhati, uccāvacaṁ vā pana sikkhati, samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā micchādiṭṭhikassa micchāpaṭipannassa sikkhati.
segs.e: Some people train in elephant riding, horse riding, chariot driving, archery, swordsmanship, or a diverse spectrum of things; or they train under an ascetic or brahmin of wrong view and wrong practice.

segs.p: Atthesā, bhikkhave, sikkhā; nesā natthīti vadāmi.
segs.e: There is such a training, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Sā ca kho esā, bhikkhave, sikkhā hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṁhitā, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: That training … doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye adhisīlampi sikkhati, adhicittampi sikkhati, adhipaññampi sikkhati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno, etadānuttariyaṁ, bhikkhave, sikkhānaṁ sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye adhisīlampi sikkhati, adhicittampi sikkhati, adhipaññampi sikkhati, niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno.
segs.e: The unsurpassable training is when someone with settled faith and fondness, sure and devoted, trains in the higher ethics, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom in the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One. …

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, sikkhānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the unsurpassable training.

segs.p: Iti dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: Such is the unsurpassable seeing, hearing, acquisition, and training.

segs.p: Pāricariyānuttariyañca kathaṁ hoti?
segs.e: But what of the unsurpassable service?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco khattiyampi paricarati, brāhmaṇampi paricarati, gahapatimpi paricarati, uccāvacaṁ vā pana paricarati, samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā micchādiṭṭhikaṁ micchāpaṭipannaṁ paricarati.
segs.e: Some people serve an aristocrat, a brahmin, a householder, or a diverse spectrum of people; or they serve ascetics and brahmins of wrong view and wrong practice.

segs.p: Atthesā, bhikkhave, pāricariyā; nesā natthīti vadāmi.
segs.e: There is such service, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Sā ca kho esā, bhikkhave, pāricariyā hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṁhitā, na nibbidāya …pe… na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: That service … doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, tathāgataṁ vā tathāgatasāvakaṁ vā paricarati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno, etadānuttariyaṁ, bhikkhave, pāricariyānaṁ sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ tathāgataṁ vā tathāgatasāvakaṁ vā paricarati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno.
segs.e: The unsurpassable service is when someone with settled faith and fondness, sure and devoted, serves a Realized One or their disciple. …

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the unsurpassable service.

segs.p: Iti dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: Such is the unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, and service.

segs.p: Anussatānuttariyañca kathaṁ hoti?
segs.e: But what of the unsurpassable recollection?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puttalābhampi anussarati, dāralābhampi anussarati, dhanalābhampi anussarati, uccāvacaṁ vā pana lābhaṁ anussarati, samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā micchādiṭṭhikaṁ micchāpaṭipannaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: Some people recollect a child, a wife, wealth, or a diverse spectrum of things; or they recollect an ascetic or brahmin of wrong view and wrong practice.

segs.p: Atthesā, bhikkhave, anussati; nesā natthīti vadāmi.
segs.e: There is such recollection, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Sā ca kho esā, bhikkhave, anussati hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṁhitā, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: That recollection is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, tathāgataṁ vā tathāgatasāvakaṁ vā anussarati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno, etadānuttariyaṁ, bhikkhave, anussatīnaṁ sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ tathāgataṁ vā tathāgatasāvakaṁ vā anussarati niviṭṭhasaddho niviṭṭhapemo ekantagato abhippasanno.
segs.e: The unsurpassable recollection is when someone with settled faith and fondness, sure and devoted, recollects a Realized One or their disciple. …

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, anussatānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: This is called the unsurpassable recollection.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha anuttariyānīti.
segs.e: These are the six unsurpassable things.

segs.p: Ye dassanānuttaraṁ laddhā,
segs.e: They’ve gained the unsurpassed seeing,

segs.p: savanañca anuttaraṁ;
segs.e: the unsurpassed hearing,

segs.p: Lābhānuttariyaṁ laddhā,
segs.e: and the unsurpassable acquisition.

segs.p: sikkhānuttariye ratā.
segs.e: They enjoy the unsurpassable training

segs.p: Upaṭṭhitā pāricariyā,
segs.e: and serve with care.

segs.p: bhāvayanti anussatiṁ;
segs.e: Then they develop recollection

segs.p: Vivekappaṭisaṁyuttaṁ,
segs.e: connected with seclusion,

segs.p: khemaṁ amatagāminiṁ.
segs.e: which is safe, and leads to freedom from death.

segs.p: Appamāde pamuditā,
segs.e: They rejoice in diligence,

segs.p: nipakā sīlasaṁvutā;
segs.e: alert and ethically restrained.

segs.p: Te ve kālena paccenti,
segs.e: And in time they arrive

segs.p: yattha dukkhaṁ nirujjhatī”ti.
segs.e: at the place where suffering ceases.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Anuttariyavaggo tatiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Sāmako aparihāniyo,
Bhayaṁ himavānussati;
Kaccāno dve ca samayā,
Udāyī anuttariyenāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.31
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.31

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Sekhasutta
segs.e: A Trainee

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “These six things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā, saṅgaṇikārāmatā, indriyesu aguttadvāratā, bhojane amattaññutā—
segs.e: They relish work, talk, sleep, and company. They don’t guard the sense doors, and they eat too much.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These six things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Na kammārāmatā, na bhassārāmatā, na niddārāmatā, na saṅgaṇikārāmatā, indriyesu guttadvāratā, bhojane mattaññutā—
segs.e: They don’t relish work, talk, sleep, and company. They guard the sense doors, and they don’t eat too much.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.32
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.32

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Paṭhamaaparihānasutta
segs.e: Non-decline (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Sir, these six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, appamādagāravatā, paṭisanthāragāravatā—
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training, for diligence, and for hospitality.

segs.p: ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.”

segs.p: Idamavoca sā devatā.
segs.e: That is what that deity said,

segs.p: Samanuñño satthā ahosi.
segs.e: and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho sā devatā “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then that deity, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened, adding:

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
‘chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
Katame cha?
Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, appamādagāravatā, paṭisanthāragāravatā—
ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
Idamavoca, bhikkhave, sā devatā.
Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
Satthugaru dhammagaru,
segs.e: “Respect for the Teacher and the teaching,

segs.p: saṅghe ca tibbagāravo;
segs.e: and keen respect for the Saṅgha;

segs.p: Appamādagaru bhikkhu,
segs.e: a mendicant who respects diligence

segs.p: paṭisanthāragāravo;
segs.e: and hospitality

segs.p: Abhabbo parihānāya,
segs.e: can’t decline,

segs.p: nibbānasseva santike”ti.
segs.e: and has drawn near to extinguishment.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.33
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.33

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Dutiyaaparihānasutta
segs.e: Non-decline (2nd)

segs.p: “Imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Tonight, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and said to me:

segs.p: ‘chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, these six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, hirigāravatā, ottappagāravatā—
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training, for conscience, and for prudence.

segs.p: ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
segs.e: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.’

segs.p: Idamavoca, bhikkhave, sā devatā.
segs.e: That is what that deity said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Satthugaru dhammagaru,
segs.e: One respectful of the Teacher and the teaching,

segs.p: saṅghe ca tibbagāravo;
segs.e: keenly respecting the Saṅgha;

segs.p: Hiriottappasampanno,
segs.e: endowed with conscience and prudence,

segs.p: sappatisso sagāravo;
segs.e: reverential and respectful—

segs.p: Abhabbo parihānāya,
segs.e: it is impossible for them to decline;

segs.p: nibbānasseva santike”ti.
segs.e: they have drawn near to extinguishment.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.34
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.34

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Mahāmoggallānasutta
segs.e: With Mahāmoggallāna

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

segs.p: “katamesānaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “Which gods know that they are

segs.p: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti?
segs.e: stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena tisso nāma bhikkhu adhunākālaṅkato aññataraṁ brahmalokaṁ upapanno hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time a monk named Tissa had recently passed away and been reborn in a realm of divinity.

segs.p: Tatrapi naṁ evaṁ jānanti:
segs.e: There they knew that

segs.p: “tisso brahmā mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo”ti.
segs.e: The divinity Tissa was very mighty and powerful.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ—jetavane antarahito tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahosi.
segs.e: And then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in that realm of divinity.

segs.p: Addasā kho tisso brahmā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: Tissa saw Moggallāna coming off in the distance,

segs.p: Disvāna āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to him,

segs.p: “ehi kho, mārisa moggallāna; svāgataṁ, mārisa moggallāna;
segs.e: “Come, my good fellow Moggallāna! Welcome, my good fellow!

segs.p: cirassaṁ kho, mārisa moggallāna; imaṁ pariyāyamakāsi, yadidaṁ idhāgamanāya.
segs.e: It’s been a long time since you took the opportunity to come here.

segs.p: Nisīda, mārisa moggallāna, idamāsanaṁ paññattan”ti.
segs.e: Sit, my good Moggallāna, this seat is for you.”

segs.p: Nisīdi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno paññatte āsane.
segs.e: Moggallāna sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Tissopi kho brahmā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Tissa bowed to Moggallāna and sat to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho tissaṁ brahmānaṁ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
segs.e: Moggallāna said to him,

segs.p: “Katamesānaṁ kho, tissa, devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti?
segs.e: “Tissa, which gods know that they are stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

segs.p: “Cātumahārājikānaṁ kho, mārisa moggallāna, devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti.
segs.e: “The gods of the four great kings know this.”

segs.p: “Sabbesaññeva nu kho, tissa, cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti?
segs.e: “But do all of them know this?”

segs.p: “Na kho, mārisa moggallāna, sabbesaṁ cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti.
segs.e: “No, my good Moggallāna, not all of them.

segs.p: Ye kho te, mārisa moggallāna, cātumahārājikā devā buddhe aveccappasādena asamannāgatā dhamme aveccappasādena asamannāgatā saṅghe aveccappasādena asamannāgatā ariyakantehi sīlehi asamannāgatā na tesaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti.
segs.e: Those who lack experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and lack the ethics loved by the noble ones, do not know that they are stream-enterers.

segs.p: Ye ca kho te, mārisa moggallāna, cātumahārājikā devā buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā, tesaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti.
segs.e: But those who have experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and have the ethics loved by the noble ones, do know that they are stream-enterers.”

segs.p: “Cātumahārājikānaññeva nu kho, tissa, devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti udāhu tāvatiṁsānampi devānaṁ …pe…
segs.e: “But Tissa, is it only the gods of the four great kings who know that they are stream-enterers, or do the gods of the thirty-three …

segs.p: yāmānampi devānaṁ …
segs.e: the gods of Yama …

segs.p: tusitānampi devānaṁ …
segs.e: the joyful gods …

segs.p: nimmānaratīnampi devānaṁ …
segs.e: the gods who love to create …
