segs.p: paranimmitavasavattīnampi devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti?
segs.e: and the gods who control what is created by others know that they are stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

segs.p: “Paranimmitavasavattīnampi kho, mārisa moggallāna, devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti.
segs.e: “The gods of these various classes know this.”

segs.p: “Sabbesaññeva nu kho, tissa, paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti?
segs.e: “But do all of them know this?”

segs.p: “Na kho, mārisa moggallāna, sabbesaṁ paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti.
segs.e: “No, my good Moggallāna, not all of them.

segs.p: Ye kho te, mārisa moggallāna, paranimmitavasavattī devā buddhe aveccappasādena asamannāgatā, dhamme aveccappasādena asamannāgatā, saṅghe aveccappasādena asamannāgatā, ariyakantehi sīlehi asamannāgatā, na tesaṁ devānaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti.
segs.e: Those who lack experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and lack the ethics loved by the noble ones, do not know that they are stream-enterers.

segs.p: Ye ca kho te, mārisa moggallāna, paranimmitavasavattī devā buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā tesaṁ evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘sotāpannā nāma avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti.
segs.e: But those who have experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and have the ethics loved by the noble ones, do know that they are stream-enterers.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno tissassa brahmuno bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā: “seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ: ‘brahmaloke antarahito jetavane pāturahosī’”ti.
segs.e: Moggallāna approved and agreed with what the divinity Tissa said. Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from that realm of divinity and reappeared in Jeta’s Grove.

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.35
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.35

segs.p: Vijjābhāgiyasutta
segs.e: Things That Play a Part in Realization

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā vijjābhāgiyā.
segs.e: “These six things play a part in realization.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā—
segs.e: The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhammā vijjābhāgiyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the six things that play a part in realization.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.

segs.p: Vivādamūlasutta
segs.e: Roots of Dispute

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, vivādamūlāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these six roots of dispute.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant is irritable and acrimonious.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti.
segs.e: Such a mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and they don’t fulfill the training.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso, dhamme agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghe agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāya na paripūrakārī so saṅghe vivādaṁ janeti, yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: They create a dispute in the Saṅgha, which is for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha.
segs.e: If you see such a root of dispute in yourselves or others, you should try to give up this bad thing.

segs.p: Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha.
segs.e: If you don’t see it, you should practice so that it doesn’t come up in the future.

segs.p: Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṁ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how to give up this bad root of dispute, so it doesn’t come up in the future.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti paḷāsī …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is offensive and contemptuous …

segs.p: issukī hoti maccharī …
segs.e: They’re jealous and stingy …

segs.p: saṭho hoti māyāvī …
segs.e: They’re devious and deceitful …

segs.p: pāpiccho hoti micchādiṭṭhi …
segs.e: They have corrupt wishes and wrong view …

segs.p: sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī.
segs.e: They’re attached to their own views, holding them tight, and refusing to let go.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti.
segs.e: Such a mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and they don’t fulfill the training.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso, dhamme … saṅghe agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāya na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe vivādaṁ janeti, yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: They create a dispute in the Saṅgha, which is for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha.
segs.e: If you see such a root of dispute in yourselves or others, you should try to give up this bad thing.

segs.p: Evarūpañce tumhe, bhikkhave, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha.
segs.e: If you don’t see it, you should practice so that it doesn’t come up in the future.

segs.p: Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṁ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how to give up this bad root of dispute, so it doesn’t come up in the future.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha vivādamūlānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six roots of dispute.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.37
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.37

segs.p: Chaḷaṅgadānasutta
segs.e: A Gift With Six Factors

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena veḷukaṇḍakī nandamātā upāsikā sāriputtamoggallānappamukhe bhikkhusaṅghe chaḷaṅgasamannāgataṁ dakkhiṇaṁ patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: Now at that time Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother, was preparing a religious donation with six factors for the mendicant Saṅgha headed by Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena veḷukaṇḍakiṁ nandamātaraṁ upāsikaṁ sāriputtamoggallānappamukhe bhikkhusaṅghe chaḷaṅgasamannāgataṁ dakkhiṇaṁ patiṭṭhāpentiṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw her doing this, with his clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman,

segs.p: Disvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: and he addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “esā, bhikkhave, veḷukaṇḍakī nandamātā upāsikā sāriputtamoggallānappamukhe bhikkhusaṅghe chaḷaṅgasamannāgataṁ dakkhiṇaṁ patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: “This Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother, is preparing a religious donation with six factors for the mendicant Saṅgha headed by Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, chaḷaṅgasamannāgatā dakkhiṇā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a religious donation have six factors?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dāyakassa tīṇaṅgāni honti, paṭiggāhakānaṁ tīṇaṅgāni.
segs.e: Three factors apply to the donor and three to the recipients.

segs.p: Katamāni dāyakassa tīṇaṅgāni?
segs.e: What three factors apply to the donor?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dāyako pubbeva dānā sumano hoti, dadaṁ cittaṁ pasādeti, datvā attamano hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a donor is in a good mood before giving, while giving they feel confident, and after giving they’re uplifted.

segs.p: Imāni dāyakassa tīṇaṅgāni.
segs.e: These three factors apply to the donor.

segs.p: Katamāni paṭiggāhakānaṁ tīṇaṅgāni?
segs.e: What three factors apply to the recipients?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, paṭiggāhakā vītarāgā vā honti rāgavinayāya vā paṭipannā, vītadosā vā honti dosavinayāya vā paṭipannā, vītamohā vā honti mohavinayāya vā paṭipannā.
segs.e: It’s when the recipients are free of greed, hate, and delusion, or practicing to be free of them.

segs.p: Imāni paṭiggāhakānaṁ tīṇaṅgāni.
segs.e: These three factors apply to the recipients.

segs.p: Iti dāyakassa tīṇaṅgāni, paṭiggāhakānaṁ tīṇaṅgāni.
segs.e: Thus three factors apply to the donor and three to the recipients.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, chaḷaṅgasamannāgatā dakkhiṇā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a religious donation has six factors.

segs.p: Evaṁ chaḷaṅgasamannāgatāya, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇāya na sukaraṁ puññassa pamāṇaṁ gahetuṁ:
segs.e: It’s not easy to grasp the merit of such a six-factored donation by saying that

segs.p: ‘ettako puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro sovaggiko sukhavipāko saggasaṁvattaniko iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness and is conducive to heaven, ripening in happiness and leading to heaven. And it leads to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, to welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandhotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde na sukaraṁ udakassa pamāṇaṁ gahetuṁ:
segs.e: It’s like trying to grasp how much water is in the ocean. It’s not easy to say

segs.p: ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakānīti vā ettakāni udakāḷhakasatānīti vā ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassānīti vā ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassānī’ti vā.
segs.e: how many gallons, how many hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands of gallons there are.

segs.p: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāudakakkhandhotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, evaṁ chaḷaṅgasamannāgatāya dakkhiṇāya na sukaraṁ puññassa pamāṇaṁ gahetuṁ:
segs.e: In the same way, it’s not easy to grasp the merit of such a six-factored donation …

segs.p: ‘ettako puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro sovaggiko sukhavipāko saggasaṁvattaniko iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattatī’ti.
Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandhotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti.
“Pubbeva dānā sumano,
segs.e: A good mood before giving,

segs.p: dadaṁ cittaṁ pasādaye;
segs.e: confidence while giving,

segs.p: Datvā attamano hoti,
segs.e: feeling uplifted after giving:

segs.p: esā yaññassa sampadā.
segs.e: this is the perfect sacrifice.

segs.p: Vītarāgā vītadosā,
segs.e: Free of greed, free of hate,

segs.p: vītamohā anāsavā;
segs.e: free of delusion, undefiled;

segs.p: Khettaṁ yaññassa sampannaṁ,
segs.e: this is the field for the perfect sacrifice,

segs.p: saññatā brahmacārayo.
segs.e: the disciplined spiritual practitioners.

segs.p: Sayaṁ ācamayitvāna,
segs.e: After rinsing,

segs.p: datvā sakehi pāṇibhi;
segs.e: you give with your own hands.

segs.p: Attano parato ceso,
segs.e: This sacrifice is very fruitful

segs.p: yañño hoti mahapphalo.
segs.e: for both yourself and others.

segs.p: Evaṁ yajitvā medhāvī,
segs.e: When an intelligent, faithful person,

segs.p: saddho muttena cetasā;
segs.e: sacrifices like this, with a mind of letting go,

segs.p: Abyāpajjaṁ sukhaṁ lokaṁ,
segs.e: that astute one is reborn

segs.p: paṇḍito upapajjatī”ti.
segs.e: in a happy, pleasing world.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.38
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.38

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Attakārīsutta
segs.e: One’s Own Volition

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ahañhi, bho gotama, evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi:
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, this is my doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘natthi attakāro, natthi parakāro’”ti.
segs.e: One does not act of one’s own volition, nor does one act of another’s volition.”

segs.p: “Māhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, evaṁvādiṁ evaṁdiṭṭhiṁ addasaṁ vā assosiṁ vā.
segs.e: “Brahmin, may I never see or hear of anyone holding such a doctrine or view!

segs.p: Kathañhi nāma sayaṁ abhikkamanto, sayaṁ paṭikkamanto evaṁ vakkhati:
segs.e: How on earth can someone who comes and goes on his own say that

segs.p: ‘natthi attakāro, natthi parakāro’ti.
segs.e: one does not act of one’s own volition, nor does one act of another’s volition?

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, atthi ārabbhadhātū”ti?
segs.e: What do you think, brahmin, is there an element of initiative?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Ārabbhadhātuyā sati ārabbhavanto sattā paññāyantī”ti?
segs.e: “Since this is so, do we find sentient beings who initiate activity?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, ārabbhadhātuyā sati ārabbhavanto sattā paññāyanti, ayaṁ sattānaṁ attakāro ayaṁ parakāro.
segs.e: “Since there is an element of initiative, and sentient beings who initiate activity are found, sentient beings act of their own volition or that of another.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, atthi nikkamadhātu …pe…
segs.e: What do you think, brahmin, is there an element of persistence …

segs.p: atthi parakkamadhātu …
segs.e: exertion …

segs.p: atthi thāmadhātu …
segs.e: strength …

segs.p: atthi ṭhitidhātu …
segs.e: endurance …

segs.p: atthi upakkamadhātū”ti?
segs.e: exertion?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Upakkamadhātuyā sati upakkamavanto sattā paññāyantī”ti?
segs.e: “Since this is so, do we find sentient beings who have exertion?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, upakkamadhātuyā sati upakkamavanto sattā paññāyanti, ayaṁ sattānaṁ attakāro ayaṁ parakāro.
segs.e: “Since there is an element of exertion, and sentient beings who have exertion are found, sentient beings act of their own volition or that of another.

segs.p: Māhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, evaṁvādiṁ evaṁdiṭṭhiṁ addasaṁ vā assosiṁ vā.
segs.e: Brahmin, may I never see or hear of anyone holding such a doctrine or view!

segs.p: Kathañhi nāma sayaṁ abhikkamanto sayaṁ paṭikkamanto evaṁ vakkhati:
segs.e: How on earth can someone who comes and goes on his own say that

segs.p: ‘natthi attakāro natthi parakāro’”ti.
segs.e: one does not act of one’s own volition, nor does one act of another’s volition?”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.39
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.39

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Nidānasutta
segs.e: Sources

segs.p: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three sources that give rise to deeds.

segs.p: Katamāni tīṇi?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Lobho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, doso nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, moho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion are sources that give rise to deeds.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, lobhā alobho samudeti;
segs.e: Greed doesn’t give rise to contentment.

segs.p: atha kho, bhikkhave, lobhā lobhova samudeti.
segs.e: Rather, greed just gives rise to greed.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, dosā adoso samudeti;
segs.e: Hate doesn’t give rise to love.

segs.p: atha kho, bhikkhave, dosā dosova samudeti.
segs.e: Rather, hate just gives rise to hate.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, mohā amoho samudeti;
segs.e: Delusion doesn’t give rise to understanding.

segs.p: atha kho, bhikkhave, mohā mohova samudeti.
segs.e: Rather, delusion just gives rise to delusion.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, lobhajena kammena dosajena kammena mohajena kammena devā paññāyanti, manussā paññāyanti, yā vā panaññāpi kāci sugatiyo.
segs.e: It’s not because of deeds born of greed, hate, and delusion that gods, humans, or those in any other good places are found.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, lobhajena kammena dosajena kammena mohajena kammena nirayo paññāyati tiracchānayoni paññāyati pettivisayo paññāyati, yā vā panaññāpi kāci duggatiyo.
segs.e: Rather, it’s because of deeds born of greed, hate, and delusion that hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, or any other bad places are found.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāya.
segs.e: These are three sources that give rise to deeds.

segs.p: Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāya.
segs.e: Mendicants, there are these three sources that give rise to deeds.

segs.p: Katamāni tīṇi?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Alobho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, adoso nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, amoho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya.
segs.e: Contentment, love, and understanding are sources that give rise to deeds.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, alobhā lobho samudeti;
segs.e: Contentment doesn’t give rise to greed.

segs.p: atha kho, bhikkhave, alobhā alobhova samudeti.
segs.e: Rather, contentment just gives rise to contentment.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, adosā doso samudeti;
segs.e: Love doesn’t give rise to hate.

segs.p: atha kho, bhikkhave, adosā adosova samudeti.
segs.e: Rather, love just gives rise to love.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, amohā moho samudeti;
segs.e: Understanding doesn’t give rise to delusion.

segs.p: atha kho, bhikkhave, amohā amohova samudeti.
segs.e: Rather, understanding just gives rise to understanding.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, alobhajena kammena adosajena kammena amohajena kammena nirayo paññāyati tiracchānayoni paññāyati pettivisayo paññāyati, yā vā panaññāpi kāci duggatiyo.
segs.e: It’s not because of deeds born of contentment, love, and understanding that hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, or any other bad places are found.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, alobhajena kammena adosajena kammena amohajena kammena devā paññāyanti, manussā paññāyanti, yā vā panaññāpi kāci sugatiyo.
segs.e: Rather, it’s because of deeds born of contentment, love, and understanding that gods, humans, or those in any other good places are found.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are three sources that give rise to deeds.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.40
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.40

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Kimilasutta
segs.e: With Kimbila

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kimilāyaṁ viharati niculavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kimbilā in the Freshwater Mangrove Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā kimilo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā kimilo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Kimbila went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why the true teaching does not last long after the final quenching of the Realized One?”

segs.p: “Idha, kimila, tathāgate parinibbute bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari agāravā viharanti appatissā, dhamme agāravā viharanti appatissā, saṅghe agāravā viharanti appatissā, sikkhāya agāravā viharanti appatissā, appamāde agāravā viharanti appatissā, paṭisanthāre agāravā viharanti appatissā.
segs.e: “Kimbila, it’s when the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen lack respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality after the final quenching of the Realized One.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, kimila, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti”.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why the true teaching does not last long after the final quenching of the Realized One.”

segs.p: “Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why the true teaching does last long after the final quenching of the Realized One?”

segs.p: “Idha, kimila, tathāgate parinibbute bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, dhamme sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, saṅghe sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, sikkhāya sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, appamāde sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, paṭisanthāre sagāravā viharanti sappatissā.
segs.e: “Kimbila, it’s when the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen maintain respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality after the final quenching of the Realized One.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, kimila, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why the true teaching does last long after the final quenching of the Realized One.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.41
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.41

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Dārukkhandhasutta
segs.e: A Tree Trunk

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā sāriputto rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasa aññatarasmiṁ padese mahantaṁ dārukkhandhaṁ.
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, descended the Vulture’s Peak together with several mendicants. At a certain spot he saw a large tree trunk,

segs.p: Disvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: and he addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: “passatha no, āvuso, tumhe amuṁ mahantaṁ dārukkhandhan”ti?
segs.e: “Reverends, do you see this large tree trunk?”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend.”

segs.p: “Ākaṅkhamāno, āvuso, bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto amuṁ dārukkhandhaṁ pathavītveva adhimucceyya.
segs.e: “If they wanted to, a mendicant with psychic powers who has mastered their mind could determine this tree trunk to be nothing but earth.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Atthi, āvuso, amumhi dārukkhandhe pathavīdhātu, yaṁ nissāya bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto amuṁ dārukkhandhaṁ pathavītveva adhimucceyya.
segs.e: Because the earth element exists in the tree trunk. Relying on that a mendicant with psychic powers could determine it to be nothing but earth.

segs.p: Ākaṅkhamāno, āvuso, bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto amuṁ dārukkhandhaṁ āpotveva adhimucceyya …pe…
segs.e: If they wanted to, a mendicant with psychic powers who has mastered their mind could determine this tree trunk to be nothing but water. …

segs.p: tejotveva adhimucceyya …
segs.e: Or they could determine it to be nothing but fire …

segs.p: vāyotveva adhimucceyya …
segs.e: Or they could determine it to be nothing but air …

segs.p: subhantveva adhimucceyya …
segs.e: Or they could determine it to be nothing but beautiful …

segs.p: asubhantveva adhimucceyya.
segs.e: Or they could determine it to be nothing but ugly.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Atthi, āvuso, amumhi dārukkhandhe asubhadhātu, yaṁ nissāya bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto amuṁ dārukkhandhaṁ asubhantveva adhimucceyyā”ti.
segs.e: Because the element of ugliness exists in the tree trunk. Relying on that a mendicant with psychic powers could determine it to be nothing but ugly.”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.42
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.42

segs.p: 4. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 4. Deities

segs.p: Nāgitasutta
segs.e: With Nāgita

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena icchānaṅgalaṁ nāma kosalānaṁ brāhmaṇagāmo tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a village of the Kosalan brahmins named Icchānaṅgala.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe.
segs.e: He stayed in a forest near Icchānaṅgala.

segs.p: Assosuṁ kho icchānaṅgalakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā:
segs.e: The brahmins and householders of Icchānaṅgala heard:

segs.p: “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito icchānaṅgalaṁ anuppatto icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe.
segs.e: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Icchānaṅgala. He is staying in a forest near Icchānaṅgala.

segs.p: Taṁ kho pana bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ evaṁ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato:
segs.e: He has this good reputation:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno …pe… buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: So imaṁ lokaṁ sadevakaṁ …pe… arahataṁ dassanaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others. He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

segs.p: Atha kho icchānaṅgalakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā tassā rattiyā accayena pahūtaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ ādāya yena icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bahidvārakoṭṭhake aṭṭhaṁsu uccāsaddā mahāsaddā.
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, they took abundant fresh and cooked foods and went to the forest near Icchānaṅgala, where they stood outside the gates making a colossal racket.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nāgito bhagavato upaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time Venerable Nāgita was the Buddha’s attendant.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ nāgitaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Nāgita,

segs.p: “ke pana te, nāgita, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope”ti?
segs.e: “Nāgita, who’s making that colossal racket? You’d think it was fishermen hauling in a catch!”

segs.p: “Ete, bhante, icchānaṅgalakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā pahūtaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ ādāya bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitā bhagavantaṁyeva uddissa bhikkhusaṅghañcā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, it’s these brahmins and householders of Icchānaṅgala. They’ve brought many fresh and cooked foods, and they’re standing outside the gates wanting to offer it specially to the Buddha and the mendicant Saṅgha.”

segs.p: “Māhaṁ, nāgita, yasena samāgamaṁ, mā ca mayā yaso.
segs.e: “Nāgita, may I never become famous. May fame not come to me.

segs.p: Yo kho, nāgita, nayimassa nekkhammasukhassa pavivekasukhassa upasamasukhassa sambodhasukhassa nikāmalābhī assa akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, yassāhaṁ nekkhammasukhassa pavivekasukhassa upasamasukhassa sambodhasukhassa nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: There are those who can’t get the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of awakening when they want, without trouble or difficulty like I can.

segs.p: so taṁ mīḷhasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ lābhasakkārasilokasukhaṁ sādiyeyyā”ti.
segs.e: Let them enjoy the filthy, lazy pleasure of possessions, honor, and popularity.”

segs.p: “Adhivāsetu dāni, bhante, bhagavā; adhivāsetu, sugato;
segs.e: “Sir, may the Blessed One please relent now! May the Holy One relent!

segs.p: adhivāsanakālo dāni, bhante, bhagavato.
segs.e: Now is the time for the Buddha to relent.

segs.p: Yena yeneva dāni, bhante, bhagavā gamissati, tanninnāva bhavissanti brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamā ceva jānapadā ca.
segs.e: Wherever the Buddha now goes, the brahmins and householders, and people of town and country will incline the same way.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, thullaphusitake deve vassante yathāninnaṁ udakāni pavattanti;
segs.e: It’s like when the heavens rain heavily and the water flows downhill.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhante, yena yeneva dāni bhagavā gamissati, tanninnāva bhavissanti brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamā ceva jānapadā ca.
segs.e: In the same way, wherever the Buddha now goes, the brahmins and householders, and people of town and country will incline the same way.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hi, bhante, bhagavato sīlapaññāṇan”ti.
segs.e: Because of the Buddha’s ethics and wisdom.”

segs.p: “Māhaṁ, nāgita, yasena samāgamaṁ, mā ca mayā yaso.
segs.e: “Nāgita, may I never become famous. May fame not come to me.

segs.p: Yo kho, nāgita, nayimassa nekkhammasukhassa pavivekasukhassa upasamasukhassa sambodhasukhassa nikāmalābhī assa akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, yassāhaṁ nekkhammasukhassa pavivekasukhassa upasamasukhassa sambodhasukhassa nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: There are those who can’t get the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of awakening when they want, without trouble or difficulty like I can.

segs.p: so taṁ mīḷhasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ lābhasakkārasilokasukhaṁ sādiyeyya.
segs.e: Let them enjoy the filthy, lazy pleasure of possessions, honor, and popularity.

segs.p: Idhāhaṁ, nāgita, bhikkhuṁ passāmi gāmantavihāriṁ samāhitaṁ nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: Take a mendicant living within a village who I see sitting immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, nāgita, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: I think to myself:

segs.p: ‘idānimaṁ āyasmantaṁ ārāmiko vā upaṭṭhahissati samaṇuddeso vā taṁ tamhā samādhimhā cāvessatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now a monastery worker, a novice, or a fellow practitioner will make this venerable fall from immersion.’

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ, nāgita, tassa bhikkhuno na attamano homi gāmantavihārena.
segs.e: So I’m not pleased that that mendicant is living within a village.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, nāgita, bhikkhuṁ passāmi āraññikaṁ araññe pacalāyamānaṁ nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: Take a mendicant in the wilderness who I see sitting nodding in meditation.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, nāgita, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: I think to myself:

segs.p: ‘idāni ayamāyasmā imaṁ niddākilamathaṁ paṭivinodetvā araññasaññaṁyeva manasi karissati ekattan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now this venerable, having dispelled that sleepiness and weariness, will focus just on the unified perception of wilderness.’

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ, nāgita, tassa bhikkhuno attamano homi araññavihārena.
segs.e: So I’m pleased that that mendicant is living in the wilderness.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, nāgita, bhikkhuṁ passāmi āraññikaṁ araññe asamāhitaṁ nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: Take a mendicant in the wilderness who I see sitting without being immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, nāgita, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: I think to myself:

segs.p: ‘idāni ayamāyasmā asamāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ samādahissati, samāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ anurakkhissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now if this venerable’s mind is not immersed in samādhi they will immerse it; or if it is immersed in samādhi, they will preserve it.’

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ, nāgita, tassa bhikkhuno attamano homi araññavihārena.
segs.e: So I’m pleased that that mendicant is living in the wilderness.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, nāgita, bhikkhuṁ passāmi āraññikaṁ araññe samāhitaṁ nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: Take a mendicant in the wilderness who I see sitting immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, nāgita, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: I think to myself:

segs.p: ‘idāni ayamāyasmā avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ vimocessati, vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ anurakkhissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now this venerable will free the unfreed mind or preserve the freed mind.’

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ, nāgita, tassa bhikkhuno attamano homi araññavihārena.
segs.e: So I’m pleased that that mendicant is living in the wilderness.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, nāgita, bhikkhuṁ passāmi gāmantavihāriṁ lābhiṁ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who I see living within a village receiving robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: So taṁ lābhasakkārasilokaṁ nikāmayamāno riñcati paṭisallānaṁ riñcati araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni;
segs.e: Enjoying possessions, honor, and popularity they neglect retreat, and they neglect remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: gāmanigamarājadhāniṁ osaritvā vāsaṁ kappeti.
segs.e: They come down to villages, towns, and capital cities and make their home there.

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ, nāgita, tassa bhikkhuno na attamano homi gāmantavihārena.
segs.e: So I’m not pleased that that mendicant is living within a village.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, nāgita, bhikkhuṁ passāmi āraññikaṁ lābhiṁ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who I see in the wilderness receiving robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: So taṁ lābhasakkārasilokaṁ paṭipaṇāmetvā na riñcati paṭisallānaṁ na riñcati araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni.
segs.e: Fending off possessions, honor, and popularity they don’t neglect retreat, and they don’t neglect remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Tenāhaṁ, nāgita, tassa bhikkhuno attamano homi araññavihārena.
segs.e: So I’m pleased that that mendicant is living in the wilderness.

segs.p: Yasmāhaṁ, nāgita, samaye addhānamaggappaṭipanno na kañci passāmi purato vā pacchato vā, phāsu me, nāgita, tasmiṁ samaye hoti antamaso uccārapassāvakammāyā”ti.
segs.e: Nāgita, when I’m walking along a road and I don’t see anyone ahead or behind I feel relaxed, even if I need to urinate or defecate.”

segs.p: Dvādasamaṁ.
Devatāvaggo catuttho.
Tassuddānaṁ
Sekhā dve aparihāni,
Moggallāna vijjābhāgiyā;
Vivādadānattakārī nidānaṁ,
Kimiladārukkhandhena nāgitoti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.43
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.43

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Nāgasutta
segs.e: The Giant

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, after the meal, on his return from almsround, he addressed Venerable Ānanda,

segs.p: “āyāmānanda, yena pubbārāmo migāramātupāsādo tenupasaṅkamissāma divāvihārāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Come, Ānanda, let’s go to the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery for the day’s meditation.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ yena pubbārāmo migāramātupāsādo tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: So the Buddha went with Ānanda to the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: In the late afternoon the Buddha came out of retreat and addressed Ānanda,

segs.p: “āyāmānanda, yena pubbakoṭṭhako tenupasaṅkamissāma gattāni parisiñcitun”ti.
segs.e: “Come, Ānanda, let’s go to the eastern gate to bathe.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ yena pubbakoṭṭhako tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṁ.
segs.e: So the Buddha went with Ānanda to the eastern gate to bathe.

segs.p: Pubbakoṭṭhake gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno.
segs.e: When he had bathed and emerged from the water he stood in one robe drying his limbs.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa seto nāma nāgo mahātūriyatāḷitavāditena pubbakoṭṭhakā paccuttarati.
segs.e: Now, at that time King Pasenadi had a giant bull elephant called “White”. It emerged from the eastern gate to the beating and playing of musical instruments.

segs.p: Apissu taṁ jano disvā evamāha:
segs.e: When people saw it they said,

segs.p: “abhirūpo vata bho rañño nāgo; dassanīyo vata bho rañño nāgo; pāsādiko vata, bho, rañño nāgo, kāyupapanno vata bho rañño nāgo”ti.
segs.e: “The royal giant is so handsome! The royal giant is so good-looking! The royal giant is so lovely! The royal giant has such a big body!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When they said this, Venerable Udāyī said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “hatthimeva nu kho, bhante, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ kāyupapannaṁ jano disvā evamāha:
segs.e: “Sir, is it only when they see elephants with such a big, formidable body that people say:

segs.p: ‘nāgo vata bho nāgo’ti, udāhu aññampi kañci mahantaṁ brahantaṁ kāyupapannaṁ jano disvā evamāha: ‘nāgo vata bho nāgo’”ti?
segs.e: ‘A giant, such a giant’? Or do they say it when they see any other creatures with big, formidable bodies?”

segs.p: “Hatthimpi kho, udāyi, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ kāyupapannaṁ jano disvā evamāha:
segs.e: “Udāyī, when they see elephants with such a big, formidable body people say:

segs.p: ‘nāgo vata bho nāgo’ti.
segs.e: ‘A giant, such a giant!’

segs.p: Assampi kho, udāyi, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ …pe…
segs.e: And also when they see a horse with a big, formidable body …

segs.p: goṇampi kho, udāyi, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ …pe…
segs.e: When they see a bull with a big, formidable body …

segs.p: uragampi kho, udāyi, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ …pe…
segs.e: When they see a serpent with a big, formidable body …

segs.p: rukkhampi kho, udāyi, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ …pe…
segs.e: When they see a tree with a big, formidable body …

segs.p: manussampi kho, udāyi, mahantaṁ brahantaṁ kāyupapannaṁ jano disvā evamāha:
segs.e: And when they see a human being with such a big, formidable body people say:

segs.p: ‘nāgo vata, bho, nāgo’ti.
segs.e: ‘A giant, such a giant!’

segs.p: Api ca, udāyi, yo sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya āguṁ na karoti kāyena vācāya manasā, tamahaṁ ‘nāgo’ti brūmī”ti.
segs.e: But Udāyī, one who does nothing monstrous by way of body, speech, and mind is who I call a ‘giant’ in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāva subhāsitañcidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā—
segs.e: How well said this was by the Buddha:

segs.p: api ca, udāyi, yo sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya āguṁ na karoti kāyena vācāya manasā, tamahaṁ ‘nāgo’ti brūmīti.
segs.e: ‘But Udāyī, one who does nothing monstrous by way of body, speech, and mind is who I call a “giant” in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.’

segs.p: Idañca panāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā subhāsitaṁ imāhi gāthāhi anumodāmi—
segs.e: And I celebrate the well-spoken words of the Buddha with these verses:

segs.p: Manussabhūtaṁ sambuddhaṁ,
segs.e: Awakened as a human being,

segs.p: attadantaṁ samāhitaṁ;
segs.e: self-tamed and immersed in samādhi,

segs.p: Iriyamānaṁ brahmapathe,
segs.e: following the spiritual path,

segs.p: cittassūpasame rataṁ.
segs.e: he loves peace of mind.

segs.p: Yaṁ manussā namassanti,
segs.e: Revered by people,

segs.p: sabbadhammāna pāraguṁ;
segs.e: gone beyond all things,

segs.p: Devāpi taṁ namassanti,
segs.e: even the gods revere him;

segs.p: iti me arahato sutaṁ.
segs.e: so I’ve heard from the perfected one.

segs.p: Sabbasaṁyojanātītaṁ,
segs.e: He has transcended all fetters

segs.p: vanā nibbanamāgataṁ;
segs.e: and escaped from entanglements.

segs.p: Kāmehi nekkhammarataṁ,
segs.e: Delighting to renounce sensual pleasures,

segs.p: muttaṁ selāva kañcanaṁ.
segs.e: he’s freed like lustrous gold from stone.

segs.p: Sabbe accarucī nāgo,
segs.e: That giant outshines all,

segs.p: himavāññe siluccaye;
segs.e: like the Himalaya beside other mountains.

segs.p: Sabbesaṁ nāganāmānaṁ,
segs.e: Of all those named ‘giant’,

segs.p: saccanāmo anuttaro.
segs.e: he is truly named, supreme.

segs.p: Nāgaṁ vo kittayissāmi,
segs.e: I shall extol the giant for you,

segs.p: na hi āguṁ karoti so;
segs.e: for he does nothing monstrous.

segs.p: Soraccaṁ avihiṁsā ca,
segs.e: Gentleness and harmlessness

segs.p: pādā nāgassa te duve.
segs.e: are two feet of the giant.

segs.p: Tapo ca brahmacariyaṁ,
segs.e: Fervor and chastity

segs.p: caraṇā nāgassa tyāpare;
segs.e: are his two other feet.

segs.p: Saddhāhattho mahānāgo,
segs.e: Faith is the giant’s trunk,

segs.p: upekkhāsetadantavā.
segs.e: and equanimity his white tusks.

segs.p: Sati gīvā siro paññā,
segs.e: Mindfulness is his neck, his head is wisdom—

segs.p: vīmaṁsā dhammacintanā;
segs.e: inquiry and thinking about principles.

segs.p: Dhammakucchisamātapo,
segs.e: His belly is the sacred hearth of the Dhamma,

segs.p: viveko tassa vāladhi.
segs.e: and his tail is seclusion.

segs.p: So jhāyī assāsarato,
segs.e: Practicing absorption, enjoying the breath,

segs.p: ajjhattaṁ susamāhito;
segs.e: he is serene within.

segs.p: Gacchaṁ samāhito nāgo,
segs.e: The giant is serene when walking,

segs.p: ṭhito nāgo samāhito.
segs.e: the giant is serene when standing,

segs.p: Seyyaṁ samāhito nāgo,
segs.e: the giant is serene when lying down,

segs.p: nisinnopi samāhito;
segs.e: and when sitting, the giant is serene.

segs.p: Sabbattha saṁvuto nāgo,
segs.e: The giant is restrained everywhere:

segs.p: esā nāgassa sampadā.
segs.e: this is the accomplishment of the giant.

segs.p: Bhuñjati anavajjāni,
segs.e: He eats blameless things,

segs.p: sāvajjāni na bhuñjati;
segs.e: he doesn’t eat blameworthy things.

segs.p: Ghāsamacchādanaṁ laddhā,
segs.e: When he gets food and clothes,

segs.p: sannidhiṁ parivajjayaṁ.
segs.e: he avoids storing them up.

segs.p: Saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ thūlaṁ,
segs.e: Having severed all bonds,

segs.p: sabbaṁ chetvāna bandhanaṁ;
segs.e: fetters large and small,

segs.p: Yena yeneva gacchati,
segs.e: wherever he goes,

segs.p: anapekkhova gacchati.
segs.e: he goes without concern.

segs.p: Yathāpi udake jātaṁ,
segs.e: A white lotus,

segs.p: puṇḍarīkaṁ pavaḍḍhati;
segs.e: fragrant and delightful,

segs.p: Nupalippati toyena,
segs.e: sprouts in water and grows there,

segs.p: sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ.
segs.e: but water does not stick to it.

segs.p: Tatheva loke sujāto,
segs.e: Just so the Buddha is born in the world,

segs.p: buddho loke viharati;
segs.e: and lives in the world,

segs.p: Nupalippati lokena,
segs.e: but the world does not stick to him,

segs.p: toyena padumaṁ yathā.
segs.e: as water does not stick to the lotus.

segs.p: Mahāginīva jalito,
segs.e: A great blazing fire

segs.p: anāhārūpasammati;
segs.e: dies down when the fuel runs out.

segs.p: Saṅkhāresūpasantesu,
segs.e: When the coals have gone out

segs.p: nibbutoti pavuccati.
segs.e: it’s said to be ‘quenched’.

segs.p: Atthassāyaṁ viññāpanī,
segs.e: This simile is taught by the discerning

segs.p: upamā viññūhi desitā;
segs.e: to express the meaning clearly.

segs.p: Viññassanti mahānāgā,
segs.e: Great giants will understand

segs.p: nāgaṁ nāgena desitaṁ.
segs.e: what the giant taught the giant.

segs.p: Vītarāgo vītadoso,
segs.e: Free of greed, free of hate,

segs.p: Vītamoho anāsavo;
segs.e: free of delusion, undefiled;

segs.p: Sarīraṁ vijahaṁ nāgo,
segs.e: the giant, giving up his body,

segs.p: Parinibbissati anāsavo”ti.
segs.e: being undefiled, will be fully quenched.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.44
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.44

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Migasālāsutta
segs.e: With Migasālā

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena migasālāya upāsikāya nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the laywoman Migasālā, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho migasālā upāsikā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho migasālā upāsikā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the laywoman Migasālā went up to Ānanda, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “Kathaṁ kathaṁ nāmāyaṁ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāyaṁ?
segs.e: “Honorable Ānanda, how on earth are we supposed to understand the teaching taught by the Buddha, when the chaste and the unchaste are both reborn in exactly the same place in the next life?

segs.p: Pitā me, bhante, purāṇo brahmacārī ahosi ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
segs.e: My father Purāṇa was chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

segs.p: So kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato sakadāgāmī satto tusitaṁ kāyaṁ upapannoti.
segs.e: When he passed away the Buddha declared that, since he was a once-returner, he was reborn in the host of joyful gods.

segs.p: Petteyyopi me, bhante, isidatto abrahmacārī ahosi sadārasantuṭṭho.
segs.e: But my uncle Isidatta was not chaste; he lived content with his wife.

segs.p: Sopi kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato sakadāgāmipatto tusitaṁ kāyaṁ upapannoti.
segs.e: When he passed away the Buddha declared that, since he too was a once-returner, he was reborn in the host of joyful gods.

segs.p: Kathaṁ kathaṁ nāmāyaṁ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāyan”ti?
segs.e: How on earth are we supposed to understand the teaching taught by the Buddha, when the chaste and the unchaste are both reborn in exactly the same place in the next life?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhagini, bhagavatā byākatan”ti.
segs.e: “You’re right, sister, but that’s how the Buddha declared it.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando migasālāya upāsikāya nivesane piṇḍapātaṁ gahetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Ānanda, after receiving almsfood at Migasālā’s home, rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then after the meal, on his return from almsround, Ānanda went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena migasālāya upāsikāya nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṁ.
Atha kho, bhante, migasālā upāsikā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho, bhante, migasālā upāsikā maṁ etadavoca:
‘kathaṁ kathaṁ nāmāyaṁ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāyaṁ.
Pitā me, bhante, purāṇo brahmacārī ahosi ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
So kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato sakadāgāmipatto tusitaṁ kāyaṁ upapannoti.
Petteyyopi me, bhante, isidatto abrahmacārī ahosi sadārasantuṭṭho.
Sopi kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato sakadāgāmipatto tusitaṁ kāyaṁ upapannoti.
Kathaṁ kathaṁ nāmāyaṁ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāyan’ti?
Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, migasālaṁ upāsikaṁ etadavocaṁ:
‘evaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhagini, bhagavatā byākatan’”ti.
“Kā cānanda, migasālā upāsikā bālā abyattā ammakā ammakapaññā, ke ca purisapuggalaparopariyañāṇe?
segs.e: “Ānanda, who is this laywoman Migasālā, a foolish incompetent aunty, with an aunty’s wit? And who is it that knows how to assess individual persons?

segs.p: Chayime, ānanda, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These six individuals are found in the world.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco puggalo sorato hoti sukhasaṁvāso, abhinandanti sabrahmacārī ekattavāsena.
segs.e: Take a certain individual who is gentle and pleasant to be with. And spiritual companions enjoy living together with them.

segs.p: Tassa savanenapi akataṁ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṁ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṁ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ na labhati.
segs.e: And they’ve not listened or learned or penetrated theoretically or found even temporary freedom.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā hānāya pareti no visesāya, hānagāmīyeva hoti no visesagāmī.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they depart for a lower place, not a higher. They’re going to a lower place, not a higher.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo sorato hoti sukhasaṁvāso, abhinandanti sabrahmacārī ekattavāsena.
segs.e: Take another individual who is gentle and pleasant to be with. And spiritual companions enjoy living together with them.

segs.p: Tassa savanenapi kataṁ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṁ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṁ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ labhati.
segs.e: And they’ve listened and learned and penetrated theoretically and found temporary freedom.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā visesāya pareti no hānāya, visesagāmīyeva hoti no hānagāmī.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they depart for a higher place, not a lower. They’re going to a higher place, not a lower.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, pamāṇikā pamiṇanti:
segs.e: Judgmental people compare them, saying:

segs.p: ‘imassapi teva dhammā aparassapi teva dhammā, kasmā tesaṁ eko hīno eko paṇīto’ti.
segs.e: ‘This one has just the same qualities as the other, so why is one worse and one better?’

segs.p: Tañhi tesaṁ, ānanda, hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
segs.e: This will be for their lasting harm and suffering.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, yvāyaṁ puggalo sorato hoti sukhasaṁvāso, abhinandanti sabrahmacārī ekattavāsena, tassa savanenapi kataṁ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṁ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṁ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ labhati.
segs.e: In this case, the individual who is gentle … and has listened, learned, penetrated theoretically, and found temporary freedom

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, puggalo amunā purimena puggalena abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: is better and finer than the other individual.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Imaṁ hānanda, puggalaṁ dhammasoto nibbahati,
segs.e: Because the stream of the teaching carries them along.

segs.p: tadantaraṁ ko jāneyya aññatra tathāgatena.
segs.e: But who knows the difference between them except a Realized One?

segs.p: Tasmātihānanda, mā puggalesu pamāṇikā ahuvattha;
segs.e: So, Ānanda, don’t be judgmental about individuals.

segs.p: mā puggalesu pamāṇaṁ gaṇhittha.
segs.e: Don’t pass judgment on individuals.

segs.p: Khaññati hānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṁ gaṇhanto.
segs.e: Those who pass judgment on individuals harm themselves.

segs.p: Ahaṁ vā, ānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṁ gaṇheyyaṁ, yo vā panassa mādiso.
segs.e: I, or someone like me, may pass judgment on individuals.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekaccassa puggalassa kodhamāno adhigato hoti, samayena samayañcassa lobhadhammā uppajjanti.
segs.e: Take another individual who is angry and conceited, and from time to time has greedy thoughts.

segs.p: Tassa savanenapi akataṁ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṁ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṁ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ na labhati.
segs.e: And they’ve not listened or learned or penetrated theoretically or found even temporary freedom.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā hānāya pareti no visesāya, hānagāmīyeva hoti no visesagāmī.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they depart for a lower place, not a higher. They’re going to a lower place, not a higher.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekaccassa puggalassa kodhamāno adhigato hoti, samayena samayañcassa lobhadhammā uppajjanti.
segs.e: Take another individual who is angry and conceited, and from time to time has greedy thoughts. …

segs.p: Tassa savanenapi kataṁ hoti …pe…
segs.e: Because the stream of the teaching carries them along. …

segs.p: no hānagāmī.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they depart for a higher place, not a lower. They’re going to a higher place, not a lower.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, pamāṇikā pamiṇanti …pe…
segs.e: Judgmental people compare them …

segs.p: yo vā panassa mādiso.
segs.e: I, or someone like me, may pass judgment on people.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekaccassa puggalassa kodhamāno adhigato hoti, samayena samayañcassa vacīsaṅkhārā uppajjanti.
segs.e: Take another individual who is angry and conceited, and from time to time has the impulse to speak inappropriately.

segs.p: Tassa savanenapi akataṁ hoti …pe… sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ na labhati.
segs.e: And they’ve not listened or learned or penetrated theoretically or found even temporary freedom.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā hānāya pareti no visesāya, hānagāmīyeva hoti no visesagāmī.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they depart for a lower place, not a higher. They’re going to a lower place, not a higher.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekaccassa puggalassa kodhamāno adhigato hoti, samayena samayañcassa vacīsaṅkhārā uppajjanti.
segs.e: Take another individual who is angry and conceited, and from time to time has the impulse to speak inappropriately.

segs.p: Tassa savanenapi kataṁ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṁ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṁ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ labhati.
segs.e: But they’ve listened and learned and penetrated theoretically and found temporary freedom.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā visesāya pareti no hānāya, visesagāmīyeva hoti no hānagāmī.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they depart for a higher place, not a lower. They’re going to a higher place, not a lower.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, pamāṇikā pamiṇanti:
segs.e: Judgmental people compare them, saying:

segs.p: ‘imassapi teva dhammā, aparassapi teva dhammā. Kasmā tesaṁ eko hīno, eko paṇīto’ti?
segs.e: ‘This one has just the same qualities as the other, so why is one worse and one better?’

segs.p: Tañhi tesaṁ, ānanda, hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
segs.e: This will be for their lasting harm and suffering.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, yassa puggalassa kodhamāno adhigato hoti, samayena samayañcassa vacīsaṅkhārā uppajjanti, tassa savanenapi kataṁ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṁ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṁ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṁ labhati.
segs.e: In this case, the individual who is angry and conceited, but has listened, learned, penetrated theoretically, and found temporary freedom

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, puggalo amunā purimena puggalena abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: is better and finer than the other individual.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Imaṁ hānanda, puggalaṁ dhammasoto nibbahati.
segs.e: Because the stream of the teaching carries them along.

segs.p: Tadantaraṁ ko jāneyya aññatra tathāgatena.
segs.e: But who knows the difference between them except a Realized One?

segs.p: Tasmātihānanda, mā puggalesu pamāṇikā ahuvattha;
segs.e: So, Ānanda, don’t be judgmental about individuals.

segs.p: mā puggalesu pamāṇaṁ gaṇhittha.
segs.e: Don’t pass judgment on individuals.

segs.p: Khaññati hānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṁ gaṇhanto.
segs.e: Those who pass judgment on individuals harm themselves.

segs.p: Ahaṁ vā, ānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṁ gaṇheyyaṁ, yo vā panassa mādiso.
segs.e: I, or someone like me, may pass judgment on individuals.

segs.p: Kā cānanda, migasālā upāsikā bālā abyattā ammakā ammakapaññā, ke ca purisapuggalaparopariyañāṇe.
segs.e: Who is this laywoman Migasālā, a foolish incompetent aunty, with an aunty’s wit? And who is it that knows how to assess individual persons?

segs.p: Ime kho, ānanda, cha puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These six individuals are found in the world.

segs.p: Yathārūpena, ānanda, sīlena purāṇo samannāgato ahosi, tathārūpena sīlena isidatto samannāgato abhavissa. Nayidha purāṇo isidattassa gatimpi aññassa.
segs.e: If Isidatta had achieved Purāṇa’s level of ethical conduct, Purāṇa could not have even known Isidatta’s destination.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya ca, ānanda, paññāya isidatto samannāgato ahosi, tathārūpāya paññāya purāṇo samannāgato abhavissa. Nayidha isidatto purāṇassa gatimpi aññassa.
segs.e: And if Purāṇa had achieved Isidatta’s level of wisdom, Isidatta could not have even known Purāṇa’s destination.

segs.p: Iti kho, ānanda, ime puggalā ubho ekaṅgahīnā”ti.
segs.e: So both individuals were lacking in one respect.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.45
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.45

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Iṇasutta
segs.e: Debt

segs.p: “Dāliddiyaṁ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, isn’t poverty suffering in the world for a person who enjoys sensual pleasures?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yampi, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko iṇaṁ ādiyati, iṇādānampi, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino”ti?
segs.e: “When a poor, penniless person falls into debt, isn’t being in debt also suffering in the world for a person who enjoys sensual pleasures?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yampi, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko iṇaṁ ādiyitvā vaḍḍhiṁ paṭissuṇāti, vaḍḍhipi, bhikkhave, dukkhā lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino”ti?
segs.e: “When a poor person who has fallen into debt agrees to pay interest, isn’t the interest also suffering in the world for a person who enjoys sensual pleasures?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yampi, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko vaḍḍhiṁ paṭissuṇitvā kālābhataṁ vaḍḍhiṁ na deti, codentipi naṁ;
segs.e: “When a poor person who has fallen into debt and agreed to pay interest fails to pay it when it falls due, they get a warning.

segs.p: codanāpi, bhikkhave, dukkhā lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t being warned suffering in the world for a person who enjoys sensual pleasures?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yampi, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko codiyamāno na deti, anucarantipi naṁ;
segs.e: “When a poor person fails to pay after getting a warning, they’re prosecuted.

segs.p: anucariyāpi, bhikkhave, dukkhā lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t being prosecuted suffering in the world for a person who enjoys sensual pleasures?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yampi, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko anucariyamāno na deti, bandhantipi naṁ;
segs.e: “When a poor person fails to pay after being prosecuted, they’re imprisoned.

segs.p: bandhanampi, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t being imprisoned suffering in the world for a person who enjoys sensual pleasures?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dāliddiyampi dukkhaṁ lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino, iṇādānampi dukkhaṁ lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino, vaḍḍhipi dukkhā lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino, codanāpi dukkhā lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino, anucariyāpi dukkhā lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino, bandhanampi dukkhaṁ lokasmiṁ kāmabhogino;
segs.e: “So mendicants, poverty, debt, interest, warnings, prosecution, and imprisonment are suffering in the world for those who enjoy sensual pleasures.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī natthi kusalesu dhammesu, ottappaṁ natthi kusalesu dhammesu, vīriyaṁ natthi kusalesu dhammesu, paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu—
segs.e: In the same way, whoever has no faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom when it comes to skillful qualities

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye daliddo assako anāḷhiko.
segs.e: is called poor and penniless in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko saddhāya asati kusalesu dhammesu, hiriyā asati kusalesu dhammesu, ottappe asati kusalesu dhammesu, vīriye asati kusalesu dhammesu, paññāya asati kusalesu dhammesu, kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: Since they have no faith, conscience, prudence, energy, or wisdom when it comes to skillful qualities, they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Idamassa iṇādānasmiṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re in debt, I say.

segs.p: So tassa kāyaduccaritassa paṭicchādanahetu pāpikaṁ icchaṁ paṇidahati.
segs.e: In order to conceal the bad things they do by way of body, speech, and mind they harbor corrupt wishes.

segs.p: ‘Mā maṁ jaññū’ti icchati, ‘mā maṁ jaññū’ti saṅkappati, ‘mā maṁ jaññū’ti vācaṁ bhāsati, ‘mā maṁ jaññū’ti kāyena parakkamati. So tassa vacīduccaritassa paṭicchādanahetu …pe… so tassa manoduccaritassa paṭicchādanahetu …pe… ‘mā maṁ jaññū’ti kāyena parakkamati.
segs.e: They wish, plan, speak, and act with the thought: ‘May no one find me out!’

segs.p: Idamassa vaḍḍhiyā vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they pay interest, I say.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ pesalā sabrahmacārī evamāhaṁsu:
segs.e: Good-hearted spiritual companions say this about them:

segs.p: ‘ayañca so āyasmā evaṅkārī evaṁsamācāro’ti.
segs.e: ‘This venerable acts like this, and behaves like that.’

segs.p: Idamassa codanāya vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re warned, I say.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā vippaṭisārasahagatā pāpakā akusalavitakkā samudācaranti.
segs.e: When they go to a wilderness, the root of a tree, or an empty hut, they’re beset by remorseful, unskillful thoughts.

segs.p: Idamassa anucariyāya vadāmi.
segs.e: This is how they’re prosecuted, I say.

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhave, daliddo assako anāḷhiko kāyena duccaritaṁ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṁ caritvā manasā duccaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā nirayabandhane vā bajjhati tiracchānayonibandhane vā.
segs.e: That poor, penniless person has done bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re trapped in the prison of hell or the animal realm.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekabandhanampi samanupassāmi evaṁdāruṇaṁ evaṅkaṭukaṁ evaṁantarāyakaraṁ anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya, yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, nirayabandhanaṁ vā tiracchānayonibandhanaṁ vāti.
segs.e: I don’t see a single prison that’s as grim, as vicious, and such an obstacle to reaching the supreme sanctuary from the yoke as the prison of hell or the animal realm.

segs.p: Dāliddiyaṁ dukkhaṁ loke,
segs.e: Poverty is said to be suffering in the world,

segs.p: iṇādānañca vuccati;
segs.e: and so is being in debt.

segs.p: Daliddo iṇamādāya,
segs.e: A poor person who has fallen into debt

segs.p: bhuñjamāno vihaññati.
segs.e: frets even when spending the loan.

segs.p: Tato anucaranti naṁ,
segs.e: And then they’re prosecuted,

segs.p: bandhanampi nigacchati;
segs.e: or even thrown in jail.

segs.p: Etañhi bandhanaṁ dukkhaṁ,
segs.e: Such imprisonment is true suffering

segs.p: kāmalābhābhijappinaṁ.
segs.e: for someone who prays for pleasure and possessions.

segs.p: Tatheva ariyavinaye,
segs.e: In the same way, in the Noble One’s training

segs.p: saddhā yassa na vijjati;
segs.e: whoever has no faith,

segs.p: Ahirīko anottappī,
segs.e: no conscience or prudence,

segs.p: pāpakammavinibbayo.
segs.e: contemplates bad deeds.

segs.p: Kāyaduccaritaṁ katvā,
segs.e: After doing bad things

segs.p: vacīduccaritāni ca;
segs.e: by way of body,

segs.p: Manoduccaritaṁ katvā,
segs.e: speech, and mind,

segs.p: ‘mā maṁ jaññū’ti icchati.
segs.e: they wish, ‘May no one find me out!’

segs.p: So saṁsappati kāyena,
segs.e: Their behavior is creepy

segs.p: vācāya uda cetasā;
segs.e: by body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Pāpakammaṁ pavaḍḍhento,
segs.e: They pile up bad deeds

segs.p: tattha tattha punappunaṁ.
segs.e: on and on, life after life.

segs.p: So pāpakammo dummedho,
segs.e: That simpleton evildoer,

segs.p: jānaṁ dukkaṭamattano;
segs.e: knowing their own misdeeds,

segs.p: Daliddo iṇamādāya,
segs.e: is a poor person who has fallen into debt,

segs.p: bhuñjamāno vihaññati.
segs.e: and frets even when spending the loan.

segs.p: Tato anucaranti naṁ,
segs.e: And when in village or wilderness

segs.p: saṅkappā mānasā dukhā;
segs.e: they’re prosecuted

segs.p: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe,
segs.e: by painful mental plans,

segs.p: yassa vippaṭisārajā.
segs.e: which are born of remorse.

segs.p: So pāpakammo dummedho,
segs.e: That simpleton evildoer,

segs.p: jānaṁ dukkaṭamattano;
segs.e: knowing their own misdeeds,

segs.p: Yonimaññataraṁ gantvā,
segs.e: goes to one of the animal realms,

segs.p: niraye vāpi bajjhati.
segs.e: or is trapped in hell.

segs.p: Etañhi bandhanaṁ dukkhaṁ,
segs.e: Such imprisonment is true suffering,

segs.p: yamhā dhīro pamuccati;
segs.e: from which the attentive are released.

segs.p: Dhammaladdhehi bhogehi,
segs.e: With confident heart, they give

segs.p: dadaṁ cittaṁ pasādayaṁ.
segs.e: with wealth that is properly earned.

segs.p: Ubhayattha kaṭaggāho,
segs.e: That faithful householder of discernment

segs.p: saddhassa gharamesino;
segs.e: holds a winning hand on both counts:

segs.p: Diṭṭhadhammahitatthāya,
segs.e: welfare and benefit in this life,

segs.p: samparāyasukhāya ca;
segs.e: and happiness in lives to come.

segs.p: Evametaṁ gahaṭṭhānaṁ,
segs.e: This is how, for a householder,

segs.p: cāgo puññaṁ pavaḍḍhati.
segs.e: merit grows by generosity.

segs.p: Tatheva ariyavinaye,
segs.e: In the same way, in the Noble One’s training,

segs.p: saddhā yassa patiṭṭhitā;
segs.e: whoever is grounded in faith,

segs.p: Hirīmano ca ottappī,
segs.e: with conscience and prudence,

segs.p: paññavā sīlasaṁvuto.
segs.e: wise, and ethically restrained,

segs.p: Eso kho ariyavinaye,
segs.e: is said to live happily

segs.p: ‘sukhajīvī’ti vuccati;
segs.e: in the Noble One’s training.

segs.p: Nirāmisaṁ sukhaṁ laddhā,
segs.e: After gaining pleasure not of the flesh,

segs.p: upekkhaṁ adhitiṭṭhati.
segs.e: they concentrate on equanimity.

segs.p: Pañca nīvaraṇe hitvā,
segs.e: They give up the five hindrances,

segs.p: niccaṁ āraddhavīriyo;
segs.e: constantly energetic,

segs.p: Jhānāni upasampajja,
segs.e: and enter the absorptions,

segs.p: ekodi nipako sato.
segs.e: unified, alert, and mindful.

segs.p: Evaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ,
segs.e: Truly knowing in this way

segs.p: sabbasaṁyojanakkhaye;
segs.e: regards the ending of all fetters,

segs.p: Sabbaso anupādāya,
segs.e: by not grasping in any way,

segs.p: sammā cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: their mind is rightly freed.

segs.p: Tassa sammā vimuttassa,
segs.e: To that unaffected one, rightly freed

segs.p: ñāṇañce hoti tādino;
segs.e: with the end of the fetters of continued existence,

segs.p: ‘Akuppā me vimuttī’ti,
segs.e: the knowledge comes:

segs.p: bhavasaṁyojanakkhaye.
segs.e: ‘My freedom is unshakable.’

segs.p: Etaṁ kho paramaṁ ñāṇaṁ,
segs.e: This is the ultimate knowledge.

segs.p: etaṁ sukhamanuttaraṁ;
segs.e: This is the supreme happiness.

segs.p: Asokaṁ virajaṁ khemaṁ,
segs.e: Sorrowless, stainless, secure:

segs.p: etaṁ ānaṇyamuttaman”ti.
segs.e: this is the highest freedom from debt.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.46
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.46

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Mahācundasutta
segs.e: By Mahācunda

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahācundo cetīsu viharati sayaṁjātiyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahācunda was staying in the land of the Cetis at Sahajāti.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā mahācundo bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There he addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “āvuso bhikkhave”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahācundassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Āyasmā mahācundo etadavoca:
segs.e: Venerable Mahācunda said this:

segs.p: “Idhāvuso, dhammayogā bhikkhū jhāyī bhikkhū apasādenti:
segs.e: “Take a case where mendicants who practice discernment of principles rebuke mendicants who practice absorption:

segs.p: ‘ime pana jhāyinomhā, jhāyinomhāti jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti avajjhāyanti.
segs.e: ‘They say, “We practice absorption meditation! We practice absorption meditation!” And they meditate and concentrate and contemplate and ruminate.

segs.p: Kimime jhāyanti, kintime jhāyanti, kathaṁ ime jhāyantī’ti?
segs.e: Why do they practice absorption meditation? In what way do they practice absorption meditation? How do they practice absorption meditation?’

segs.p: Tattha dhammayogā ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, jhāyī ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, na ca bahujanahitāya paṭipannā honti bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: In this case the mendicants who practice discernment of principles are not inspired, and the mendicants who practice absorption are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, jhāyī bhikkhū dhammayoge bhikkhū apasādenti:
segs.e: Now, take a case where mendicants who practice absorption meditation rebuke mendicants who practice discernment of principles:

segs.p: ‘ime pana dhammayogamhā, dhammayogamhāti uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā pākatindriyā.
segs.e: ‘They say, “We practice discernment of principles! We practice discernment of principles!” But they’re haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

segs.p: Kimime dhammayogā, kintime dhammayogā, kathaṁ ime dhammayogā’ti?
segs.e: Why do they practice discernment of principles? In what way do they practice discernment of principles? How do they practice discernment of principles?’

segs.p: Tattha jhāyī ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, dhammayogā ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, na ca bahujanahitāya paṭipannā honti bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: In this case the mendicants who practice absorption are not inspired, and the mendicants who practice discernment of principles are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, dhammayogā bhikkhū dhammayogānaññeva bhikkhūnaṁ vaṇṇaṁ bhāsanti, no jhāyīnaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ vaṇṇaṁ bhāsanti.
segs.e: Now, take a case where mendicants who practice discernment of principles praise only others like them, not mendicants who practice absorption.

segs.p: Tattha dhammayogā ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, jhāyī ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, na ca bahujanahitāya paṭipannā honti bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: In this case the mendicants who practice discernment of principles are not inspired, and the mendicants who practice absorption are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, jhāyī bhikkhū jhāyīnaññeva bhikkhūnaṁ vaṇṇaṁ bhāsanti, no dhammayogānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ vaṇṇaṁ bhāsanti.
segs.e: And take a case where mendicants who practice absorption praise only others like them, not mendicants who practice discernment of principles.

segs.p: Tattha jhāyī ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, dhammayogā ca bhikkhū nappasīdanti, na ca bahujanahitāya paṭipannā honti bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: In this case the mendicants who practice absorption are not inspired, and the mendicants who practice discernment of principles are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Tasmātihāvuso, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘dhammayogā samānā jhāyīnaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ vaṇṇaṁ bhāsissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘As mendicants who practice discernment of principles, we will praise mendicants who practice absorption.’

segs.p: Evañhi vo, āvuso, sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Acchariyā hete, āvuso, puggalā dullabhā lokasmiṁ, ye amataṁ dhātuṁ kāyena phusitvā viharanti.
segs.e: Because it’s rare to find such incredible individuals in the world who have direct meditative experience of the element free of death.

segs.p: Tasmātihāvuso, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘jhāyī samānā dhammayogānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ vaṇṇaṁ bhāsissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘As mendicants who practice absorption, we will praise mendicants who practice discernment of principles.’

segs.p: Evañhi vo, āvuso, sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Acchariyā hete, āvuso, puggalā dullabhā lokasmiṁ ye gambhīraṁ atthapadaṁ paññāya ativijjha passantī”ti.
segs.e: Because it’s incredibly rare to find individuals in the world who see the meaning of a deep saying with penetrating wisdom.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.47
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.47

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Paṭhamasandiṭṭhikasutta
segs.e: Apparent in the Present Life (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho moḷiyasīvako paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: And then the wanderer Moḷiyasīvaka went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho moḷiyasīvako paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “‘sandiṭṭhiko dhammo, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati.
segs.e: “Sir, they speak of ‘a teaching apparent in the present life’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti?
segs.e: In what way is the teaching apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, sīvaka, taññevettha paṭipucchāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
segs.e: “Well then, Sīvaka, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, sīvaka,
segs.e: What do you think, Sīvaka?

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ lobhaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ lobho’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ lobhaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ lobho’ti pajānāsī”ti?
segs.e: When there’s greed in you, do you understand ‘I have greed in me’? And when there’s no greed in you, do you understand ‘I have no greed in me’?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho tvaṁ, sīvaka, santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ lobhaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ lobho’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ lobhaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ lobho’ti pajānāsi—
segs.e: “Since you know this,

segs.p: evampi kho, sīvaka, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti …pe….
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, sīvaka,
segs.e: What do you think, Sīvaka?

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ dosaṁ …pe…
segs.e: When there’s hate …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ mohaṁ …pe…
segs.e: delusion …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ lobhadhammaṁ …pe…
segs.e: greedy ideas …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ dosadhammaṁ …pe…
segs.e: hateful ideas …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ mohadhammaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ mohadhammo’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ mohadhammaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ mohadhammo’ti pajānāsī”ti?
segs.e: When there are delusional ideas in you, do you understand ‘I have delusional ideas in me’? And when there are no delusional ideas in you, do you understand ‘I have no delusional ideas in me’?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho tvaṁ, sīvaka, santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ mohadhammaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ mohadhammo’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ mohadhammaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ mohadhammo’ti pajānāsi—
segs.e: “Since you know this,

segs.p: evaṁ kho, sīvaka, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.48
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.48

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Dutiyasandiṭṭhikasutta
segs.e: Apparent in the Present Life (2nd)

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “‘sandiṭṭhiko dhammo, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo’ti, bho gotama, vuccati.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, they speak of ‘a teaching apparent in the present life’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bho gotama, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti?
segs.e: In what way is the teaching apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, brāhmaṇa,
segs.e: What do you think, brahmin?

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgo’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgo’ti pajānāsī”ti?
segs.e: When there’s greed in you, do you understand ‘I have greed in me’? And when there’s no greed in you, do you understand ‘I have no greed in me’?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgo’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ rāgaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ rāgo’ti pajānāsi—
segs.e: “Since you know this,
