segs.p: evampi kho, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti …pe….
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, brāhmaṇa,
segs.e: What do you think, brahmin?

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ dosaṁ …pe…
segs.e: When there’s hate …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ mohaṁ …pe…
segs.e: delusion …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ kāyasandosaṁ …pe…
segs.e: corruption that leads to physical deeds …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vacīsandosaṁ …pe…
segs.e: corruption that leads to speech …

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ manosandosaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ manosandoso’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ manosandosaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ manosandoso’ti pajānāsī”ti?
segs.e: When there’s corruption that leads to mental deeds in you, do you understand ‘I have corruption that leads to mental deeds in me’? And when there’s no corruption that leads to mental deeds in you, do you understand ‘I have no corruption that leads to mental deeds in me’?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ manosandosaṁ ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ manosandoso’ti pajānāsi, asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ manosandosaṁ ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ manosandoso’ti pajānāsi—
segs.e: “Since you know this,

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhiko dhammo hoti akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.
segs.e: this is how the teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.49
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.49

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Khemasutta
segs.e: With Khema

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca khemo āyasmā ca sumano sāvatthiyaṁ viharanti andhavanasmiṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Khema and Venerable Sumana were staying near Sāvatthī in the Dark Forest.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ca khemo āyasmā ca sumano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā khemo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then they went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Venerable Khema said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Yo so, bhante, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto tassa na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “Sir, a mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—does not think:

segs.p: ‘atthi me seyyoti vā atthi me sadisoti vā atthi me hīnoti vā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘There is someone better than me, or equal to me, or worse than me.’”

segs.p: Idamavocāyasmā khemo.
segs.e: That is what Khema said,

segs.p: Samanuñño satthā ahosi.
segs.e: and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā khemo “samanuñño me satthā”ti uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Khema, knowing that the Teacher concurred, got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sumano acirapakkante āyasmante kheme bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then, not long after Khema had left, Sumana said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “yo so, bhante, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto tassa na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “Sir, a mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—does not think:

segs.p: ‘natthi me seyyoti vā natthi me sadisoti vā natthi me hīnoti vā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘There is no one better than me, or equal to me, or worse than me.’”

segs.p: Idamavocāyasmā sumano.
segs.e: That is what Sumana said,

segs.p: Samanuñño satthā ahosi.
segs.e: and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sumano “samanuñño me satthā”ti uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Sumana, knowing that the Teacher concurred, got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu āyasmante ca kheme āyasmante ca sumane bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, not long after Khema and Sumana had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, kulaputtā aññaṁ byākaronti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, this is how gentlemen declare enlightenment.

segs.p: Attho ca vutto attā ca anupanīto.
segs.e: The goal is spoken of, but the self is not involved.

segs.p: Atha ca pana idhekacce moghapurisā hasamānakā maññe aññaṁ byākaronti.
segs.e: But it seems that there are some futile men here who declare enlightenment as a joke.

segs.p: Te pacchā vighātaṁ āpajjantīti.
segs.e: Later they will fall into distress.

segs.p: Na ussesu na omesu,
segs.e: They don’t represent themselves

segs.p: Samatte nopanīyare;
segs.e: as being among superiors, inferiors, or equals.

segs.p: Khīṇā jāti vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ,
segs.e: Rebirth is ended, <j>the spiritual journey has been completed.

segs.p: Caranti saṁyojanavippamuttā”ti.
segs.e: They live freed from fetters.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.50
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.50

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Indriyasaṁvarasutta
segs.e: Sense Restraint

segs.p: “Indriyasaṁvare, bhikkhave, asati indriyasaṁvaravipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti sīlaṁ;
segs.e: “Mendicants, when there is no sense restraint, one who lacks sense restraint has destroyed a vital condition for ethical conduct.

segs.p: sīle asati sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: When there is no ethical conduct, one who lacks ethics has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi asati sammāsamādhivipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane asati yathābhūtañāṇadassanavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge asati nibbidāvirāgavipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is no disillusionment and dispassion, one who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho sākhāpalāsavipanno.
segs.e: Suppose there was a tree that lacked branches and foliage.

segs.p: Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi na pāripūriṁ gacchati, pheggupi na pāripūriṁ gacchati, sāropi na pāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would not grow to fullness.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, indriyasaṁvare asati indriyasaṁvaravipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti sīlaṁ …pe…
segs.e: In the same way, when there is no sense restraint, one who lacks sense restraint has destroyed a vital condition for ethical conduct. …

segs.p: vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: One who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Indriyasaṁvare, bhikkhave, sati indriyasaṁvarasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti sīlaṁ;
segs.e: When there is sense restraint, one who has fulfilled sense restraint has fulfilled a vital condition for ethical conduct.

segs.p: sīle sati sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: When there is ethical conduct, one who has fulfilled ethical conduct has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi sati sammāsamādhisampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane sati yathābhūtañāṇadassanasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge sati nibbidāvirāgasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is disillusionment and dispassion, one who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho sākhāpalāsasampanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi pāripūriṁ gacchati, pheggupi pāripūriṁ gacchati, sāropi pāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Suppose there was a tree that was complete with branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would all grow to fullness.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, indriyasaṁvare sati indriyasaṁvarasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti sīlaṁ …pe…
segs.e: In the same way, when there is sense restraint, one who has fulfilled sense restraint has fulfilled a vital condition for ethical conduct. …

segs.p: vimuttiñāṇadassanan”ti.
segs.e: One who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.51
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.51

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Ānandasutta
segs.e: With Ānanda

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Ānanda sat down to one side, and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu assutañceva dhammaṁ suṇāti, sutā cassa dhammā na sammosaṁ gacchanti, ye cassa dhammā pubbe cetasā samphuṭṭhapubbā te ca samudācaranti, aviññātañca vijānātī”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, how does a mendicant get to hear a teaching they haven’t heard before? How do they remember those teachings they have heard? How do they keep exercising the teachings with which they are already familiar? And how do they come to understand what they haven’t understood before?”

segs.p: “Āyasmā kho ānando bahussuto.
segs.e: “Well, Venerable Ānanda, you’re very learned.

segs.p: Paṭibhātu āyasmantaṁyeva ānandan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t you clarify this yourself?”

segs.p: “Tenahāvuso sāriputta, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, Reverend Sāriputta, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Sāriputta replied.

segs.p: Āyasmā ānando etadavoca:
segs.e: Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ geyyaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ gāthaṁ udānaṁ itivuttakaṁ jātakaṁ abbhutadhammaṁ vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: So yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti, yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ vāceti, yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti, yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
segs.e: Then, just as they learned and memorized it, they teach others in detail, make them recite in detail, they rehearse it themselves in detail, and they think about and consider the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ āvāse therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā tasmiṁ āvāse vassaṁ upeti.
segs.e: They enter the rains retreat in a monastery with senior mendicants who are very learned, inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines.

segs.p: Te kālena kālaṁ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati paripañhati:
segs.e: From time to time they go up to those mendicants and ask them questions:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ, bhante, kathaṁ; imassa kvattho’ti?
segs.e: ‘Why, sir, does it say this? What does that mean?’

segs.p: Te tassa āyasmato avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodenti.
segs.e: Those venerables reveal what is hidden, clarify what is unclear, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu assutañceva dhammaṁ suṇāti, sutā cassa dhammā na sammosaṁ gacchanti, ye cassa dhammā pubbe cetasā samphuṭṭhapubbā te ca samudācaranti, aviññātañca vijānātī”ti.
segs.e: This is how a mendicant gets to hear a teaching they haven’t heard before. It’s how they remember those teachings they have heard. It’s how they keep exercising the teachings with which they are already familiar. And it’s how they come to understand what they haven’t understood before.”

segs.p: “Acchariyaṁ, āvuso, abbhutaṁ, āvuso, yāva subhāsitañcidaṁ āyasmatā ānandena.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, reverend, it’s amazing! How well said this was by Venerable Ānanda!

segs.p: Imehi ca mayaṁ chahi dhammehi samannāgataṁ āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ dhārema.
segs.e: And we will remember Venerable Ānanda as someone who possesses these six qualities.

segs.p: Āyasmā hi ānando dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: For Ānanda memorizes the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ geyyaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ gāthaṁ udānaṁ itivuttakaṁ jātakaṁ abbhutadhammaṁ vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Āyasmā ānando yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti, āyasmā ānando yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ vāceti, āyasmā ānando yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti, āyasmā ānando yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
Āyasmā ānando yasmiṁ āvāse therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā tasmiṁ āvāse vassaṁ upeti.
Te āyasmā ānando kālena kālaṁ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati paripañhati:
‘idaṁ, bhante, kathaṁ; imassa kvattho’ti?
Te āyasmato ānandassa avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodentī”ti.
segs.e: Those venerables reveal to Ānanda what is hidden, clarify what is unclear, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.52
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.52

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Khattiyasutta
segs.e: Aristocrats

segs.p: Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: And then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Khattiyā, bho gotama, kiṁadhippāyā, kiṁupavicārā, kiṁadhiṭṭhānā, kiṁabhinivesā, kiṁpariyosānā”ti?
segs.e: “Aristocrats, worthy Gotama, have what as their ambition? What is their preoccupation? What are they fixated on? What do they insist on? What is their ultimate goal?”

segs.p: “Khattiyā kho, brāhmaṇa, bhogādhippāyā paññūpavicārā balādhiṭṭhānā pathavībhinivesā issariyapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: “Aristocrats, brahmin, have wealth as their ambition. They’re preoccupied with wisdom. They’re fixated on power. They insist on territory. Their ultimate goal is authority.”

segs.p: “Brāhmaṇā pana, bho gotama, kiṁadhippāyā, kiṁupavicārā, kiṁadhiṭṭhānā, kiṁabhinivesā, kiṁpariyosānā”ti?
segs.e: “Brahmins, worthy Gotama, have what as their ambition? What is their preoccupation? What are they fixated on? What do they insist on? What is their ultimate goal?”

segs.p: “Brāhmaṇā kho, brāhmaṇa, bhogādhippāyā paññūpavicārā mantādhiṭṭhānā yaññābhinivesā brahmalokapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: “Brahmins have wealth as their ambition. They’re preoccupied with wisdom. They’re fixated on the hymns. They insist on sacrifice. Their ultimate goal is the realm of divinity.”

segs.p: “Gahapatikā pana, bho gotama, kiṁadhippāyā, kiṁupavicārā, kiṁadhiṭṭhānā, kiṁabhinivesā, kiṁpariyosānā”ti?
segs.e: “Householders, worthy Gotama, have what as their ambition? What is their preoccupation? What are they fixated on? What do they insist on? What is their ultimate goal?”

segs.p: “Gahapatikā kho, brāhmaṇa, bhogādhippāyā paññūpavicārā sippādhiṭṭhānā kammantābhinivesā niṭṭhitakammantapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: “Householders have wealth as their ambition. They’re preoccupied with wisdom. They’re fixated on their profession. They insist on work. Their ultimate goal is to complete their work.”

segs.p: “Itthī pana, bho gotama, kiṁadhippāyā, kiṁupavicārā, kiṁadhiṭṭhānā, kiṁabhinivesā, kiṁpariyosānā”ti?
segs.e: “Women, worthy Gotama, have what as their ambition? What is their preoccupation? What are they fixated on? What do they insist on? What is their ultimate goal?”

segs.p: “Itthī kho, brāhmaṇa, purisādhippāyā alaṅkārūpavicārā puttādhiṭṭhānā asapattībhinivesā issariyapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: “Women have a man as their ambition. They’re preoccupied with adornments. They’re fixated on their children. They insist on being without a co-wife. Their ultimate goal is authority.”

segs.p: “Corā pana, bho gotama, kiṁadhippāyā, kiṁupavicārā, kiṁadhiṭṭhānā, kiṁabhinivesā, kiṁpariyosānā”ti?
segs.e: “Bandits, worthy Gotama, have what as their ambition? What is their preoccupation? What are they fixated on? What do they insist on? What is their ultimate goal?”

segs.p: “Corā kho, brāhmaṇa, ādānādhippāyā gahanūpavicārā satthādhiṭṭhānā andhakārābhinivesā adassanapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: “Bandits have theft as their ambition. They’re preoccupied with a hiding place. They’re fixated on their sword. They insist on darkness. Their ultimate goal is invisibility.”

segs.p: “Samaṇā pana, bho gotama, kiṁadhippāyā, kiṁupavicārā, kiṁadhiṭṭhānā, kiṁabhinivesā, kiṁpariyosānā”ti?
segs.e: “Ascetics, worthy Gotama, have what as their ambition? What is their preoccupation? What are they fixated on? What do they insist on? What is their ultimate goal?”

segs.p: “Samaṇā kho, brāhmaṇa, khantisoraccādhippāyā paññūpavicārā sīlādhiṭṭhānā ākiñcaññābhinivesā nibbānapariyosānā”ti.
segs.e: “Ascetics have patience and gentleness as their ambition. They’re preoccupied with wisdom. They’re fixated on ethical conduct. They insist on owning nothing. Their culmination is extinguishment.”

segs.p: “Acchariyaṁ, bho gotama, abbhutaṁ, bho gotama.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, worthy Gotama, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Khattiyānampi bhavaṁ gotamo jānāti adhippāyañca upavicārañca adhiṭṭhānañca abhinivesañca pariyosānañca. Brāhmaṇānampi bhavaṁ gotamo jānāti …pe… gahapatīnampi bhavaṁ gotamo jānāti … itthīnampi bhavaṁ gotamo jānāti … corānampi bhavaṁ gotamo jānāti … samaṇānampi bhavaṁ gotamo jānāti adhippāyañca upavicārañca adhiṭṭhānañca abhinivesañca pariyosānañca.
segs.e: The worthy Gotama knows the ambition, preoccupation, fixation, insistence, and ultimate goal of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, women, bandits, and ascetics.

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe…
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.53
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.53

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Appamādasutta
segs.e: Diligence

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Atthi nu kho, bho gotama, eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato yo ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ, yo ca attho samparāyiko”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, is there one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures benefits for both this life and lives to come?”

segs.p: “Atthi kho, brāhmaṇa, eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato yo ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ, yo ca attho samparāyiko”ti.
segs.e: “There is, brahmin.”

segs.p: “Katamo pana, bho gotama, eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato yo ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ, yo ca attho samparāyiko”ti?
segs.e: “So what is it?”

segs.p: “Appamādo kho, brāhmaṇa, eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ, yo ca attho samparāyiko.
segs.e: “Diligence, brahmin, is one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures benefits for both this life and lives to come.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, yāni kānici jaṅgalānaṁ pāṇānaṁ padajātāni, sabbāni tāni hatthipade samodhānaṁ gacchanti; hatthipadaṁ tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṁ mahantattena.
segs.e: The footprints of all creatures that walk can fit inside an elephant’s footprint. So an elephant’s footprint is said to be the biggest of them all.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, appamādo eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ, yo ca attho samparāyiko.
segs.e: In the same way, diligence is one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures benefits for both this life and lives to come.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo sabbā tā kūṭaṅgamā kūṭaninnā kūṭasamosaraṇā, kūṭaṁ tāsaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: The rafters of a bungalow all lean to the peak, slope to the peak, and meet at the peak, so the peak is said to be the topmost of them all.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, diligence is one thing …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, pabbajalāyako pabbajaṁ lāyitvā agge gahetvā odhunāti nidhunāti nicchādeti;
segs.e: A reed-cutter, having cut the reeds, grabs them at the top and shakes them down, shakes them about, and shakes them off.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, diligence is one thing …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, ambapiṇḍiyā vaṇṭacchinnāya yāni kānici ambāni vaṇṭūpanibandhanāni sabbāni tāni tadanvayāni bhavanti;
segs.e: When the stalk of a bunch of mangoes is cut, all the mangoes attached to the stalk will follow along.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, diligence is one thing …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, ye keci khuddarājāno sabbete rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā bhavanti, rājā tesaṁ cakkavattī aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: All lesser rulers are vassals of a wheel-turning monarch, so the wheel-turning monarch is said to be the foremost of them all.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, diligence is one thing …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, yā kāci tārakarūpānaṁ pabhā sabbā tā candassa pabhāya kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ, candappabhā tāsaṁ aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: The radiance of all the stars is not worth a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance, so the moon’s radiance is said to be the best of them all.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, appamādo eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ yo ca attho samparāyiko.
segs.e: In the same way, diligence is one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures benefits for both this life and lives to come.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, eko dhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ubho atthe samadhiggayha tiṭṭhati—diṭṭhadhammikañceva atthaṁ, yo ca attho samparāyiko”ti.
segs.e: This is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures benefits for both this life and lives to come.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.54
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.54

segs.p: 5. Dhammikavagga
segs.e: 5. About Dhammika

segs.p: Dhammikasutta
segs.e: About Dhammika

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā dhammiko jātibhūmiyaṁ āvāsiko hoti sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattasu āvāsesu.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Dhammika was a resident in all seven monasteries of his native land.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ āyasmā dhammiko āgantuke bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati vihiṁsati vitudati roseti vācāya.
segs.e: There he abused visiting mendicants; he insulted, harmed, attacked, and harassed them.

segs.p: Te ca āgantukā bhikkhū āyasmatā dhammikena akkosiyamānā paribhāsiyamānā vihesiyamānā vitudiyamānā rosiyamānā vācāya pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
segs.e: The visiting mendicants who were treated in this way did not stay. They left, abandoning the monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho jātibhūmakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the local lay followers thought to themselves,

segs.p: “mayaṁ kho bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhitā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena.
segs.e: “We have supplied the mendicant Saṅgha with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Atha ca pana āgantukā bhikkhū pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
segs.e: But the visiting mendicants don’t stay. They leave, abandoning the monastery.

segs.p: Ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo yena āgantukā bhikkhū pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsan”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, what is the reason for this?”

segs.p: Atha kho jātibhūmakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the local lay followers thought to themselves,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho āyasmā dhammiko āgantuke bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati vihiṁsati vitudati roseti vācāya.
segs.e: “This Venerable Dhammika abuses visiting mendicants; he insults, harms, attacks, and harasses them.

segs.p: Te ca āgantukā bhikkhū āyasmatā dhammikena akkosiyamānā paribhāsiyamānā vihesiyamānā vitudiyamānā rosiyamānā vācāya pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
segs.e: The visiting mendicants who were treated in this way do not stay. They leave, abandoning the monastery.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ pabbājeyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we banish Venerable Dhammika?”

segs.p: Atha kho jātibhūmakā upāsakā yena āyasmā dhammiko tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then the local lay followers went up to Venerable Dhammika and said to him,

segs.p: “pakkamatu, bhante, āyasmā dhammiko imamhā āvāsā;
segs.e: “Sir, please leave this monastery.

segs.p: alaṁ te idha vāsenā”ti.
segs.e: You’ve stayed here long enough.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā dhammiko tamhā āvāsā aññaṁ āvāsaṁ agamāsi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Dhammika left and went to another monastery.

segs.p: Tatrapi sudaṁ āyasmā dhammiko āgantuke bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati vihiṁsati vitudati roseti vācāya.
segs.e: There he abused visiting mendicants; he insulted, harmed, attacked, and harassed them.

segs.p: Te ca āgantukā bhikkhū āyasmatā dhammikena akkosiyamānā paribhāsiyamānā vihesiyamānā vitudiyamānā rosiyamānā vācāya pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
segs.e: The visiting mendicants who were treated in this way did not stay. They left, abandoning the monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho jātibhūmakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the local lay followers thought to themselves: …

segs.p: “mayaṁ kho bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhitā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena.
Atha ca pana āgantukā bhikkhū pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
Ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo yena āgantukā bhikkhū pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsan”ti?
Atha kho jātibhūmakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ etadahosi:
“ayaṁ kho āyasmā dhammiko āgantuke bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati vihiṁsati vitudati roseti vācāya.
Te ca āgantukā bhikkhū āyasmatā dhammikena akkosiyamānā paribhāsiyamānā vihesiyamānā vitudiyamānā rosiyamānā vācāya pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ pabbājeyyāmā”ti.
Atha kho jātibhūmakā upāsakā yenāyasmā dhammiko tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: They said to Venerable Dhammika,

segs.p: “pakkamatu, bhante, āyasmā dhammiko imamhāpi āvāsā;
segs.e: “Sir, please leave this monastery.

segs.p: alaṁ te idha vāsenā”ti.
segs.e: You’ve stayed here long enough.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā dhammiko tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṁ āvāsaṁ agamāsi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Dhammika left and went to another monastery.

segs.p: Tatrapi sudaṁ āyasmā dhammiko āgantuke bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati vihiṁsati vitudati roseti vācāya.
segs.e: There he abused visiting mendicants; he insulted, harmed, attacked, and harassed them.

segs.p: Te ca āgantukā bhikkhū āyasmatā dhammikena akkosiyamānā paribhāsiyamānā vihesiyamānā vitudiyamānā rosiyamānā vācāya pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
segs.e: The visiting mendicants who were treated in this way did not stay. They left, abandoning the monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho jātibhūmakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the local lay followers thought to themselves,

segs.p: “mayaṁ kho bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhitā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena.
Atha ca pana āgantukā bhikkhū pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsaṁ.
Ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo yena āgantukā bhikkhū pakkamanti, na saṇṭhanti, riñcanti āvāsan”ti?
Atha kho jātibhūmakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ etadahosi: “ayaṁ kho āyasmā dhammiko āgantuke bhikkhū akkosati …pe….
Yannūna mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ pabbājeyyāma sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattahi āvāsehī”ti.
segs.e: “Why don’t we banish Venerable Dhammika from all seven monasteries in our native land?”

segs.p: Atha kho jātibhūmakā upāsakā yenāyasmā dhammiko tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then the local lay followers went up to Venerable Dhammika and said to him,

segs.p: “pakkamatu, bhante, āyasmā dhammiko sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattahi āvāsehī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, please leave all seven monasteries in our native land.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato dhammikassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Venerable Dhammika thought,

segs.p: “pabbājito khomhi jātibhūmakehi upāsakehi sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattahi āvāsehi.
segs.e: “I’ve been banished by the local lay followers from all seven monasteries in my native land.

segs.p: Kahaṁ nu kho dāni gacchāmī”ti?
segs.e: Where am I to go now?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato dhammikassa etadahosi:
segs.e: He thought,

segs.p: “yannūnāhaṁ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Why don’t I go to see the Buddha?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā dhammiko pattacīvaramādāya yena rājagahaṁ tena pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Dhammika took his bowl and robe and set out for Rājagaha.

segs.p: Anupubbena yena rājagahaṁ gijjhakūṭo pabbato yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ dhammikaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Eventually he came to Rājagaha and the Vulture’s Peak. He went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, āgacchasī”ti?
segs.e: “So, Brahmin Dhammika, where have you come from?”

segs.p: “Pabbājito ahaṁ, bhante, jātibhūmakehi upāsakehi sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattahi āvāsehī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I’ve been banished by the local lay followers from all seven monasteries in my native land.”

segs.p: “Alaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, kiṁ te iminā, yaṁ taṁ tato tato pabbājenti, so tvaṁ tato tato pabbājito mameva santike āgacchasi.
segs.e: “Enough, Brahmin Dhammika, what’s that to you? Now that you’ve been banished from all of those places, you have come to me.

segs.p: Bhūtapubbaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sāmuddikā vāṇijā tīradassiṁ sakuṇaṁ gahetvā nāvāya samuddaṁ ajjhogāhanti.
segs.e: Once upon a time, some sea-merchants set sail for the ocean deeps, taking with them a land-spotting bird.

segs.p: Te atīradakkhiṇiyā nāvāya tīradassiṁ sakuṇaṁ muñcanti.
segs.e: When their ship was out of sight of land, they released the bird.

segs.p: So gacchateva puratthimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati pacchimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uttaraṁ disaṁ, gacchati dakkhiṇaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uddhaṁ, gacchati anudisaṁ.
segs.e: It flew right away to the east, the west, the north, the south, upwards, and in-between.

segs.p: Sace so samantā tīraṁ passati, tathāgatakova hoti.
segs.e: If it saw land on any side, it went there and stayed.

segs.p: Sace pana so samantā tīraṁ na passati tameva nāvaṁ paccāgacchati.
segs.e: But if it saw no land on any side it returned to the ship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, yaṁ taṁ tato tato pabbājenti so tvaṁ tato tato pabbājito mameva santike āgacchasi.
segs.e: In the same way, now that you’ve been banished from all of those places, you have come to me.

segs.p: Bhūtapubbaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, rañño korabyassa suppatiṭṭho nāma nigrodharājā ahosi pañcasākho sītacchāyo manoramo.
segs.e: Once upon a time, King Koravya had a royal banyan tree with five trunks called ‘Well Planted’. It was shady and lovely.

segs.p: Suppatiṭṭhassa kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, nigrodharājassa dvādasayojanāni abhiniveso ahosi, pañca yojanāni mūlasantānakānaṁ.
segs.e: Its canopy spread over twelve leagues, while the network of roots spread for five leagues.

segs.p: Suppatiṭṭhassa kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, nigrodharājassa tāva mahantāni phalāni ahesuṁ;
segs.e: Its fruits were as large as

segs.p: seyyathāpi nāma āḷhakathālikā.
segs.e: a rice pot.

segs.p: Evamassa sādūni phalāni ahesuṁ;
segs.e: And they were as sweet as

segs.p: seyyathāpi nāma khuddaṁ madhuṁ anelakaṁ.
segs.e: pure wild honey.

segs.p: Suppatiṭṭhassa kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, nigrodharājassa ekaṁ khandhaṁ rājā paribhuñjati saddhiṁ itthāgārena, ekaṁ khandhaṁ balakāyo paribhuñjati, ekaṁ khandhaṁ negamajānapadā paribhuñjanti, ekaṁ khandhaṁ samaṇabrāhmaṇā paribhuñjanti, ekaṁ khandhaṁ migā paribhuñjanti.
segs.e: The king and harem made use of one trunk, the troops another, the people of town and country another, ascetics and brahmins another, and beasts and birds another.

segs.p: Suppatiṭṭhassa kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, nigrodharājassa na koci phalāni rakkhati, na ca sudaṁ aññamaññassa phalāni hiṁsanti.
segs.e: No one guarded the fruit, yet no one damaged another’s fruits.

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, aññataro puriso suppatiṭṭhassa nigrodharājassa yāvadatthaṁ phalāni bhakkhitvā sākhaṁ bhañjitvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then a certain person ate as much as he liked of the fruit, then broke off a branch and left.

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, suppatiṭṭhe nigrodharāje adhivatthāya devatāya etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the deity haunting the royal banyan tree thought,

segs.p: ‘acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho.
segs.e: ‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!

segs.p: Yāva pāpo manusso, yatra hi nāma suppatiṭṭhassa nigrodharājassa yāvadatthaṁ phalāni bhakkhitvā sākhaṁ bhañjitvā pakkamissati, yannūna suppatiṭṭho nigrodharājā āyatiṁ phalaṁ na dadeyyā’ti.
segs.e: How wicked this person is, to eat as much as they like, then break off a branch and leave! Why don’t I make sure that the royal banyan tree gives no fruit in future?’

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, suppatiṭṭho nigrodharājā āyatiṁ phalaṁ na adāsi.
segs.e: Then the royal banyan tree gave no more fruit.

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, rājā korabyo yena sakko devānamindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then King Koravya went up to Sakka, lord of gods, and said to him,

segs.p: ‘yagghe, mārisa, jāneyyāsi suppatiṭṭho nigrodharājā phalaṁ na detī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Please good fellow, you should know that the royal banyan tree called Well Planted gives no fruit.’

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sakko devānamindo tathārūpaṁ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkhāsi, yathā bhusā vātavuṭṭhi āgantvā suppatiṭṭhaṁ nigrodharājaṁ pavattesi ummūlamakāsi.
segs.e: Then Sakka used his psychic powers to will that a violent storm come. And it felled and uprooted the royal banyan tree.

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, suppatiṭṭhe nigrodharāje adhivatthā devatā dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then the deity haunting the tree stood to one side, miserable and sad, weeping, with a tearful face.

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sakko devānamindo yena suppatiṭṭhe nigrodharāje adhivatthā devatā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā suppatiṭṭhe nigrodharāje adhivatthaṁ devataṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sakka went up to that deity, and said,

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu tvaṁ, devate, dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā ekamantaṁ ṭhitā’ti?
segs.e: ‘Why, god, are you standing to one side, miserable and sad, weeping, with a tearful face?’

segs.p: ‘Tathā hi pana me, mārisa, bhusā vātavuṭṭhi āgantvā bhavanaṁ pavattesi ummūlamakāsī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Because, my good fellow, a violent storm came and felled and uprooted my home.’

segs.p: ‘Api nu tvaṁ, devate, rukkhadhamme ṭhitāya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi āgantvā bhavanaṁ pavattesi ummūlamakāsī’ti?
segs.e: ‘Well, did you stand by your tree’s duty when the storm came?’

segs.p: ‘Kathaṁ pana, mārisa, rukkho rukkhadhamme ṭhito hotī’ti?
segs.e: ‘But my good fellow, how does a tree stand by its duty?’

segs.p: ‘Idha, devate, rukkhassa mūlaṁ mūlatthikā haranti, tacaṁ tacatthikā haranti, pattaṁ pattatthikā haranti, pupphaṁ pupphatthikā haranti, phalaṁ phalatthikā haranti.
segs.e: ‘It’s when those who need the tree’s roots, bark, leaves, flowers, or fruit take what they need.

segs.p: Na ca tena devatāya anattamanatā vā anabhinandi vā karaṇīyā.
segs.e: Yet the deity is not displeased or upset because of this.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, devate, rukkho rukkhadhamme ṭhito hotī’ti.
segs.e: This is how a tree stands by its duty.’

segs.p: ‘Aṭṭhitāyeva kho me, mārisa, rukkhadhamme bhusā vātavuṭṭhi āgantvā bhavanaṁ pavattesi ummūlamakāsī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I was not standing by a tree’s duty when the storm came and felled and uprooted my home.’

segs.p: ‘Sace kho tvaṁ, devate, rukkhadhamme tiṭṭheyyāsi, siyā te bhavanaṁ yathāpure’ti.
segs.e: ‘God, if you were to stand by a tree’s duty, your home may be as it was before.’

segs.p: ‘Ṭhassāmahaṁ, mārisa, rukkhadhamme, hotu me bhavanaṁ yathāpure’ti.
segs.e: ‘I will stand by a tree’s duty! May my home be as it was before!’

segs.p: Atha kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sakko devānamindo tathārūpaṁ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkhāsi, yathā bhusā vātavuṭṭhi āgantvā suppatiṭṭhaṁ nigrodharājaṁ ussāpesi, sacchavīni mūlāni ahesuṁ.
segs.e: Then Sakka used his psychic power to will that a violent storm come. And it raised up that mighty banyan tree and the bark of the roots was healed.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, api nu taṁ samaṇadhamme ṭhitaṁ jātibhūmakā upāsakā pabbājesuṁ sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattahi āvāsehī”ti?
segs.e: In the same way, Brahmin Dhammika, were you standing by an ascetic’s duty when the local lay followers banished you from all seven of the monasteries in your native land?”

segs.p: “Kathaṁ pana, bhante, samaṇo samaṇadhamme ṭhito hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how do I stand by an ascetic’s duty?”

segs.p: “Idha, brāhmaṇa dhammika, samaṇo akkosantaṁ na paccakkosati, rosantaṁ na paṭirosati, bhaṇḍantaṁ na paṭibhaṇḍati.
segs.e: “When someone abuses, annoys, or argues with an ascetic, the ascetic doesn’t abuse, annoy, or argue back at them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, samaṇo samaṇadhamme ṭhito hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how an ascetic stands by an ascetic’s duty.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhitaṁyeva maṁ, bhante, samaṇadhamme jātibhūmakā upāsakā pabbājesuṁ sabbaso jātibhūmiyaṁ sattahi āvāsehī”ti.
segs.e: “I was not standing by an ascetic’s duty when the local lay followers banished me from all seven of the monasteries in my native land.”

segs.p: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sunetto nāma satthā ahosi titthakaro kāmesu vītarāgo.
segs.e: “Once upon a time, there was a teacher named Sunetta. He was a religious founder and was free of desire for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Sunettassa kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, satthuno anekāni sāvakasatāni ahesuṁ.
segs.e: He had many hundreds of disciples.

segs.p: Sunetto satthā sāvakānaṁ brahmalokasahabyatāya dhammaṁ desesi.
segs.e: He taught them a Dhamma for rebirth in the company of Divinity.

segs.p: Ye kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sunettassa satthuno brahmalokasahabyatāya dhammaṁ desentassa cittāni na pasādesuṁ te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjiṁsu.
segs.e: Those lacking confidence in Sunetta were—when their body broke up, after death—reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ye kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sunettassa satthuno brahmalokasahabyatāya dhammaṁ desentassa cittāni pasādesuṁ te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjiṁsu.
segs.e: Those full of confidence in Sunetta were—when their body broke up, after death—reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Bhūtapubbaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, mūgapakkho nāma satthā ahosi …pe…
segs.e: Once upon a time, there was a teacher named Mūgapakkha …

segs.p: Aranemi nāma satthā ahosi …
segs.e: Aranemi …

segs.p: … Kuddālako nāma satthā ahosi …
segs.e: Kuddālaka …

segs.p: … Hatthipālo nāma satthā ahosi …
segs.e: Hatthipāla …

segs.p: … Jotipālo nāma satthā ahosi titthakaro kāmesu vītarāgo.
segs.e: Jotipāla. He was a religious founder and was free of desire for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Jotipālassa kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, satthuno anekāni sāvakasatāni ahesuṁ.
segs.e: He had many hundreds of disciples.

segs.p: Jotipālo satthā sāvakānaṁ brahmalokasahabyatāya dhammaṁ desesi.
segs.e: He taught them a Dhamma for rebirth in the company of Divinity.

segs.p: Ye kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, jotipālassa satthuno brahmalokasahabyatāya dhammaṁ desentassa cittāni na pasādesuṁ te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjiṁsu.
segs.e: Those lacking confidence in Jotipāla were—when their body broke up, after death—reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ye kho pana, brāhmaṇa dhammika, jotipālassa satthuno brahmalokasahabyatāya dhammaṁ desentassa cittāni pasādesuṁ te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjiṁsu.
segs.e: Those full of confidence in Jotipāla were—when their body broke up, after death—reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, brāhmaṇa dhammika,
segs.e: What do you think, Brahmin Dhammika?

segs.p: yo ime cha satthāre titthakare kāmesu vītarāge, anekasataparivāre sasāvakasaṅghe paduṭṭhacitto akkoseyya paribhāseyya, bahuṁ so apuññaṁ pasaveyyā”ti?
segs.e: If someone with malicious intent were to abuse and insult these six teachers with their hundreds of followers, would they not brim with much wickedness?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yo kho, brāhmaṇa dhammika, ime cha satthāre titthakare kāmesu vītarāge anekasataparivāre sasāvakasaṅghe paduṭṭhacitto akkoseyya paribhāseyya, bahuṁ so apuññaṁ pasaveyya.
segs.e: “They would indeed.

segs.p: Yo ekaṁ diṭṭhisampannaṁ puggalaṁ paduṭṭhacitto akkosati paribhāsati, ayaṁ tato bahutaraṁ apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: But someone who abuses and insults a single individual accomplished in view with malicious intent brims even more with wickedness.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa dhammika, ito bahiddhā evarūpiṁ khantiṁ vadāmi, yathāmaṁ sabrahmacārīsu.
segs.e: Brahmin Dhammika, I say that any injury done by those outside of the Buddhist community does not compare with what is done to one’s own spiritual companions.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, brāhmaṇa dhammika, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘na no samasabrahmacārīsu cittāni paduṭṭhāni bhavissantī’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will have no malicious intent for those who we want to have as our spiritual companions.’

segs.p: Evañhi te, brāhmaṇa dhammika, sikkhitabbanti.
segs.e: That is how you should train.

segs.p: Sunetto mūgapakkho ca,
segs.e: Sunetta and Mūgapakkha,

segs.p: aranemi ca brāhmaṇo;
segs.e: and Aranemi the brahmin,

segs.p: Kuddālako ahu satthā,
segs.e: Hatthipāla the student,

segs.p: hatthipālo ca māṇavo.
segs.e: and Kuddālaka were Teachers.

segs.p: Jotipālo ca govindo,
segs.e: And Jotipāla Govinda

segs.p: ahu sattapurohito;
segs.e: was priest for seven kings.

segs.p: Ahiṁsakā atītaṁse,
segs.e: These six famous teachers,

segs.p: cha satthāro yasassino.
segs.e: harmless ones of the past,

segs.p: Nirāmagandhā karuṇedhimuttā,
segs.e: were free of putrefaction, compassionate,

segs.p: Kāmasaṁyojanātigā;
segs.e: gone beyond the fetter of sensuality.

segs.p: Kāmarāgaṁ virājetvā,
segs.e: Detached from sensual desire,

segs.p: Brahmalokūpagā ahuṁ.
segs.e: they were reborn in the realm of divinity.

segs.p: Ahesuṁ sāvakā tesaṁ,
segs.e: Many hundreds of

segs.p: Anekāni satānipi;
segs.e: their disciples were also

segs.p: Nirāmagandhā karuṇedhimuttā,
segs.e: free of putrefaction-stench, compassionate,

segs.p: Kāmasaṁyojanātigā;
segs.e: gone beyond the fetter of sensuality.

segs.p: Kāmarāgaṁ virājetvā,
segs.e: Detached from sensual desire,

segs.p: Brahmalokūpagā ahuṁ.
segs.e: they were reborn in the realm of divinity.

segs.p: Yete isī bāhirake,
segs.e: One who insults

segs.p: vītarāge samāhite;
segs.e: with malicious intent

segs.p: Paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo,
segs.e: these non-Buddhist seers,

segs.p: yo naro paribhāsati;
segs.e: free of desire, immersed in samādhi;

segs.p: Bahuñca so pasavati,
segs.e: such a man

segs.p: apuññaṁ tādiso naro.
segs.e: brims with much wickedness.

segs.p: Yo cekaṁ diṭṭhisampannaṁ,
segs.e: But one who insults

segs.p: Bhikkhuṁ buddhassa sāvakaṁ;
segs.e: with malicious intent

segs.p: Paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo,
segs.e: a single individual accomplished in view,

segs.p: Yo naro paribhāsati;
segs.e: a mendicant disciple of the Buddha;

segs.p: Ayaṁ tato bahutaraṁ,
segs.e: that man

segs.p: Apuññaṁ pasave naro.
segs.e: brims even more with wickedness.

segs.p: Na sādhurūpaṁ āsīde,
segs.e: You shouldn’t attack a holy person,

segs.p: diṭṭhiṭṭhānappahāyinaṁ;
segs.e: who has given up the grounds for views.

segs.p: Sattamo puggalo eso,
segs.e: This individual is called

segs.p: ariyasaṅghassa vuccati.
segs.e: the seventh of the noble Saṅgha.

segs.p: Avītarāgo kāmesu,
segs.e: They’re not free of desire for sensual pleasures,

segs.p: yassa pañcindriyā mudū;
segs.e: and their faculties are still immature:

segs.p: Saddhā sati ca vīriyaṁ,
segs.e: faith, mindfulness, and energy,

segs.p: samatho ca vipassanā.
segs.e: serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Tādisaṁ bhikkhumāsajja,
segs.e: If you attack such a mendicant,

segs.p: pubbeva upahaññati;
segs.e: you first hurt yourself.

segs.p: Attānaṁ upahantvāna,
segs.e: Having hurt yourself,

segs.p: pacchā aññaṁ vihiṁsati.
segs.e: you harm the other.

segs.p: Yo ca rakkhati attānaṁ,
segs.e: But if you protect yourself,

segs.p: rakkhito tassa bāhiro;
segs.e: the other is also protected.

segs.p: Tasmā rakkheyya attānaṁ,
segs.e: So you should protect yourself.

segs.p: akkhato paṇḍito sadā”ti.
segs.e: An astute person is always uninjured.”

segs.p: Dvādasamaṁ.
Dhammikavaggo pañcamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Nāgamigasālā iṇaṁ,
Cundaṁ dve sandiṭṭhikā duve;
Khemaindriya ānanda,
Khattiyā appamādena dhammikoti.
Paṭhamo paṇṇāsako samatto.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.55
