segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Soṇasutta
segs.e: With Soṇa

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā soṇo rājagahe viharati sītavanasmiṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Soṇa was staying near Rājagaha in the Cool Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato soṇassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

segs.p: “ye kho keci bhagavato sāvakā āraddhavīriyā viharanti, ahaṁ tesaṁ aññataro.
segs.e: “I am one of the Buddha’s most energetic disciples.

segs.p: Atha ca pana me na anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccati, saṁvijjanti kho pana me kule bhogā, sakkā bhogā ca bhuñjituṁ puññāni ca kātuṁ.
segs.e: Yet my mind is not freed from defilements by not grasping. But my family has wealth. I could enjoy that wealth and make merit.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjeyyaṁ puññāni ca kareyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I resign the training and return to a lesser life, so I can enjoy my wealth and make merit?”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato soṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ kho—gijjhakūṭe pabbate antarahito sītavane āyasmato soṇassa sammukhe pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha knew Venerable Soṇa’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the Vulture’s Peak and reappeared in the Cool Grove in front of Soṇa,

segs.p: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane.
segs.e: and sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Āyasmāpi kho soṇo bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Soṇa bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ soṇaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “Nanu te, soṇa, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: “Soṇa, as you were in private retreat didn’t this thought come to your mind:

segs.p: ‘ye kho keci bhagavato sāvakā āraddhavīriyā viharanti, ahaṁ tesaṁ aññataro.
segs.e: ‘I am one of the Buddha’s most energetic disciples.

segs.p: Atha ca pana me na anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccati, saṁvijjanti kho pana me kule bhogā, sakkā bhogā ca bhuñjituṁ puññāni ca kātuṁ.
segs.e: Yet my mind is not freed from defilements by not grasping. But my family has wealth. I could enjoy that wealth and make merit.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjeyyaṁ puññāni ca kareyyan’”ti?
segs.e: Why don’t I resign the training and return to a lesser life, so I can enjoy my wealth and make merit?’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, soṇa,
segs.e: “What do you think, Soṇa?

segs.p: kusalo tvaṁ pubbe agāriyabhūto vīṇāya tantissare”ti?
segs.e: When you were still a layman, weren’t you a good player of the arched harp?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo accāyatā honti, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṁ samaye saravatī vā hoti kammaññā vā”ti?
segs.e: “When your harp’s strings were tuned too tight, was it resonant and playable?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo atisithilā honti, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṁ samaye saravatī vā hoti kammaññā vā”ti?
segs.e: “When your harp’s strings were tuned too slack, was it resonant and playable?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Yadā pana te, soṇa, vīṇāya tantiyo na accāyatā honti nātisithilā same guṇe patiṭṭhitā, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṁ samaye saravatī vā hoti kammaññā vā”ti?
segs.e: “But when your harp’s strings were tuned neither too tight nor too slack, but fixed at an even tension, was it resonant and playable?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho, soṇa, accāraddhavīriyaṁ uddhaccāya saṁvattati, atisithilavīriyaṁ kosajjāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “In the same way, Soṇa, when energy is too forceful it leads to restlessness. When energy is too slack it leads to laziness.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, soṇa, vīriyasamathaṁ adhiṭṭhaha, indriyānañca samataṁ paṭivijjha, tattha ca nimittaṁ gaṇhāhī”ti.
segs.e: So, Soṇa, you should focus on energy and serenity, find a balance of the faculties, and learn the character of this situation.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā soṇo bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Soṇa replied.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ soṇaṁ iminā ovādena ovaditvā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ kho—sītavane antarahito gijjhakūṭe pabbate pāturahosi.
segs.e: After advising Soṇa like this, the Buddha, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from the Cool Grove and reappeared on the Vulture’s Peak.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā soṇo aparena samayena vīriyasamathaṁ adhiṭṭhāsi, indriyānañca samataṁ paṭivijjhi, tattha ca nimittaṁ aggahesi.
segs.e: After some time Soṇa focused on energy and serenity, found a balance of the faculties, and learned the pattern of this situation.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā soṇo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anāgāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Soṇa, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā soṇo arahataṁ ahosi.
segs.e: And Venerable Soṇa became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato soṇassa arahattappattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then, when Soṇa had attained perfection, he thought,

segs.p: “yannūnāhaṁ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyaṁ; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike aññaṁ byākareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Why don’t I go to the Buddha and declare my enlightenment in his presence?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā soṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā soṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Soṇa went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Yo so, bhante, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto, so cha ṭhānāni adhimutto hoti—
segs.e: “Sir, a mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—is dedicated to six things.

segs.p: nekkhammādhimutto hoti, pavivekādhimutto hoti, abyāpajjādhimutto hoti, taṇhākkhayādhimutto hoti, upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti, asammohādhimutto hoti.
segs.e: They are dedicated to renunciation, seclusion, kindness, the ending of craving, the ending of grasping, and mental clarity.

segs.p: Siyā kho pana, bhante, idhekaccassa āyasmato evamassa:
segs.e: It may be, sir, that one of the venerables here thinks:

segs.p: ‘kevalaṁsaddhāmattakaṁ nūna ayamāyasmā nissāya nekkhammādhimutto’ti.
segs.e: ‘Maybe this venerable is dedicated to renunciation solely out of mere faith.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, bhante, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But it should not be seen like this.

segs.p: Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu vusitavā katakaraṇīyo karaṇīyaṁ attano asamanupassanto katassa vā paṭicayaṁ khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā nekkhammādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā nekkhammādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā nekkhammādhimutto hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant with defilements ended does not see in themselves anything more to do, or anything that needs improvement. They’re dedicated to renunciation because they’re free of greed, hate, and delusion with the end of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Siyā kho pana, bhante, idhekaccassa āyasmato evamassa:
segs.e: It may be, sir, that one of the venerables here thinks:

segs.p: ‘lābhasakkārasilokaṁ nūna ayamāyasmā nikāmayamāno pavivekādhimutto’ti.
segs.e: ‘Maybe this venerable is dedicated to seclusion because they enjoy possessions, honor, and popularity.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, bhante, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But it should not be seen like this. …

segs.p: Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu vusitavā katakaraṇīyo karaṇīyaṁ attano asamanupassanto katassa vā paṭicayaṁ khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā pavivekādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā pavivekādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā pavivekādhimutto hoti.
Siyā kho pana, bhante, idhekaccassa āyasmato evamassa:
segs.e: It may be, sir, that one of the venerables here thinks:

segs.p: ‘sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ nūna ayamāyasmā sārato paccāgacchanto abyāpajjādhimutto’ti.
segs.e: ‘Maybe this venerable is dedicated to kindness because they believe that adhering to precepts and observances is essential.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, bhante, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But it should not be seen like this. …

segs.p: Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu vusitavā katakaraṇīyo karaṇīyaṁ attano asamanupassanto katassa vā paṭicayaṁ khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā abyāpajjādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā abyāpajjādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā abyāpajjādhimutto hoti.
Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā taṇhākkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā taṇhākkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā taṇhākkhayādhimutto hoti.
segs.e: They’re dedicated to the ending of craving because they’re free of greed, hate, and delusion with the end of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti.
segs.e: They’re dedicated to the ending of grasping because they’re free of greed, hate, and delusion with the end of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā asammohādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā asammohādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā asammohādhimutto hoti.
segs.e: They’re dedicated to clarity of mind because they’re free of greed, hate, and delusion with the end of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Evaṁ sammā vimuttacittassa, bhante, bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti.
segs.e: When a mendicant’s mind is rightly freed like this, even if compelling sights come into the range of vision they don’t overcome their mind.

segs.p: Amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ vayañcassānupassati.
segs.e: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

segs.p: Bhusā cepi sotaviññeyyā saddā …
segs.e: Even if compelling sounds …

segs.p: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
segs.e: smells …

segs.p: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
segs.e: tastes …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā …
segs.e: touches …

segs.p: manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti.
segs.e: and ideas come into the range of the mind they don’t overcome the mind.

segs.p: Amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ vayañcassānupassati.
segs.e: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, selo pabbato acchiddo asusiro ekagghano.
segs.e: Suppose there was a mountain that was one solid mass of rock, without cracks or holes.

segs.p: Atha puratthimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi neva naṁ saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampavedheyya, atha pacchimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi …
segs.e: Even if violent storms were to blow up out of the east, the west, the north, and the south,

segs.p: atha uttarāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi …
atha dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi neva naṁ saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampavedheyya;
segs.e: they couldn’t make it shake or rock or tremble.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhante, evaṁ sammāvimuttacittassa bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti.
segs.e: In the same way, when a mendicant’s mind is rightly freed like this, even if compelling sights come into the range of vision they don’t overcome their mind. …

segs.p: Amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti, ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ vayañcassānupassati.
Bhusā cepi sotaviññeyyā saddā …
ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā …
manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti.
Amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ vayañcassānupassatīti.
segs.e: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

segs.p: Nekkhammaṁ adhimuttassa,
segs.e: When you’re dedicated to renunciation

segs.p: pavivekañca cetaso;
segs.e: and seclusion of the heart;

segs.p: Abyāpajjādhimuttassa,
segs.e: when you’re dedicated to kindness

segs.p: upādānakkhayassa ca.
segs.e: and the end of grasping;

segs.p: Taṇhākkhayādhimuttassa,
segs.e: when you’re dedicated to the ending of craving

segs.p: asammohañca cetaso;
segs.e: and clarity of heart;

segs.p: Disvā āyatanuppādaṁ,
segs.e: and you’ve seen the arising of the senses,

segs.p: sammā cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: your mind is rightly freed.

segs.p: Tassa sammā vimuttassa,
segs.e: For that one, rightly freed,

segs.p: santacittassa bhikkhuno;
segs.e: a mendicant with peaceful mind,

segs.p: Katassa paṭicayo natthi,
segs.e: there’s nothing to be improved,

segs.p: karaṇīyaṁ na vijjati.
segs.e: and nothing more to do.

segs.p: Selo yathā ekagghano,
segs.e: As the wind cannot stir

segs.p: vātena na samīrati;
segs.e: a solid mass of rock,

segs.p: Evaṁ rūpā rasā saddā,
segs.e: so too sights, tastes, sounds,

segs.p: gandhā phassā ca kevalā.
segs.e: smells, and touches—the lot—

segs.p: Iṭṭhā dhammā aniṭṭhā ca,
segs.e: and ideas, whether liked or disliked,

segs.p: nappavedhenti tādino;
segs.e: don’t disturb the unaffected one.

segs.p: Ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ vippamuttaṁ,
segs.e: Their mind is steady and free

segs.p: vayañcassānupassatī”ti.
segs.e: as they observe fall.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.56
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.56

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Phaggunasutta
segs.e: With Phagguna

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā phagguno ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Phagguna was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “āyasmā, bhante, phagguno ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: “Sir, Venerable Phagguna is sick.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yenāyasmā phagguno tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: Sir, please go to Venerable Phagguna out of sympathy.”

segs.p: Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
segs.e: The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā phagguno tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to Venerable Phagguna.

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā phagguno bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: Venerable Phagguna saw the Buddha coming off in the distance

segs.p: Disvāna mañcake samadhosi.
segs.e: and stirred in his cot.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ phaggunaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “alaṁ, phagguna, mā tvaṁ mañcake samadhosi.
segs.e: “It’s all right, Phagguna, don’t get up.

segs.p: Santimāni āsanāni parehi paññattāni, tatthāhaṁ nisīdissāmī”ti.
segs.e: There are some seats spread out by others, I will sit there.”

segs.p: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane.
segs.e: He sat down on the seat spread out

segs.p: Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ phaggunaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to Venerable Phagguna:

segs.p: “Kacci te, phagguna, khamanīyaṁ kacci yāpanīyaṁ? Kacci te dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, Phagguna; I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

segs.p: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
segs.e: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani abhimattheyya; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimattā vātā muddhani ūhananti.
segs.e: The winds piercing my head are so severe, it feels like a strong man drilling into my head with a sharp point.

segs.p: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
segs.e: I’m not keeping well.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena sīsaveṭhanaṁ dadeyya; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā.
segs.e: The pain in my head is so severe, it feels like a strong man tightening a strong leather strap around my head.

segs.p: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
segs.e: I’m not keeping well.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṁ parikanteyya; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimattā vātā kucchiṁ parikantanti.
segs.e: The winds slicing my belly are so severe, like a deft butcher or their apprentice were slicing open a cow’s belly with a sharp meat cleaver.

segs.p: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
segs.e: I’m not keeping well.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṁ purisaṁ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṁ samparitāpeyyuṁ; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimatto kāyasmiṁ ḍāho.
segs.e: The burning in my body is so severe, it feels like two strong men grabbing a weaker man by the arms to burn and scorch him on a pit of glowing coals.

segs.p: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.
segs.e: I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ phaggunaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired Venerable Phagguna with a Dhamma talk, after which he rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā phagguno acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi.
segs.e: Not long after the Buddha left, Venerable Phagguna passed away.

segs.p: Tamhi cassa samaye maraṇakāle indriyāni vippasīdiṁsu.
segs.e: At the time of his death, his faculties were bright and clear.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “āyasmā, bhante, phagguno acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi.
segs.e: “Sir, soon after the Buddha left, Venerable Phagguna died.

segs.p: Tamhi cassa samaye maraṇakāle indriyāni vippasīdiṁsū”ti.
segs.e: At the time of his death, his faculties were bright and clear.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ hānanda, phaggunassa bhikkhuno indriyāni na vippasīdissanti.
segs.e: “And why shouldn’t his faculties be bright and clear?

segs.p: Phaggunassa, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ ahosi.
segs.e: The mendicant Phagguna’s mind was not freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ.
segs.e: But when he heard that teaching his mind was freed from them.

segs.p: Chayime, ānanda, ānisaṁsā kālena dhammassavane kālena atthupaparikkhāya.
segs.e: Ānanda, there are these six benefits to hearing the teaching at the right time and examining the meaning at the right time.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idhānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Firstly, take the case of a mendicant whose mind is not freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: At the time of death they get to see the Realized One.

segs.p: Tassa tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: The Realized One teaches Dhamma to them that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, paṭhamo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
segs.e: This is the first benefit of listening to the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is not freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, api ca kho tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya.
segs.e: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, but they get to see a Realized One’s disciple.

segs.p: Tassa tathāgatasāvako dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: The Realized One’s disciple teaches them Dhamma …

segs.p: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, dutiyo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
segs.e: This is the second benefit of listening to the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is not freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, napi tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya;
segs.e: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, or to see a Realized One’s disciple.

segs.p: api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
segs.e: But they think about and consider the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Tassa yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakkayato anuvicārayato manasānupekkhato pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: As they do so their mind is freed from the five lower fetters.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, tatiyo ānisaṁso kālena atthupaparikkhāya.
segs.e: This is the third benefit of listening to the teaching.

segs.p: Idhānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, anuttare ca kho upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Next, take the case of a mendicant whose mind is freed from the five lower fetters, but not with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: At the time of death they get to see the Realized One.

segs.p: Tassa tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ …pe… brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: The Realized One teaches them Dhamma …

segs.p: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, catuttho ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
segs.e: This is the fourth benefit of listening to the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, anuttare ca kho upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is freed from the five lower fetters, but not with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, api ca kho tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya.
segs.e: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, but they get to see a Realized One’s disciple.

segs.p: Tassa tathāgatasāvako dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ …pe… parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: The Realized One’s disciple teaches them Dhamma …

segs.p: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, pañcamo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
segs.e: This is the fifth benefit of listening to the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, anuttare ca kho upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is freed from the five lower fetters, but not with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, napi tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya;
segs.e: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, or to see a Realized One’s disciple.

segs.p: api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
segs.e: But they think about and consider the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Tassa yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakkayato anuvicārayato manasānupekkhato anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ vimuccati.
segs.e: As they do so their mind is freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, ānanda, chaṭṭho ānisaṁso kālena atthupaparikkhāya.
segs.e: This is the sixth benefit of listening to the teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, ānanda, cha ānisaṁsā kālena dhammassavane kālena atthupaparikkhāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the six benefits to hearing the teaching at the right time and examining the meaning at the right time.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.57
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.57

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Chaḷabhijātisutta
segs.e: The Six Classes of Rebirth

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “pūraṇena, bhante, kassapena chaḷabhijātiyo paññattā—
segs.e: “Sir, Pūraṇa Kassapa describes six classes of rebirth:

segs.p: kaṇhābhijāti paññattā, nīlābhijāti paññattā, lohitābhijāti paññattā, haliddābhijāti paññattā, sukkābhijāti paññattā, paramasukkābhijāti paññattā.
segs.e: black, blue, red, yellow, white, and ultimate white.

segs.p: Tatridaṁ, bhante, pūraṇena kassapena kaṇhābhijāti paññattā, orabbhikā sūkarikā sākuṇikā māgavikā luddā macchaghātakā corā coraghātakā bandhanāgārikā ye vā panaññepi keci kurūrakammantā.
segs.e: The black class of rebirth consists of slaughterers of sheep, pigs, poultry, or deer, hunters or fishers, bandits, executioners, butchers of cattle, jailers, and any others with a cruel livelihood.

segs.p: Tatridaṁ, bhante, pūraṇena kassapena nīlābhijāti paññattā, bhikkhū kaṇṭakavuttikā ye vā panaññepi keci kammavādā kriyavādā.
segs.e: The blue class of rebirth consists of mendicants whose life is thorny, and any others who teach the efficacy of deeds and action.

segs.p: Tatridaṁ, bhante, pūraṇena kassapena lohitābhijāti paññattā, nigaṇṭhā ekasāṭakā.
segs.e: The red class of rebirth consists of the Jain ascetics who wear one cloth.

segs.p: Tatridaṁ, bhante, pūraṇena kassapena haliddābhijāti paññattā, gihī odātavasanā acelakasāvakā.
segs.e: The yellow class of rebirth consists of the lay people dressed in white who are disciples of the naked ascetics.

segs.p: Tatridaṁ, bhante, pūraṇena kassapena sukkābhijāti paññattā, ājīvakā ājīvakiniyo.
segs.e: The white class of rebirth consists of male and female Ājīvaka ascetics.

segs.p: Tatridaṁ, bhante, pūraṇena kassapena paramasukkābhijāti paññattā, nando vaccho kiso saṅkicco makkhali gosālo.
segs.e: And the ultimate white class of rebirth consists of Nanda Vaccha, Kisa Saṅkicca, and the bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla.

segs.p: Pūraṇena, bhante, kassapena imā chaḷabhijātiyo paññattā”ti.
segs.e: These are the six classes of rebirth that Pūraṇa Kassapa describes.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ panānanda, pūraṇassa kassapassa sabbo loko etadabbhanujānāti imā chaḷabhijātiyo paññāpetun”ti?
segs.e: “But Ānanda, did the whole world authorize Pūraṇa Kassapa to describe these six classes of rebirth?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, puriso daliddo assako anāḷhiko, tassa akāmakassa bilaṁ olaggeyyuṁ: ‘idaṁ te, ambho purisa, maṁsañca khāditabbaṁ, mūlañca anuppadātabban’ti.
segs.e: “It’s as if they were to force a chop on a poor, penniless person, telling them, ‘Eat this meat and pay for it!’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, ānanda, pūraṇena kassapena appaṭiññāya etesaṁ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ imā chaḷabhijātiyo paññattā, yathā taṁ bālena abyattena akhettaññunā akusalena.
segs.e: In the same way, Pūraṇa Kassapa has described these six classes of rebirth without the consent of those ascetics and brahmins. And he has done so in a foolish, incompetent, unskilled way, lacking common sense.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho panānanda, chaḷabhijātiyo paññāpemi.
segs.e: I, however, also describe six classes of rebirth.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “katamā cānanda, chaḷabhijātiyo?
segs.e: “And what, Ānanda, are the six classes of rebirth?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to a dark result.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekacco kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to a bright result.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekacco kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekacco sukkābhijātiyo samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to a dark result.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekacco sukkābhijātiyo samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to a bright result.

segs.p: Idha panānanda, ekacco sukkābhijātiyo samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segs.p: Kathañcānanda, kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati?
segs.e: And how does someone born into a dark class give rise to a dark result?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco nīce kule paccājāto hoti—caṇḍālakule vā nesādakule vā venakule vā rathakārakule vā pukkusakule vā, dalidde appannapānabhojane kasiravuttike, yattha kasirena ghāsacchādo labbhati.
segs.e: It’s when someone is reborn in a low family—a family of corpse-workers, hunters, bamboo-workers, chariot-makers, or scavengers—poor, with little to eat or drink, where life is tough, and food and shelter are hard to find.

segs.p: So ca hoti dubbaṇṇo duddasiko okoṭimako bavhābādho kāṇo vā kuṇī vā khañjo vā pakkhahato vā, na lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
segs.e: And they’re ugly, unsightly, deformed, sickly—one-eyed, crippled, lame, or half-paralyzed. They don’t get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; or bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: And they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya duccaritaṁ caritvā, manasā duccaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: That’s how someone born into a dark class gives rise to a dark result.

segs.p: Kathañcānanda, kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati?
segs.e: And how does someone born into a dark class give rise to a bright result?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco nīce kule paccājāto hoti—caṇḍālakule vā …pe…
segs.e: It’s when some person is reborn in a low family …

segs.p: seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
So kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: But they do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena sucaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ caritvā, manasā sucaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: That’s how someone born into a dark class gives rise to a bright result.

segs.p: Kathañcānanda, kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati?
segs.e: And how does someone born into a dark class give rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco nīce kule paccājāto hoti—caṇḍālakule vā …pe…
segs.e: It’s when some person is reborn in a low family …

segs.p: so ca hoti dubbaṇṇo duddasiko okoṭimako.
So kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajati.
segs.e: They shave off their hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: So evaṁ pabbajito samāno pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto, satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṁ bhāvetvā akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: They give up the five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom. They firmly establish their mind in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. They truly develop the seven awakening factors. And then they give rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, kaṇhābhijātiyo samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: That’s how someone born in a dark class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segs.p: Kathañcānanda, sukkābhijātiyo samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati?
segs.e: And how does someone born into a bright class give rise to a dark result?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco ucce kule paccājāto hoti—khattiyamahāsālakule vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakule vā gahapatimahāsālakule vā, aḍḍhe mahaddhane mahābhoge pahūtajātarūparajate pahūtavittūpakaraṇe pahūtadhanadhaññe.
segs.e: It’s when someone is reborn in an eminent family—a well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

segs.p: So ca hoti abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato, lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
segs.e: And they’re attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. They get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: But they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya duccaritaṁ caritvā, manasā duccaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, sukkābhijātiyo samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: That’s how someone born into a bright class gives rise to a dark result.

segs.p: Kathañcānanda, sukkābhijātiyo samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati?
segs.e: And how does someone born into a bright class give rise to a bright result?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco ucce kule paccājāto hoti—khattiyamahāsālakule vā …pe…
segs.e: It’s when some person is reborn in an eminent family …

segs.p: seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
So kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: And they do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena sucaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ caritvā, manasā sucaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, sukkābhijātiyo samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: That’s how someone born into a bright class give rise to a bright result.

segs.p: Kathañcānanda, sukkābhijātiyo samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati?
segs.e: And how does someone born into a bright class give rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright?

segs.p: Idhānanda, ekacco ucce kule paccājāto hoti—khattiyamahāsālakule vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakule vā gahapatimahāsālakule vā, aḍḍhe mahaddhane mahābhoge pahūtajātarūparajate pahūtavittūpakaraṇe pahūtadhanadhaññe.
segs.e: It’s when some person is reborn in an eminent family …

segs.p: So ca hoti abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato, lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
So kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajati.
segs.e: They shave off their hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: So evaṁ pabbajito samāno pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto, satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṁ bhāvetvā akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: They give up the five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom. They firmly establish their mind in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. They truly develop the seven awakening factors. And then they give rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, sukkābhijātiyo samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.
segs.e: That’s how someone born into a bright class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segs.p: Imā kho, ānanda, chaḷabhijātiyo”ti.
segs.e: These are the six classes of rebirth.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.58
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.58

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Āsavasutta
segs.e: Defilements

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ye āsavā saṁvarā pahātabbā te saṁvarena pahīnā honti,
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who, by restraint, has given up the defilements that should be given up by restraint.

segs.p: ye āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā te paṭisevanāya pahīnā honti,
segs.e: By using, they’ve given up the defilements that should be given up by using.

segs.p: ye āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā te adhivāsanāya pahīnā honti,
segs.e: By enduring, they’ve given up the defilements that should be given up by enduring.

segs.p: ye āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā te parivajjanāya pahīnā honti,
segs.e: By avoiding, they’ve given up the defilements that should be given up by avoiding.

segs.p: ye āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā te vinodanāya pahīnā honti,
segs.e: By dispelling, they’ve given up the defilements that should be given up by dispelling.

segs.p: ye āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā te bhāvanāya pahīnā honti.
segs.e: By developing, they’ve given up the defilements that should be given up by developing.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā saṁvarā pahātabbā ye saṁvarena pahīnā honti?
segs.e: And what are the defilements that should be given up by restraint?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cakkhundriyasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, reflecting rationally, lives restraining the eye faculty.

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, cakkhundriyasaṁvaraṁ asaṁvutassa viharato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, cakkhundriyasaṁvaraṁ saṁvutassa viharato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without restraint of the eye faculty do not arise when there is such restraint.

segs.p: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso sotindriya …pe…
segs.e: Reflecting rationally, they live restraining the ear faculty …

segs.p: ghānindriya …
segs.e: the nose faculty …

segs.p: jivhindriya …
segs.e: the tongue faculty …

segs.p: kāyindriya …
segs.e: the body faculty …

segs.p: manindriyasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati.
segs.e: the mind faculty.

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, manindriyasaṁvaraṁ asaṁvutassa viharato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, manindriyasaṁvaraṁ saṁvutassa viharato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without restraint of the mind faculty do not arise when there is such restraint.

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā saṁvarā pahātabbā ye saṁvarena pahīnā honti.
segs.e: These are called the defilements that should be given up by restraint.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā ye paṭisevanāya pahīnā honti?
segs.e: And what are the defilements that should be given up by using?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cīvaraṁ paṭisevati:
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, reflecting rationally, makes use of robes:

segs.p: ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva hirikopīnapaṭicchādanatthaṁ’.
segs.e: ‘Only for the sake of warding off cold and heat; for warding off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; and for covering up the private parts.’

segs.p: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso piṇḍapātaṁ paṭisevati:
segs.e: Reflecting rationally, they make use of almsfood:

segs.p: ‘neva davāya na madāya na maṇḍanāya na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṁsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṁ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṁ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro ca’.
segs.e: ‘Not for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration, but only to sustain this body, to avoid harm, and to support spiritual practice. In this way, I shall put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and I will have the means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

segs.p: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso senāsanaṁ paṭisevati:
segs.e: Reflecting rationally, they make use of lodgings:

segs.p: ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva utuparissayavinodanapaṭisallānārāmatthaṁ’.
segs.e: ‘Only for the sake of warding off cold and heat; for warding off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; to shelter from harsh weather and to enjoy retreat.’

segs.p: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ paṭisevati:
segs.e: Reflecting rationally, they make use of medicines and supplies for the sick:

segs.p: ‘yāvadeva uppannānaṁ veyyābādhikānaṁ vedanānaṁ paṭighātāya, abyābajjhaparamatāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Only for the sake of warding off the pains of illness and to promote good health.’

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, appaṭisevato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, paṭisevato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without using these things do not arise when they are used.

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā ye paṭisevanāya pahīnā honti.
segs.e: These are called the defilements that should be given up by using.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā ye adhivāsanāya pahīnā honti?
segs.e: And what are the defilements that should be given up by enduring?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa, jighacchāya, pipāsāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ, duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ, uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, reflecting rationally, endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. They endure the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles. They endure rude and unwelcome criticism. And they put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, anadhivāsato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, adhivāsato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without enduring these things do not arise when they are endured.

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā ye adhivāsanāya pahīnā honti.
segs.e: These are called the defilements that should be given up by enduring.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā ye parivajjanāya pahīnā honti?
segs.e: And what are the defilements that should be given up by avoiding?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso caṇḍaṁ hatthiṁ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṁ assaṁ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṁ goṇaṁ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṁ kukkuraṁ parivajjeti, ahiṁ khāṇuṁ kaṇṭakaṭṭhānaṁ sobbhaṁ papātaṁ candanikaṁ oḷigallaṁ, yathārūpe anāsane nisinnaṁ, yathārūpe agocare carantaṁ, yathārūpe pāpake mitte bhajantaṁ viññū sabrahmacārī pāpakesu ṭhānesu okappeyyuṁ, so tañca anāsanaṁ tañca agocaraṁ te ca pāpake mitte paṭisaṅkhā yoniso parivajjeti.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, reflecting rationally, avoids a wild elephant, a wild horse, a wild ox, a wild dog, a snake, a stump, thorny ground, a pit, a cliff, a swamp, and a sewer. Reflecting rationally, they avoid sitting on inappropriate seats, walking in inappropriate neighborhoods, and mixing with bad friends—whatever sensible spiritual companions would believe to be a bad setting.

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, aparivajjayato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, parivajjayato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without avoiding these things do not arise when they are avoided.

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā ye parivajjanāya pahīnā honti.
segs.e: These are called the defilements that should be given up by avoiding.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā ye vinodanāya pahīnā honti?
segs.e: And what are the defilements that should be given up by dispelling?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti,
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, reflecting rationally, doesn’t tolerate a sensual,

segs.p: paṭisaṅkhā yoniso uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …
segs.e: malicious,

segs.p: uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ …
segs.e: or cruel thought that has arisen, but gives it up, dispels it, eliminates it, and obliterates it.

segs.p: uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
segs.e: They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, avinodayato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, vinodayato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without dispelling these things do not arise when they are dispelled.

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā ye vinodanāya pahīnā honti.
segs.e: These are called the defilements that should be given up by dispelling.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā ye bhāvanāya pahīnā honti?
segs.e: And what are the defilements that should be given up by developing?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vosaggapariṇāmiṁ,
segs.e: Take a mendicant who, reflecting rationally, develops the awakening factors of mindfulness,

segs.p: paṭisaṅkhā yoniso dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …
segs.e: investigation of principles,

segs.p: vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …
segs.e: energy,

segs.p: pītisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …
segs.e: rapture,

segs.p: passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …
segs.e: tranquility,

segs.p: samādhisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti …
segs.e: immersion,

segs.p: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vosaggapariṇāmiṁ.
segs.e: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

segs.p: Yaṁ hissa, bhikkhave, abhāvayato uppajjeyyuṁ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, bhāvayato evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: For the distressing and feverish defilements that might arise in someone who lives without developing these things do not arise when they are developed.

segs.p: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā ye bhāvanāya pahīnā honti.
segs.e: These are called the defilements that should be given up by developing.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.59
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.59

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Dārukammikasutta
segs.e: With Dārukammika

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

segs.p: Atha kho dārukammiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho dārukammikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Dārukammika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “api nu te, gahapati, kule dānaṁ dīyatī”ti?
segs.e: “Householder, I wonder whether your family gives gifts?”

segs.p: “Dīyati me, bhante, kule dānaṁ.
segs.e: “It does, sir.

segs.p: Tañca kho ye te bhikkhū āraññikā piṇḍapātikā paṁsukūlikā arahanto vā arahattamaggaṁ vā samāpannā, tathārūpesu me, bhante, bhikkhūsu dānaṁ dīyatī”ti.
segs.e: Gifts are given to those mendicants who are perfected or on the path to perfection; they live in the wilderness, eat only almsfood, and wear rag robes.”

segs.p: “Dujjānaṁ kho etaṁ, gahapati, tayā gihinā kāmabhoginā puttasambādhasayanaṁ ajjhāvasantena, kāsikacandanaṁ paccanubhontena, mālāgandhavilepanaṁ dhārayantena, jātarūparajataṁ sādiyantena ime vā arahanto ime vā arahattamaggaṁ samāpannāti.
segs.e: “Householder, as a layman enjoying sensual pleasures, living at home with your children, using sandalwood imported from Kāsi, wearing garlands, fragrance, and makeup, and accepting gold and currency, it’s hard for you to know who is perfected or on the path to perfection.

segs.p: Āraññiko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti uddhato unnaḷo capalo mukharo vikiṇṇavāco muṭṭhassati asampajāno asamāhito vibbhantacitto pākatindriyo.
segs.e: If a mendicant living in the wilderness is haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying mind and undisciplined faculties,

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re reprehensible.

segs.p: Āraññiko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti anuddhato anunnaḷo acapalo amukharo avikiṇṇavāco upaṭṭhitassati sampajāno samāhito ekaggacitto saṁvutindriyo.
segs.e: If a mendicant living in the wilderness is not haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, or loose-tongued, but has established mindfulness, situational awareness and immersion, with unified mind and restrained faculties,

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re praiseworthy.

segs.p: Gāmantavihārī cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti uddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who lives within a village is restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re reprehensible.

segs.p: Gāmantavihārī cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti anuddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who lives within a village is not restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re praiseworthy.

segs.p: Piṇḍapātiko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti uddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who eats only almsfood is restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re reprehensible.

segs.p: Piṇḍapātiko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti anuddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who eats only almsfood is not restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re praiseworthy.

segs.p: Nemantaniko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti uddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who accepts invitations is restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re reprehensible.

segs.p: Nemantaniko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti anuddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who accepts invitations is not restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re praiseworthy.

segs.p: Paṁsukūliko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti uddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who wears rag robes is restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re reprehensible.

segs.p: Paṁsukūliko cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti anuddhato …pe…
segs.e: If a mendicant who wears rag robes is not restless …

segs.p: evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re praiseworthy.

segs.p: Gahapaticīvaradharo cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti uddhato unnaḷo capalo mukharo vikiṇṇavāco muṭṭhassati asampajāno asamāhito vibbhantacitto pākatindriyo.
segs.e: If a mendicant who wears robes offered by householders is haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying mind and undisciplined faculties,

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena gārayho.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re reprehensible.

segs.p: Gahapaticīvaradharo cepi, gahapati, bhikkhu hoti anuddhato anunnaḷo acapalo amukharo avikiṇṇavāco upaṭṭhitassati sampajāno samāhito ekaggacitto saṁvutindriyo.
segs.e: If a mendicant who wears robes offered by householders is not haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, or loose-tongued, but has established mindfulness, situational awareness and immersion, with unified mind and restrained faculties,

segs.p: Evaṁ so tenaṅgena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: then in this respect they’re praiseworthy.

segs.p: Iṅgha tvaṁ, gahapati, saṅghe dānaṁ dehi.
segs.e: Go ahead, householder, give gifts to the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Saṅghe te dānaṁ dadato cittaṁ pasīdissati.
segs.e: Your mind will become bright and clear,

segs.p: So tvaṁ pasannacitto kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjissasī”ti.
segs.e: and when your body breaks up, after death, you’ll be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: “Esāhaṁ, bhante, ajjatagge saṅghe dānaṁ dassāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, from this day forth I will give gifts to the Saṅgha.”

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Hatthisāriputtasutta
segs.e: With Hatthisāriputta

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā therā bhikkhū pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnā sannipatitā abhidhammakathaṁ kathenti.
segs.e: Now at that time several senior mendicants, after the meal, on their return from almsround, sat together in the pavilion talking about the teachings.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ āyasmā citto hatthisāriputto therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ abhidhammakathaṁ kathentānaṁ antarantarā kathaṁ opāteti.
segs.e: Venerable Citta Hatthisāriputta interrupted them while they were talking.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ cittaṁ hatthisāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita said to Venerable Citta Hatthisāriputta,

segs.p: “māyasmā citto hatthisāriputto therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ abhidhammakathaṁ kathentānaṁ antarantarā kathaṁ opātesi, yāva kathāpariyosānaṁ āyasmā citto āgametū”ti.
segs.e: “Venerable, please don’t interrupt the senior mendicants while they’re talking about the teachings. Wait until the end of the discussion.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmato cittassa hatthisāriputtassa sahāyakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When he said this, Citta Hatthisāriputta’s companions said to Mahākoṭṭhita,

segs.p: “māyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ cittaṁ hatthisāriputtaṁ apasādesi, paṇḍito āyasmā citto hatthisāriputto.
segs.e: “Venerable, please don’t rebuke Citta Hatthisāriputta. He is astute,

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā citto hatthisāriputto therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ abhidhammakathaṁ kathetun”ti.
segs.e: and quite capable of talking about the teachings with the senior mendicants.”

segs.p: “Dujjānaṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso, parassa cetopariyāyaṁ ajānantehi.
segs.e: “It’s not easy to know this, reverends, for those who don’t encompass another’s mind.

segs.p: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo tāvadeva soratasorato hoti, nivātanivāto hoti, upasantupasanto hoti, yāva satthāraṁ upanissāya viharati aññataraṁ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṁ sabrahmacāriṁ.
segs.e: Take an individual who is the gentlest of the gentle, the most placid of the placid, the calmest of the calm, so long as they live relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role.

segs.p: Yato ca kho so vapakassateva satthārā, vapakassati garuṭṭhāniyehi sabrahmacārīhi, so saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi raññā rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi.
segs.e: But when they’re separated from the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role, they mix closely with monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; with rulers and their chief ministers, and with monastics of other religions and their disciples.

segs.p: Tassa saṁsaṭṭhassa vissatthassa pākatassa bhassamanuyuttassa viharato rāgo cittaṁ anuddhaṁseti.
segs.e: As they mix closely, they become familiar and loose, spending time chatting, and so lust infects their mind.

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, goṇo kiṭṭhādo dāmena vā baddho vaje vā oruddho.
segs.e: Suppose an ox fond of crops was tied up or shut in a pen.

segs.p: Yo nu kho, āvuso, evaṁ vadeyya: ‘na dānāyaṁ goṇo kiṭṭhādo punadeva kiṭṭhaṁ otarissatī’ti, sammā nu kho so, āvuso, vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would it be right to say that that ox will never again invade the crops?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “No it would not, reverend.

segs.p: “Ṭhānañhetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṁ so goṇo kiṭṭhādo dāmaṁ vā chetvā vajaṁ vā bhinditvā, atha punadeva kiṭṭhaṁ otareyyāti.
segs.e: For it’s quite possible that that ox will snap the ropes or break out of the pen, and then invade the crops.”

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, idhekacco puggalo tāvadeva soratasorato hoti, nivātanivāto hoti, upasantupasanto hoti yāva satthāraṁ upanissāya viharati aññataraṁ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṁ sabrahmacāriṁ.
segs.e: “In the same way, take an individual who is the gentlest of the gentle …

segs.p: Yato ca kho so vapakassateva satthārā, vapakassati garuṭṭhāniyehi sabrahmacārīhi, so saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi raññā rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi.
Tassa saṁsaṭṭhassa vissatthassa pākatassa bhassamanuyuttassa viharato rāgo cittaṁ anuddhaṁseti.
segs.e: As they mix closely, they become familiar and loose, spending time chatting, and so lust infects their mind.

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And take an individual who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … enters and remains in the first absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi paṭhamassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the first absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, cātumahāpathe thullaphusitako devo vassanto rajaṁ antaradhāpeyya, cikkhallaṁ pātukareyya.
segs.e: Suppose the heavens were raining heavily at the crossroads so that the dust vanished and mud appeared.

segs.p: Yo nu kho, āvuso, evaṁ vadeyya: ‘na dāni amusmiṁ cātumahāpathe punadeva rajo pātubhavissatī’ti, sammā nu kho so, āvuso, vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would it be right to say that now dust will never appear at this crossroad again?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “No it would not, reverend.

segs.p: “Ṭhānañhetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṁ amusmiṁ cātumahāpathe manussā vā atikkameyyuṁ, gopasū vā atikkameyyuṁ, vātātapo vā snehagataṁ pariyādiyeyya, atha punadeva rajo pātubhaveyyāti.
segs.e: For it is quite possible that people or cattle and so on will cross over the crossroad, or that the wind and sun will evaporate the moisture so that the dust appears again.”

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, idhekacco puggalo vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “In the same way, take an individual who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … enters and remains in the first absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi paṭhamassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the first absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And take an individual who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled … enters and remains in the second absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi dutiyassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the second absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre mahantaṁ taḷākaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose there was a large pond not far from a town or village.

segs.p: Tattha thullaphusitako devo vuṭṭho sippisambukampi sakkharakaṭhalampi antaradhāpeyya.
segs.e: After the heavens have rained heavily there, the clams and mussels, and pebbles and gravel would vanish.

segs.p: Yo nu kho, āvuso, evaṁ vadeyya: ‘na dāni amusmiṁ taḷāke punadeva sippisambukā vā sakkharakaṭhalā vā pātubhavissantī’ti, sammā nu kho so, āvuso, vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would it be right to say that now the clams and mussels, and pebbles and gravel will never appear here again?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “No it would not, reverend.

segs.p: “Ṭhānañhetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṁ amusmiṁ taḷāke manussā vā piveyyuṁ, gopasū vā piveyyuṁ, vātātapo vā snehagataṁ pariyādiyeyya, atha punadeva sippisambukāpi sakkharakaṭhalāpi pātubhaveyyunti.
segs.e: For it’s quite possible that people or cattle and so on will drink from the pond, or that the wind and sun will evaporate it so that the clams and mussels, and pebbles and gravel appear again.”

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, idhekacco puggalo vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “In the same way, take an individual who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled … enters and remains in the second absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi dutiyassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the second absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And take an individual who, with the fading away of rapture … enters and remains in the third absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi tatiyassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the third absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, purisaṁ paṇītabhojanaṁ bhuttāviṁ ābhidosikaṁ bhojanaṁ nacchādeyya.
segs.e: Suppose a person had finished a delicious meal. They’d have no appetite for leftovers.

segs.p: Yo nu kho, āvuso, evaṁ vadeyya: ‘na dāni amuṁ purisaṁ punadeva bhojanaṁ chādessatī’ti, sammā nu kho so, āvuso, vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would it be right to say that now food will never appeal to this person again?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “No it would not, reverend.

segs.p: “Ṭhānañhetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati, amuṁ purisaṁ paṇītabhojanaṁ bhuttāviṁ yāvassa sā ojā kāye ṭhassati tāva na aññaṁ bhojanaṁ chādessati.
segs.e: For it’s quite possible that other food won’t appeal to that person as long as the nourishment is still present.

segs.p: Yato ca khvassa sā ojā antaradhāyissati, atha punadeva taṁ bhojanaṁ chādeyyāti.
segs.e: But when the nourishment vanishes food will appeal again.”

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, idhekacco puggalo pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “In the same way, take an individual who, with the fading away of rapture … enters and remains in the third absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi tatiyassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the third absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Idha, panāvuso, ekacco puggalo sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And take an individual who, giving up pleasure and pain … enters and remains in the fourth absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi catutthassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the fourth absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, pabbatasaṅkhepe udakarahado nivāto vigataūmiko.
segs.e: Suppose that in a mountain glen there was a lake, placid and free of waves.

segs.p: Yo nu kho, āvuso, evaṁ vadeyya: ‘na dāni amusmiṁ udakarahade punadeva ūmi pātubhavissatī’ti, sammā nu kho so, āvuso, vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would it be right to say that now waves will never appear in this lake again?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “No it would not, reverend.

segs.p: “Ṭhānañhetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati, yā puratthimāya disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi. Sā tasmiṁ udakarahade ūmiṁ janeyya. Yā pacchimāya disāya āgaccheyya …pe… yā uttarāya disāya āgaccheyya … yā dakkhiṇāya disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi. Sā tasmiṁ udakarahade ūmiṁ janeyyāti.
segs.e: For it is quite possible that a violent storm could blow up out of the east, west, north, or south, and stir up waves in that lake.”

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, idhekacco puggalo sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “In the same way, take an individual who, giving up pleasure and pain … enters and remains in the fourth absorption.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi catutthassa jhānassā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi …pe…
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the fourth absorption!’ they mix closely with monks …

segs.p: sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Idha, panāvuso, ekacco puggalo sabbanimittānaṁ amanasikārā animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And take an individual who, not focusing on any signs, enters and remains in the signless immersion of the heart.

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi animittassa cetosamādhissā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi raññā rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi.
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I get the signless immersion of the heart!’ they mix closely with monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; with rulers and their chief ministers, and with monastics of other religions and their disciples.

segs.p: Tassa saṁsaṭṭhassa vissatthassa pākatassa bhassamanuyuttassa viharato rāgo cittaṁ anuddhaṁseti.
segs.e: As they mix closely, they become familiar and loose, spending time chatting, and so lust infects their mind.

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rājā vā rājamahāmatto vā caturaṅginiyā senāya addhānamaggappaṭipanno aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe ekarattiṁ vāsaṁ upagaccheyya.
segs.e: Suppose a ruler or their chief minister, while walking along the road with an army of four divisions, was to arrive at a forest grove where they set up camp for the night.

segs.p: Tatra hatthisaddena assasaddena rathasaddena pattisaddena bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddena cīrikasaddo antaradhāyeyya.
segs.e: There, because of the noise of the elephants, horses, chariots, soldiers, and the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals, the chirping of crickets would vanish.

segs.p: Yo nu kho, āvuso, evaṁ vadeyya: ‘na dāni amusmiṁ vanasaṇḍe punadeva cīrikasaddo pātubhavissatī’ti, sammā nu kho so, āvuso, vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would it be right to say that now the chirping of crickets will never be heard in this woodland grove again?”

segs.p: “No hidaṁ, āvuso”.
segs.e: “No it would not, reverend.

segs.p: “Ṭhānañhetaṁ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṁ so rājā vā rājamahāmatto vā tamhā vanasaṇḍā pakkameyya, atha punadeva cīrikasaddo pātubhaveyyāti.
segs.e: For it is quite possible that the ruler or their chief minister will leave that woodland grove so that the chirping of crickets will be heard there again.”

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, idhekacco puggalo sabbanimittānaṁ amanasikārā animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “In the same way, take an individual who, not focusing on any signs, enters and remains in the signless immersion of the heart …

segs.p: So ‘lābhimhi animittassa cetosamādhissā’ti saṁsaṭṭho viharati bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi raññā rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi.
Tassa saṁsaṭṭhassa vissatthassa pākatassa bhassamanuyuttassa viharato rāgo cittaṁ anuddhaṁseti.
So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattatī”ti.
segs.e: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā citto hatthisāriputto aparena samayena sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: Then after some time Venerable Citta Hatthisāriputta resigned the training and returned to a lesser life.

segs.p: Atha kho cittassa hatthisāriputtassa sahāyakā bhikkhū yenāyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then the mendicants who were his companions went up to Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita and said,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho āyasmatā mahākoṭṭhikena citto hatthisāriputto cetasā ceto paricca vidito:
segs.e: “Did Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita encompass Citta Hatthisāriputta’s mind and know that

segs.p: ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṁ citto hatthisāriputto lābhī, atha ca pana sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatī’ti;
segs.e: he had gained this and that meditative attainments, yet he would still resign the training and return to a lesser life?

segs.p: udāhu devatā etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ:
segs.e: Or did deities tell you about it?”

segs.p: ‘citto, bhante, hatthisāriputto imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṁ lābhī, atha ca pana sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatī’”ti?
“Cetasā ceto paricca vidito me, āvuso:
segs.e: “Reverends, I encompassed his mind and knew this.

segs.p: ‘citto hatthisāriputto imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṁ lābhī, atha ca pana sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatī’ti.
Devatāpi me etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ:
segs.e: And deities also told me.”

segs.p: ‘citto, bhante, hatthisāriputto imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṁ lābhī, atha ca pana sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatī’”ti.

Atha kho cittassa hatthisāriputtassa sahāyakā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then the mendicants who were Citta Hatthisāriputta’s companions went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “citto, bhante, hatthisāriputto imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṁ lābhī, atha ca pana sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattatī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Citta Hatthisāriputta, who had gained this and that meditative attainments, has still resigned the training and returned to a lesser life.”

segs.p: “Na, bhikkhave, citto ciraṁ sarissati nekkhammassā”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, soon Citta will remember renunciation.”

segs.p: Atha kho citto hatthisāriputto nacirasseva kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbaji.
segs.e: And not long after Citta Hatthisāriputta shaved off his hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā citto hatthisāriputto eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Citta Hatthisāriputta, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā citto hatthisāriputto arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Citta Hatthisāriputta became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.61
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.61

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Majjhesutta
segs.e: In the Middle

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulānaṁ therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṁ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time, after the meal, on return from almsround, several senior mendicants sat together in the pavilion and this discussion came up among them,

segs.p: “vuttamidaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā pārāyane metteyyapañhe:
segs.e: “Reverends, this was said by the Buddha in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Metteyya’:

segs.p: ‘Yo ubhonte viditvāna,
segs.e: ‘The thoughtful one, knowing both ends,

segs.p: majjhe mantā na lippati;
segs.e: is not stuck in the middle.

segs.p: Taṁ brūmi mahāpurisoti,
segs.e: He is a great man, I declare;

segs.p: sodha sibbinimaccagā’”ti.
segs.e: he has escaped the seamstress here.’

segs.p: “Katamo nu kho, āvuso, eko anto, katamo dutiyo anto, kiṁ majjhe, kā sibbinī”ti?
segs.e: But what is one end? What’s the second end? What’s the middle? And who is the seamstress?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “phasso kho, āvuso, eko anto, phassasamudayo dutiyo anto, phassanirodho majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “Contact, reverends, is one end. The origin of contact is the second end. The cessation of contact is the middle. And craving is the seamstress,

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
segs.e: for craving weaves one to being regenerated in one state of existence or another.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows what should be directly known and completely understands what should be completely understood. Knowing and understanding thus they make an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “atītaṁ kho, āvuso, eko anto, anāgataṁ dutiyo anto, paccuppannaṁ majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “The past, reverends, is one end. The future is the second end. The present is the middle. And craving is the seamstress …

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto, pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows … an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “sukhā, āvuso, vedanā eko anto, dukkhā vedanā dutiyo anto, adukkhamasukhā vedanā majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “Pleasant feeling, reverends, is one end. Painful feeling is the second end. Neutral feeling is the middle. And craving is the seamstress …

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
