Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto, pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows … an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “nāmaṁ kho, āvuso, eko anto, rūpaṁ dutiyo anto, viññāṇaṁ majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “Name, reverends, is one end. Form is the second end. Consciousness is the middle. And craving is the seamstress …

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows … an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “cha kho, āvuso, ajjhattikāni āyatanāni eko anto, cha bāhirāni āyatanāni dutiyo anto, viññāṇaṁ majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “The six interior sense fields, reverends, are one end. The six exterior sense fields are the second end. Consciousness is the middle. And craving is the seamstress …

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows … an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “sakkāyo kho, āvuso, eko anto, sakkāyasamudayo dutiyo anto, sakkāyanirodho majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “Substantial reality, reverends, is one end. The origin of substantial reality is the second end. The cessation of substantial reality is the middle. And craving is the seamstress,

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
segs.e: for craving weaves one to being regenerated in one state of existence or another.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows what should be directly known and completely understands what should be completely understood. Knowing and understanding thus they make an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu there bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the senior mendicants:

segs.p: “byākataṁ kho, āvuso, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ.
segs.e: “Each of us has spoken from the heart.

segs.p: Āyāmāvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocessāma.
segs.e: Come, reverends, let’s go to the Buddha, and inform him about this.

segs.p: Yathā no bhagavā byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā”ti.
segs.e: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho therā bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” those senior mendicants replied.

segs.p: Atha kho therā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: Then those senior mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho therā bhikkhū yāvatako ahosi sabbeheva saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo, taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesuṁ.
segs.e: and informed the Buddha of all they had discussed. They asked,

segs.p: “Kassa nu kho, bhante, subhāsitan”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, who has spoken well?”

segs.p: “Sabbesaṁ vo, bhikkhave, subhāsitaṁ pariyāyena, api ca yaṁ mayā sandhāya bhāsitaṁ pārāyane metteyyapañhe:
segs.e: “Mendicants, you’ve all spoken well in a way. However, this is what I was referring to in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Metteyya’ when I said:

segs.p: ‘Yo ubhonte viditvāna,
segs.e: ‘The thoughtful one, knowing both ends,

segs.p: majjhe mantā na lippati;
segs.e: is not stuck in the middle.

segs.p: Taṁ brūmi mahāpurisoti,
segs.e: He is a great man, I declare;

segs.p: sodha sibbinimaccagā’ti.
segs.e: he has escaped the seamstress here.’

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho therā bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “phasso kho, bhikkhave, eko anto, phassasamudayo dutiyo anto, phassanirodho majjhe, taṇhā sibbinī;
segs.e: “Contact, mendicants, is one end. The origin of contact is the second end. The cessation of contact is the middle. And craving is the seamstress,

segs.p: taṇhā hi naṁ sibbati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
segs.e: for craving weaves one to being regenerated in one state of existence or another.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānāti, pariññeyyaṁ parijānāti, abhiññeyyaṁ abhijānanto pariññeyyaṁ parijānanto diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant directly knows what should be directly known and completely understands what should be completely understood. Knowing and understanding thus they make an end of suffering in this very life.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.62
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.62

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Purisindriyañāṇasutta
segs.e: Knowledge of the Faculties of Persons

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena daṇḍakappakaṁ nāma kosalānaṁ nigamo tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a town of the Kosalans named Daṇḍakappaka.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: The Buddha left the road and sat at the root of a tree on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Te ca bhikkhū daṇḍakappakaṁ pavisiṁsu āvasathaṁ pariyesituṁ.
segs.e: The mendicants entered Daṇḍakappaka to look for a guest house.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ yena aciravatī nadī tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṁ.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda together with several mendicants went to the Aciravatī River to bathe.

segs.p: Aciravatiyā nadiyā gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno.
segs.e: When he had bathed and emerged from the water he stood in one robe drying his limbs.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a certain mendicant went up to Venerable Ānanda, and said to him,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso ānanda, sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā nu kho devadatto bhagavatā byākato:
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, when the Buddha declared that Devadatta was

segs.p: ‘āpāyiko devadatto nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho’ti, udāhu kenacideva pariyāyenāti?
segs.e: going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable, did he do so after wholeheartedly deliberating, or was this just a way of speaking?”

segs.p: Evaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā byākatan”ti.
segs.e: “You’re right, reverend, that’s how the Buddha declared it.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ yena aciravatī nadī tenupasaṅkamiṁ gattāni parisiñcituṁ.
Aciravatiyā nadiyā gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsiṁ gattāni pubbāpayamāno.
Atha kho, bhante, aññataro bhikkhu yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ etadavoca:
‘kiṁ nu kho, āvuso ānanda, sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā nu kho devadatto bhagavatā byākato—
āpāyiko devadatto nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekicchoti, udāhu kenacideva pariyāyenā’ti?
Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavocaṁ:
‘evaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā byākatan’”ti.
“So vā kho, ānanda, bhikkhu navo bhavissati acirapabbajito, thero vā pana bālo abyatto.
segs.e: “Ānanda, that mendicant must be junior, recently gone forth, or else a foolish, incompetent senior mendicant.

segs.p: Kathañhi nāma yaṁ mayā ekaṁsena byākataṁ tattha dvejjhaṁ āpajjissati.
segs.e: How on earth can he take something that I have declared categorically to be ambiguous?

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, ānanda, aññaṁ ekapuggalampi samanupassāmi, yo evaṁ mayā sabbaṁ cetaso samannāharitvā byākato, yathayidaṁ devadatto.
segs.e: I do not see a single other individual about whom I have given such whole-hearted deliberation before making a declaration as I did in the case of Devadatta.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañcāhaṁ, ānanda, devadattassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattampi sukkadhammaṁ addasaṁ;
segs.e: As long as I saw even a fraction of a hair’s tip of goodness in Devadatta

segs.p: neva tāvāhaṁ devadattaṁ byākāsiṁ:
segs.e: I did not declare that he was

segs.p: ‘āpāyiko devadatto nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho’ti.
segs.e: going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable.

segs.p: Yato ca kho ahaṁ, ānanda, devadattassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattampi sukkadhammaṁ na addasaṁ;
segs.e: But when I saw that there was not even a fraction of a hair’s tip of goodness in Devadatta

segs.p: athāhaṁ devadattaṁ byākāsiṁ:
segs.e: I declared that he was

segs.p: ‘āpāyiko devadatto nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho’ti.
segs.e: going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, gūthakūpo sādhikaporiso pūro gūthassa samatittiko.
segs.e: Suppose there was a sewer deeper than a man’s height, full to the brim with feces,

segs.p: Tatra puriso sasīsako nimuggo assa.
segs.e: and someone was sunk into it over their head.

segs.p: Tassa kocideva puriso uppajjeyya atthakāmo hitakāmo yogakkhemakāmo tamhā gūthakūpā uddharitukāmo.
segs.e: Then along comes a person who wants to help make them safe, who wants to lift them out of that sewer.

segs.p: So taṁ gūthakūpaṁ samantānuparigacchanto neva passeyya tassa purisassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattampi gūthena amakkhitaṁ, yattha taṁ gahetvā uddhareyya.
segs.e: But circling all around the sewer they couldn’t see even a fraction of a hair’s tip of that person that was not smeared with feces.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, yato devadattassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattampi sukkadhammaṁ na addasaṁ;
segs.e: In the same way, when I saw that there was not even a fraction of a hair’s tip of goodness in Devadatta

segs.p: athāhaṁ devadattaṁ byākāsiṁ:
segs.e: I declared that he was

segs.p: ‘āpāyiko devadatto nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho’ti.
segs.e: going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable.

segs.p: Sace tumhe, ānanda, suṇeyyātha tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇāni vibhajissāmī”ti?
segs.e: If you would all listen, Ānanda, I will analyze the Realized One’s knowledges of the faculties of persons.”

segs.p: “Etassa, bhagavā, kālo; etassa, sugata, kālo
segs.e: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

segs.p: yaṁ bhagavā purisindriyañāṇāni vibhajeyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: Let the Buddha analyze the faculties of persons. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tenahānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, Ānanda, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, ānanda, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “Ānanda, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa kusalā dhammā antarahitā, akusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
segs.e: ‘The skillful qualities of this individual have vanished, but the unskillful qualities are still present.

segs.p: Atthi ca khvassa kusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tamhā tassa kusalā kusalaṁ pātubhavissati.
segs.e: Nevertheless, their skillful root is unbroken, and from that the skillful will appear.

segs.p: Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ aparihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: So this individual is not liable to decline in the future.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, bījāni akhaṇḍāni apūtīni avātātapahatāni sāradāni sukhasayitāni sukhette suparikammakatāya bhūmiyā nikkhittāni.
segs.e: Suppose some seeds were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. And they were sown in a well-prepared, productive field.

segs.p: Jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, imāni bījāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissantī”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t you know that those seeds would grow, increase, and mature?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, idhekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand …

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
‘imassa kho puggalassa kusalā dhammā antarahitā, akusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
Atthi ca khvassa kusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tamhā tassa kusalā kusalaṁ pātubhavissati.
Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ aparihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: This individual is not liable to decline in the future …

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisapuggalo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
segs.e: This is how another individual is known to the Realized One by encompassing their mind.

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇaṁ cetasā ceto paricca viditaṁ hoti.
segs.e: And this is how the Realized One knows a person’s faculties by encompassing their mind.

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa āyatiṁ dhammasamuppādo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
segs.e: And this is how the Realized One knows the future origination of a person’s qualities by encompassing their mind.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, ānanda, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: When I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa akusalā dhammā antarahitā, kusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
segs.e: ‘The unskillful qualities of this individual have vanished, but the skillful qualities are still present.

segs.p: Atthi ca khvassa akusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tamhā tassa akusalā akusalaṁ pātubhavissati.
segs.e: Nevertheless, their unskillful root is unbroken, and from that the unskillful will appear.

segs.p: Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ parihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: So this individual is still liable to decline in the future.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, bījāni akhaṇḍāni apūtīni avātātapahatāni sāradāni sukhasayitāni puthusilāya nikkhittāni.
segs.e: Suppose some seeds were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. And they were sown on a broad rock.

segs.p: Jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, nayimāni bījāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissantī”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t you know that those seeds would not grow, increase, and mature?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, idhekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand …

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
‘imassa kho puggalassa akusalā dhammā antarahitā, kusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
Atthi ca khvassa akusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tamhā tassa akusalā akusalaṁ pātubhavissati.
Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ parihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: This individual is still liable to decline in the future …

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisapuggalo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
segs.e: This is how another individual is known to the Realized One …

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇaṁ cetasā ceto paricca viditaṁ hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa āyatiṁ dhammasamuppādo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
Idha panāhaṁ, ānanda, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: When I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:

segs.p: ‘natthi imassa puggalassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattopi sukko dhammo, samannāgatoyaṁ puggalo ekantakāḷakehi akusalehi dhammehi, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This individual has not even a fraction of a hair’s tip of goodness. They have absolutely dark, unskillful qualities. When their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, bījāni khaṇḍāni pūtīni vātātapahatāni sukhette suparikammakatāya bhūmiyā nikkhittāni.
segs.e: Suppose some seeds were broken, spoiled, weather-damaged. And they were sown in a well-prepared, productive field.

segs.p: Jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, nayimāni bījāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissantī”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t you know that those seeds would not grow, increase, and mature?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, idhekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand …

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:

‘natthi imassa puggalassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattopi sukko dhammo, samannāgatoyaṁ puggalo ekantakāḷakehi akusalehi dhammehi, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This individual has not even a fraction of a hair’s tip of goodness. They have absolutely dark, unskillful qualities. When their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’ …”

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisapuggalo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇaṁ cetasā ceto paricca viditaṁ hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa āyatiṁ dhammasamuppādo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hotī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “sakkā nu kho, bhante, imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ aparepi tayo puggalā sappaṭibhāgā paññāpetun”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, can you describe three other individuals who share a portion of these three?”

segs.p: “Sakkā, ānandā”ti bhagavā avoca:
segs.e: “I can, Ānanda,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: “idhāhaṁ, ānanda, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “Ānanda, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa kusalā dhammā antarahitā, akusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
segs.e: ‘The skillful qualities of this individual have vanished, but the unskillful qualities are still present.

segs.p: Atthi ca khvassa kusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tampi sabbena sabbaṁ samugghātaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Nevertheless, their skillful root is unbroken, but it’s about to be totally destroyed.

segs.p: Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ parihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: So this individual is still liable to decline in the future.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, aṅgārāni ādittāni sampajjalitāni sajotibhūtāni puthusilāya nikkhittāni.
segs.e: Suppose there were some burning coals, blazing and glowing, placed on a broad rock.

segs.p: Jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, nayimāni aṅgārāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissantī”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t you know that those coals would not grow, increase, and spread?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi vā pana, ānanda, sāyanhasamayaṁ sūriye ogacchante, jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, āloko antaradhāyissati andhakāro pātubhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “Or suppose it’s the late afternoon and the sun was going down. Wouldn’t you know that the light was about to vanish and darkness appear?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi vā, panānanda, abhido addharattaṁ bhattakālasamaye, jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, āloko antarahito andhakāro pātubhūto”ti?
segs.e: “Or suppose that it’s nearly time for the midnight meal. Wouldn’t you know that the light had vanished and the darkness appeared?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, idhekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand …

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
‘imassa kho puggalassa kusalā dhammā antarahitā, akusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
Atthi ca khvassa kusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tampi sabbena sabbaṁ samugghātaṁ gacchati.
Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ parihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: This individual is still liable to decline in the future …

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisapuggalo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇaṁ cetasā ceto paricca viditaṁ hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa āyatiṁ dhammasamuppādo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
Idha panāhaṁ, ānanda, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: When I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa akusalā dhammā antarahitā, kusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
segs.e: ‘The unskillful qualities of this individual have vanished, but the skillful qualities are still present.

segs.p: Atthi ca khvassa akusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tampi sabbena sabbaṁ samugghātaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Nevertheless, their unskillful root is unbroken, but it’s about to be totally destroyed.

segs.p: Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ aparihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: So this individual is not liable to decline in the future.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, aṅgārāni ādittāni sampajjalitāni sajotibhūtāni sukkhe tiṇapuñje vā kaṭṭhapuñje vā nikkhittāni.
segs.e: Suppose there were some burning coals, blazing and glowing, placed on a pile of grass or timber.

segs.p: Jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, imāni aṅgārāni vuḍḍhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissantī”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t you know that those coals would grow, increase, and spread?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi vā panānanda, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ sūriye uggacchante, jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, andhakāro antaradhāyissati, āloko pātubhavissatī”ti?
segs.e: “Or suppose it’s the crack of dawn and the sun is rising. Wouldn’t you know that the dark will vanish and the light appear?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi vā panānanda, abhido majjhanhike bhattakālasamaye, jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, andhakāro antarahito āloko pātubhūto”ti?
segs.e: “Or suppose that it’s nearly time for the midday meal. Wouldn’t you know that the dark had vanished and the light appeared?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, idhekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand …

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
‘imassa kho puggalassa akusalā dhammā antarahitā, kusalā dhammā sammukhībhūtā.
Atthi ca khvassa akusalamūlaṁ asamucchinnaṁ, tampi sabbena sabbaṁ samugghātaṁ gacchati.
Evamayaṁ puggalo āyatiṁ aparihānadhammo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: This individual is not liable to decline in the future …

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisapuggalo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇaṁ cetasā ceto paricca viditaṁ hoti.
Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa āyatiṁ dhammasamuppādo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
Idha panāhaṁ, ānanda, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: When I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:

segs.p: ‘natthi imassa puggalassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattopi akusalo dhammo, samannāgatoyaṁ puggalo ekantasukkehi anavajjehi dhammehi, diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This individual has not even a fraction of a hair’s tip of unskillful qualities. They have absolutely bright, blameless qualities. They will become extinguished in this very life.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, aṅgārāni sītāni nibbutāni sukkhe tiṇapuñje vā kaṭṭhapuñje vā nikkhittāni.
segs.e: Suppose there were some cool, quenched coals, placed on a pile of grass or timber.

segs.p: Jāneyyāsi tvaṁ, ānanda, nayimāni aṅgārāni vuḍḍhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissantī”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t you know that those coals would not grow, increase, and spread?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, ānanda, idhekaccaṁ puggalaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand …

segs.p: ‘imassa kho puggalassa vijjamānā kusalāpi dhammā akusalāpi dhammā’ti.
Tamenaṁ aparena samayena evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
‘natthi imassa puggalassa vālaggakoṭinittudanamattopi akusalo dhammo, samannāgatoyaṁ puggalo ekantasukkehi anavajjehi dhammehi, diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This individual has not even a fraction of a hair’s tip of unskillful qualities. They have absolutely bright, blameless qualities. They will become extinguished in this very life.’

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisapuggalo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
segs.e: This is how another individual is known to the Realized One by encompassing their mind.

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa purisindriyañāṇaṁ cetasā ceto paricca viditaṁ hoti.
segs.e: And this is how the Realized One knows a person’s faculties by encompassing their mind.

segs.p: Evampi kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa āyatiṁ dhammasamuppādo cetasā ceto paricca vidito hoti.
segs.e: And this is how the Realized One knows the future origination of a person’s qualities by encompassing their mind.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, ye te purimā tayo puggalā tesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ eko aparihānadhammo, eko parihānadhammo, eko āpāyiko nerayiko.
segs.e: And so, Ānanda, of the first three individuals one is not liable to decline, one is liable to decline, and one is bound for a place of loss, hell.

segs.p: Tatrānanda, yeme pacchimā tayo puggalā imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ eko parihānadhammo, eko aparihānadhammo, eko parinibbānadhammo”ti.
segs.e: And of the second three individuals, one is liable to decline, one is not liable to decline, and one is bound to become extinguished.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.63
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.63

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Nibbedhikasutta
segs.e: Penetrative

segs.p: “Nibbedhikapariyāyaṁ vo, bhikkhave, dhammapariyāyaṁ desessāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you a penetrative exposition of the teaching.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Katamo ca so, bhikkhave, nibbedhikapariyāyo dhammapariyāyo?
segs.e: “Mendicants, what is the penetrative exposition of the teaching?

segs.p: Kāmā, bhikkhave, veditabbā, kāmānaṁ nidānasambhavo veditabbo, kāmānaṁ vemattatā veditabbā, kāmānaṁ vipāko veditabbo, kāmanirodho veditabbo, kāmanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā.
segs.e: Sensual pleasures should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.

segs.p: Vedanā, bhikkhave, veditabbā, vedanānaṁ nidānasambhavo veditabbo, vedanānaṁ vemattatā veditabbā, vedanānaṁ vipāko veditabbo, vedanānirodho veditabbo, vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā.
segs.e: Feelings should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.

segs.p: Saññā, bhikkhave, veditabbā, saññānaṁ nidānasambhavo veditabbo, saññānaṁ vemattatā veditabbā, saññānaṁ vipāko veditabbo, saññānirodho veditabbo, saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā.
segs.e: Perceptions should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.

segs.p: Āsavā, bhikkhave, veditabbā, āsavānaṁ nidānasambhavo veditabbo, āsavānaṁ vemattatā veditabbā, āsavānaṁ vipāko veditabbo, āsavanirodho veditabbo, āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā.
segs.e: Defilements should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.

segs.p: Kammaṁ, bhikkhave, veditabbaṁ, kammānaṁ nidānasambhavo veditabbo, kammānaṁ vemattatā veditabbā, kammānaṁ vipāko veditabbo, kammanirodho veditabbo, kammanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā.
segs.e: Deeds should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.

segs.p: Dukkhaṁ, bhikkhave, veditabbaṁ, dukkhassa nidānasambhavo veditabbo, dukkhassa vemattatā veditabbā, dukkhassa vipāko veditabbo, dukkhanirodho veditabbo, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā.
segs.e: Suffering should be known. And its source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation should be known.

segs.p: ‘Kāmā, bhikkhave, veditabbā, kāmānaṁ nidānasambhavo veditabbo, kāmānaṁ vemattatā veditabbā, kāmānaṁ vipāko veditabbo, kāmanirodho veditabbo, kāmanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbā’ti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’ That’s what I said,

segs.p: Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: but why did I say it?

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā—
segs.e: There are these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā,
segs.e: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: sotaviññeyyā saddā …
segs.e: Sounds known by the ear …

segs.p: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
segs.e: Smells known by the nose …

segs.p: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
segs.e: Tastes known by the tongue …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
segs.e: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

segs.p: Api ca kho, bhikkhave, nete kāmā kāmaguṇā nāmete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti—
segs.e: However, these are not sensual pleasures. In the training of the Noble One they’re called ‘kinds of sensual stimulation’.

segs.p: Saṅkapparāgo purisassa kāmo,
segs.e: Greedy intention is a person’s sensual pleasure.

segs.p: Nete kāmā yāni citrāni loke;
segs.e: The world’s pretty things aren’t sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Saṅkapparāgo purisassa kāmo,
segs.e: Greedy intention is a person’s sensual pleasure.

segs.p: Tiṭṭhanti citrāni tatheva loke;
segs.e: The world’s pretty things stay just as they are,

segs.p: Athettha dhīrā vinayanti chandanti.
segs.e: but the attentive remove desire for them.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, kāmānaṁ nidānasambhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Phasso, bhikkhave, kāmānaṁ nidānasambhavo.
segs.e: Contact is their source.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, kāmānaṁ vemattatā?
segs.e: And what is the diversity of sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Añño, bhikkhave, kāmo rūpesu, añño kāmo saddesu, añño kāmo gandhesu, añño kāmo rasesu, añño kāmo phoṭṭhabbesu.
segs.e: The sensual desire for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches are all different.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, kāmānaṁ vemattatā.
segs.e: This is called the diversity of sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, kāmānaṁ vipāko?
segs.e: And what is the result of sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, kāmayamāno tajjaṁ tajjaṁ attabhāvaṁ abhinibbatteti puññabhāgiyaṁ vā apuññabhāgiyaṁ vā, ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, kāmānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: When one who desires sensual pleasures generates a corresponding incarnation, partaking of either good or bad deeds—this is called the result of sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, kāmanirodho?
segs.e: And what is the cessation of sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Phassanirodho, bhikkhave, kāmanirodho.
segs.e: When contact ceases, sensual pleasures cease.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo kāmanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of sensual pleasures is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ kāme pajānāti, evaṁ kāmānaṁ nidānasambhavaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kāmānaṁ vemattataṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kāmānaṁ vipākaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kāmanirodhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kāmanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti, so imaṁ nibbedhikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pajānāti kāmanirodhaṁ.
segs.e: When a noble disciple understands sensual pleasures in this way—and understands their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation—they understand that this penetrative spiritual life is the cessation of sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Kāmā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… kāmanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti,
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Vedanā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti,
segs.e: ‘Feelings should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Tisso imā, bhikkhave, vedanā—
segs.e: There are these three feelings:

segs.p: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā.
segs.e: pleasant, painful, and neutral.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, vedanānaṁ nidānasambhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of feelings?

segs.p: Phasso, bhikkhave, vedanānaṁ nidānasambhavo.
segs.e: Contact is their source.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, vedanānaṁ vemattatā?
segs.e: And what is the diversity of feelings?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, sāmisā sukhā vedanā, atthi nirāmisā sukhā vedanā, atthi sāmisā dukkhā vedanā, atthi nirāmisā dukkhā vedanā, atthi sāmisā adukkhamasukhā vedanā, atthi nirāmisā adukkhamasukhā vedanā.
segs.e: There are pleasant feelings of the flesh, pleasant feelings not of the flesh, painful feelings of the flesh, painful feelings not of the flesh, neutral feelings of the flesh, and neutral feelings not of the flesh.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, vedanānaṁ vemattatā.
segs.e: This is called the disparity of feelings.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, vedanānaṁ vipāko?
segs.e: And what is the result of feelings?

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, vediyamāno tajjaṁ tajjaṁ attabhāvaṁ abhinibbatteti puññabhāgiyaṁ vā apuññabhāgiyaṁ vā,
segs.e: When one who feels generates a corresponding incarnation, partaking of either good or bad deeds—

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, vedanānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: this is called the result of feelings.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, vedanānirodho?
segs.e: And what is the cessation of feelings?

segs.p: Phassanirodho, bhikkhave, vedanānirodho.
segs.e: When contact ceases, feelings cease.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of feelings is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ vedanaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ vedanānaṁ nidānasambhavaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ vedanānaṁ vemattataṁ pajānāti, evaṁ vedanānaṁ vipākaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ vedanānirodhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ vedanānirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti. So imaṁ nibbedhikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pajānāti vedanānirodhaṁ.
segs.e: When a noble disciple understands feelings in this way … they understand that this penetrative spiritual life is the cessation of feelings.

segs.p: Vedanā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti,
segs.e: ‘Feelings should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Saññā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti,
segs.e: ‘Perceptions should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Chayimā, bhikkhave, saññā—
segs.e: There are these six perceptions:

segs.p: rūpasaññā, saddasaññā, gandhasaññā, rasasaññā, phoṭṭhabbasaññā, dhammasaññā.
segs.e: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, saññānaṁ nidānasambhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of perceptions?

segs.p: Phasso, bhikkhave, saññānaṁ nidānasambhavo.
segs.e: Contact is their source.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, saññānaṁ vemattatā?
segs.e: And what is the diversity of perceptions?

segs.p: Aññā, bhikkhave, saññā rūpesu, aññā saññā saddesu, aññā saññā gandhesu, aññā saññā rasesu, aññā saññā phoṭṭhabbesu, aññā saññā dhammesu.
segs.e: The perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas are all different.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, saññānaṁ vemattatā.
segs.e: This is called the diversity of perceptions.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, saññānaṁ vipāko?
segs.e: And what is the result of perceptions?

segs.p: Vohāravepakkaṁ, bhikkhave, saññaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: Communication is the result of perception, I say.

segs.p: Yathā yathā naṁ sañjānāti tathā tathā voharati, evaṁ saññī ahosinti.
segs.e: You communicate something in whatever manner you perceive it, saying ‘That’s what I perceived.’

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, saññānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: This is called the result of perceptions.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, saññānirodho?
segs.e: And what is the cessation of perception?

segs.p: Phassanirodho, bhikkhave, saññānirodho.
segs.e: When contact ceases, perception ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of perceptions is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ saññaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ saññānaṁ nidānasambhavaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ saññānaṁ vemattataṁ pajānāti, evaṁ saññānaṁ vipākaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ saññānirodhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ saññānirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti, so imaṁ nibbedhikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pajānāti saññānirodhaṁ.
segs.e: When a noble disciple understands perception in this way … they understand that this penetrative spiritual life is the cessation of perception.

segs.p: Saññā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti.
segs.e: ‘Perceptions should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: Iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Āsavā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti,
segs.e: ‘Defilements should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Tayome, bhikkhave, āsavā—
segs.e: There are these three defilements:

segs.p: kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, avijjāsavo.
segs.e: the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ nidānasambhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of defilements?

segs.p: Avijjā, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ nidānasambhavo.
segs.e: Ignorance is the source of defilements.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ vemattatā?
segs.e: And what is the disparity of defilements?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, āsavā nirayagamanīyā, atthi āsavā tiracchānayonigamanīyā, atthi āsavā pettivisayagamanīyā, atthi āsavā manussalokagamanīyā, atthi āsavā devalokagamanīyā.
segs.e: There are defilements that lead to rebirth in hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, the human world, and the world of the gods.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ vemattatā.
segs.e: This is called the disparity of defilements.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ vipāko?
segs.e: And what is the result of defilements?

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, avijjāgato tajjaṁ tajjaṁ attabhāvaṁ abhinibbatteti puññabhāgiyaṁ vā apuññabhāgiyaṁ vā, ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: When one who is ignorant generates a corresponding incarnation, partaking of either good or bad deeds—this is called the result of defilements.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, āsavanirodho?
segs.e: And what is the cessation of defilements?

segs.p: Avijjānirodho, bhikkhave, āsavanirodho.
segs.e: When ignorance ceases, defilements cease.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of defilements is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ āsave pajānāti, evaṁ āsavānaṁ nidānasambhavaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ āsavānaṁ vemattataṁ pajānāti, evaṁ āsavānaṁ vipākaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ āsavānaṁ nirodhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ āsavānaṁ nirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti, so imaṁ nibbedhikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pajānāti āsavanirodhaṁ.
segs.e: When a noble disciple understands defilements in this way … they understand that this penetrative spiritual life is the cessation of defilements.

segs.p: Āsavā, bhikkhave, veditabbā …pe… āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti.
segs.e: ‘Defilements should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: Iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Kammaṁ, bhikkhave, veditabbaṁ …pe… kammanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Deeds should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’ That’s what I said,

segs.p: Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: but why did I say it?

segs.p: Cetanāhaṁ, bhikkhave, kammaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: It is intention that I call deeds.

segs.p: Cetayitvā kammaṁ karoti—
segs.e: For after making a choice one acts

segs.p: kāyena vācāya manasā.
segs.e: by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ nidānasambhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of deeds?

segs.p: Phasso, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ nidānasambhavo.
segs.e: Contact is their source.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ vemattatā?
segs.e: And what is the disparity of deeds?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, kammaṁ nirayavedanīyaṁ, atthi kammaṁ tiracchānayonivedanīyaṁ, atthi kammaṁ pettivisayavedanīyaṁ, atthi kammaṁ manussalokavedanīyaṁ, atthi kammaṁ devalokavedanīyaṁ.
segs.e: There are deeds that lead to rebirth in hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, the human world, and the world of the gods.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ vemattatā.
segs.e: This is called the disparity of deeds.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ vipāko?
segs.e: And what is the result of deeds?

segs.p: Tividhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ vipākaṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: The result of deeds is threefold, I say:

segs.p: diṭṭheva dhamme, upapajje vā, apare vā pariyāye.
segs.e: in this very life, on rebirth in the next life, or at some later time.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, kammānaṁ vipāko.
segs.e: This is called the result of deeds.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, kammanirodho?
segs.e: And what is the cessation of deeds?

segs.p: Phassanirodho, bhikkhave, kammanirodho.
segs.e: When contact ceases, deeds cease.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo kammanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of deeds is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ kammaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kammānaṁ nidānasambhavaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kammānaṁ vemattataṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kammānaṁ vipākaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kammanirodhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ kammanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti, so imaṁ nibbedhikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pajānāti kammanirodhaṁ.
segs.e: When a noble disciple understands deeds in this way … they understand that this penetrative spiritual life is the cessation of deeds.

segs.p: Kammaṁ, bhikkhave, veditabbaṁ …pe… kammanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti,
segs.e: ‘Deeds should be known. And their source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation should be known.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Dukkhaṁ, bhikkhave, veditabbaṁ, dukkhassa nidānasambhavo veditabbo, dukkhassa vemattatā veditabbā, dukkhassa vipāko veditabbo, dukkhanirodho veditabbo, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti.
segs.e: ‘Suffering should be known. And its source, disparity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation should be known.’

segs.p: Iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ, kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, byādhipi dukkho, maraṇampi dukkhaṁ, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsāpi dukkhā, yampicchaṁ na labhati tampi dukkhaṁ, saṅkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā.
segs.e: Rebirth is suffering; old age is suffering; illness is suffering; death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are suffering; not getting what you wish for is suffering. In brief, the five grasping aggregates are suffering.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhassa nidānasambhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of suffering?

segs.p: Taṇhā, bhikkhave, dukkhassa nidānasambhavo.
segs.e: Craving is the source of suffering.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, dukkhassa vemattatā?
segs.e: And what is the disparity of suffering?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ adhimattaṁ, atthi parittaṁ, atthi dandhavirāgi, atthi khippavirāgi.
segs.e: There is suffering that is severe, mild, slow to fade, and quick to fade.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhassa vemattatā.
segs.e: This is called the disparity of suffering.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhassa vipāko?
segs.e: And what is the result of suffering?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco yena dukkhena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati, yena vā pana dukkhena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto bahiddhā pariyeṭṭhiṁ āpajjati:
segs.e: It’s when someone who is overcome and overwhelmed by suffering sorrows and wails and laments, beating their breast and falling into confusion. Or else, overcome by that suffering, they begin an external search, wondering:

segs.p: ‘ko ekapadaṁ dvipadaṁ jānāti imassa dukkhassa nirodhāyā’ti?
segs.e: ‘Who knows one or two phrases to stop this suffering?’

segs.p: Sammohavepakkaṁ vāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ vadāmi pariyeṭṭhivepakkaṁ vā.
segs.e: The result of suffering is either confusion or a search, I say.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhassa vipāko.
segs.e: This is called the result of suffering.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodho?
segs.e: And what is the cessation of suffering?

segs.p: Taṇhānirodho, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodho.
segs.e: When craving ceases, suffering ceases.

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo dukkhassa nirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The practice that leads to the cessation of suffering is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ dukkhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ dukkhassa nidānasambhavaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ dukkhassa vemattataṁ pajānāti, evaṁ dukkhassa vipākaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ dukkhanirodhaṁ pajānāti, evaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti, so imaṁ nibbedhikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pajānāti dukkhanirodhaṁ.
segs.e: When a noble disciple understands suffering in this way … they understand that this penetrative spiritual life is the cessation of suffering.

segs.p: Dukkhaṁ, bhikkhave, veditabbaṁ, dukkhassa nidānasambhavo veditabbo, dukkhassa vemattatā veditabbā, dukkhassa vipāko veditabbo, dukkhanirodho veditabbo, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā veditabbāti.
segs.e: ‘Suffering should be known. And its source, diversity, result, cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation should be known.’

segs.p: Iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho so, bhikkhave, nibbedhikapariyāyo dhammapariyāyo”ti.
segs.e: This is the penetrative exposition of the teaching.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.64
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.64

segs.p: 6. Mahāvagga
segs.e: 6. The Great Chapter

segs.p: Sīhanādasutta
segs.e: The Lion’s Roar

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the Realized One possesses six powers of a Realized One. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: Firstly, the Realized One truly understands the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Since he truly understands this, this is a power of the Realized One. Relying on this he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṁ kammasamādānānaṁ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Realized One truly understands the result of deeds undertaken in the past, future, and present in terms of grounds and causes.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṁ kammasamādānānaṁ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Since he truly understands this, this is a power of the Realized One. …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṁ saṅkilesaṁ vodānaṁ vuṭṭhānaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Realized One truly understands corruption, cleansing, and emergence regarding the absorptions, liberations, immersions, and attainments.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato …pe… idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Since he truly understands this, this is a power of the Realized One. …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgato anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ, dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Realized One recollects many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. He remembers: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so he recollects his many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ, dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Since he truly understands this, this is a power of the Realized One. …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, the Realized One sees sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. He understands how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Since he truly understands this, this is a power of the Realized One. …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgato āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Realized One has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And he lives having realized it with his own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Since he truly understands this, this is a power of the Realized One. Relying on this he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: These are the six powers of a Realized One that the Realized One possesses. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

segs.p: Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṁ ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṁ pucchanti.
segs.e: If others come to the Realized One and ask questions about his true knowledge of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible,

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ viditaṁ tathā tathā tesaṁ tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākaroti.
segs.e: the Realized One answers them in whatever manner he has truly known it.

segs.p: Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṁ kammasamādānānaṁ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṁ pucchanti.
segs.e: If others come to the Realized One and ask questions about his true knowledge of the result of deeds undertaken in the past, future, and present in terms of grounds and causes,

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṁ kammasamādānānaṁ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ viditaṁ tathā tathā tesaṁ tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṁ kammasamādānānaṁ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākaroti.
segs.e: the Realized One answers them in whatever manner he has truly known it.

segs.p: Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṁ jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṁ saṅkilesaṁ vodānaṁ vuṭṭhānaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṁ pucchanti.
segs.e: If others come to the Realized One and ask questions about his true knowledge of corruption, cleansing, and emergence regarding the absorptions, liberations, immersions, and attainments,

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṁ saṅkilesaṁ vodānaṁ vuṭṭhānaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ viditaṁ tathā tathā tesaṁ tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṁ saṅkilesaṁ vodānaṁ vuṭṭhānaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākaroti.
segs.e: the Realized One answers them in whatever manner he has truly known it.

segs.p: Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṁ pubbenivāsānussatiṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṁ pucchanti.
segs.e: If others come to the Realized One and ask questions about his true knowledge of recollection of past lives,

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa pubbenivāsānussatiṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ viditaṁ tathā tathā tesaṁ tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākaroti.
segs.e: the Realized One answers them in whatever manner he has truly known it.

segs.p: Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṁ sattānaṁ cutūpapātaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṁ pucchanti.
segs.e: If others come to the Realized One and ask questions about his true knowledge of passing away and rebirth of sentient beings,

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa sattānaṁ cutūpapātaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ viditaṁ tathā tathā tesaṁ tathāgato sattānaṁ cutūpapātaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākaroti.
segs.e: the Realized One answers them in whatever manner he has truly known it.

segs.p: Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṁ āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṁ pucchanti.
segs.e: If others come to the Realized One and ask questions about his true knowledge of the ending of defilements,

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ viditaṁ tathā tathā tesaṁ tathāgato āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇena pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākaroti.
segs.e: the Realized One answers them in whatever manner he has truly known it.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yampidaṁ ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ tampi samāhitassa vadāmi no asamāhitassa.
segs.e: And I say that true knowledge of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible is for those with immersion, not for those without immersion.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṁ kammasamādānānaṁ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ tampi samāhitassa vadāmi no asamāhitassa.
segs.e: And true knowledge of the result of deeds undertaken in the past, future, and present in terms of grounds and causes is for those with immersion, not for those without immersion.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṁ saṅkilesaṁ vodānaṁ vuṭṭhānaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ tampi samāhitassa vadāmi no asamāhitassa.
segs.e: And true knowledge of corruption, cleansing, and emergence regarding the absorptions, liberations, immersions, and attainments is for those with immersion, not for those without immersion.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ pubbenivāsānussatiṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ tampi samāhitassa vadāmi no asamāhitassa.
segs.e: And true knowledge of the recollection of past lives is for those with immersion, not for those without immersion.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ sattānaṁ cutūpapātaṁ yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ tampi samāhitassa vadāmi no asamāhitassa.
segs.e: And true knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of sentient beings is for those with immersion, not for those without immersion.

segs.p: Yampidaṁ āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… yathābhūtaṁ ñāṇaṁ tampi samāhitassa vadāmi no asamāhitassa.
segs.e: And true knowledge of the ending of defilements is for those with immersion, not for those without immersion.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, samādhi maggo, asamādhi kummaggo”ti.
segs.e: And so, mendicants, immersion is the path. No immersion is the wrong path.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Mahāvaggo chaṭṭho.
Tassuddānaṁ
Soṇo phagguno bhijāti,
āsavā dāruhatthi ca;
Majjhe ñāṇaṁ nibbedhikaṁ,
sīhanādoti te dasāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.65
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.65

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Anāgāmiphalasutta
segs.e: The Fruit of Non-Return

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo anāgāmiphalaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up six things you can’t realize the fruit of non-return.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Assaddhiyaṁ, ahirikaṁ, anottappaṁ, kosajjaṁ, muṭṭhassaccaṁ, duppaññataṁ—
segs.e: Lack of faith, conscience, and prudence; laziness, unmindfulness, and witlessness.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo anāgāmiphalaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six things you can’t realize the fruit of non-return.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo anāgāmiphalaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up six things you can realize the fruit of non-return.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Assaddhiyaṁ, ahirikaṁ, anottappaṁ, kosajjaṁ, muṭṭhassaccaṁ, duppaññataṁ—
segs.e: Lack of faith, conscience, and prudence; laziness, unmindfulness, and witlessness.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo anāgāmiphalaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six things you can realize the fruit of non-return.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.66
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.66

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Arahattasutta
segs.e: Perfection

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up six things you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Thinaṁ, middhaṁ, uddhaccaṁ, kukkuccaṁ, assaddhiyaṁ, pamādaṁ—
segs.e: Dullness, drowsiness, restlessness, remorse, lack of faith, and negligence.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six things you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up six things you can realize perfection.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Thinaṁ, middhaṁ, uddhaccaṁ, kukkuccaṁ, assaddhiyaṁ, pamādaṁ—
segs.e: Dullness, drowsiness, restlessness, remorse, lack of faith, and negligence.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six things you can realize perfection.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.67
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.67
