segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Mittasutta
segs.e: Friends

segs.p: “‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāpamitto pāpasahāyo pāpasampavaṅko, pāpamitte sevamāno bhajamāno payirupāsamāno, tesañca diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjamāno ābhisamācārikaṁ dhammaṁ paripūressatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible that a mendicant with bad friends, companions, and associates, while frequenting, accompanying, and attending, and following their example, will fulfill the practice dealing with the supplementary regulations.

segs.p: ‘Ābhisamācārikaṁ dhammaṁ aparipūretvā sekhaṁ dhammaṁ paripūressatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without fulfilling the practice dealing with supplementary regulations, it’s impossible to fulfill the practice of a trainee.

segs.p: ‘Sekhaṁ dhammaṁ aparipūretvā sīlāni paripūressatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without fulfilling the practice of a trainee, it’s impossible to fulfill ethics.

segs.p: ‘Sīlāni aparipūretvā kāmarāgaṁ vā rūparāgaṁ vā arūparāgaṁ vā pajahissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without fulfilling ethics, it’s impossible to give up sensual desire, or desire to be reborn in the realm of luminous form or in the formless realm.

segs.p: ‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko, kalyāṇamitte sevamāno bhajamāno payirupāsamāno, tesañca diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjamāno ābhisamācārikaṁ dhammaṁ paripūressatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s quite possible that a mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates, while frequenting, accompanying, and attending, and following their example, will fulfill the practice dealing with the supplementary regulations.

segs.p: ‘Ābhisamācārikaṁ dhammaṁ paripūretvā sekhaṁ dhammaṁ paripūressatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Having fulfilled the practice dealing with supplementary regulations, it’s possible to fulfill the practice of a trainee.

segs.p: ‘Sekhaṁ dhammaṁ paripūretvā sīlāni paripūressatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Having fulfilled the practice of a trainee, it’s possible to fulfill ethics.

segs.p: ‘Sīlāni paripūretvā kāmarāgaṁ vā rūparāgaṁ vā arūparāgaṁ vā pajahissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: Having fulfilled ethics, it’s possible to give up sensual desire, and desire to be reborn in the realm of luminous form and in the formless realm.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.68
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.68

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Saṅgaṇikārāmasutta
segs.e: Enjoying Company

segs.p: “‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅgaṇikārāmo saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ anuyutto, gaṇārāmo gaṇarato gaṇārāmataṁ anuyutto, eko paviveke abhiramissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible that a mendicant who enjoys company and groups, who loves them and likes to enjoy them, should take pleasure in being alone in seclusion.

segs.p: ‘Eko paviveke anabhiramanto cittassa nimittaṁ gahessatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without taking pleasure in being alone in seclusion, it’s impossible to learn the patterns of the mind.

segs.p: ‘Cittassa nimittaṁ agaṇhanto sammādiṭṭhiṁ paripūressatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without learning the mind’s character, it’s impossible to fulfill right view.

segs.p: ‘Sammādiṭṭhiṁ aparipūretvā sammāsamādhiṁ paripūressatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without fulfilling right view, it’s impossible to fulfill right immersion.

segs.p: ‘Sammāsamādhiṁ aparipūretvā saṁyojanāni pajahissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without fulfilling right immersion, it’s impossible to give up the fetters.

segs.p: ‘Saṁyojanāni appahāya nibbānaṁ sacchikarissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without giving up the fetters, it’s impossible to realize extinguishment.

segs.p: ‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na saṅgaṇikārāmo na saṅgaṇikarato na saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ anuyutto, na gaṇārāmo na gaṇarato na gaṇārāmataṁ anuyutto, eko paviveke abhiramissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s quite possible that a mendicant who doesn’t enjoy company and groups, who doesn’t love them and like to enjoy them, should take pleasure in being alone in seclusion.

segs.p: ‘Eko paviveke abhiramanto cittassa nimittaṁ gahessatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: For someone who takes pleasure in being alone in seclusion, it’s possible to learn the mind’s character.

segs.p: ‘Cittassa nimittaṁ gaṇhanto sammādiṭṭhiṁ paripūressatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: For someone who learns the mind’s character, it’s possible to fulfill right view.

segs.p: ‘Sammādiṭṭhiṁ paripūretvā sammāsamādhiṁ paripūressatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Having fulfilled right view, it’s possible to fulfill right immersion.

segs.p: ‘Sammāsamādhiṁ paripūretvā saṁyojanāni pajahissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Having fulfilled right immersion, it’s possible to give up the fetters.

segs.p: ‘Saṁyojanāni pahāya nibbānaṁ sacchikarissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: Having given up the fetters, it’s possible to realize extinguishment.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.69
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.69

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Devatāsutta
segs.e: A God

segs.p: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Sir, these six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā—
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training; being easy to admonish, and good friendship.

segs.p: ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.”

segs.p: Idamavoca sā devatā.
segs.e: That is what that deity said,

segs.p: Samanuñño satthā ahosi.
segs.e: and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho sā devatā “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then that deity, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Tonight, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and said to me:

segs.p: ‘chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, these six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā—
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training; being easy to admonish, and good friendship.

segs.p: ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
segs.e: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.’

segs.p: Idamavoca, bhikkhave, sā devatā.
segs.e: That is what that deity said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: “Sir, this is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu attanā ca satthugāravo hoti satthugāravatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant personally respects the Teacher and praises such respect.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na satthugāravā te ca satthugāravatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack such respect to respect the Teacher.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū satthugāravā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who respect the Teacher at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Attanā ca dhammagāravo hoti …
segs.e: They personally respect the teaching …

segs.p: saṅghagāravo hoti …
segs.e: They personally respect the Saṅgha …

segs.p: sikkhāgāravo hoti …
segs.e: They personally respect the training …

segs.p: suvaco hoti …
segs.e: They are personally easy to admonish …

segs.p: kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇamittatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: They personally have good friends, and praise such friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na kalyāṇamittā te ca kalyāṇamittatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack good friends to develop good friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū kalyāṇamittā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who have good friends at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”

segs.p: “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta.
segs.e: “Good, good, Sāriputta!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, sāriputta, imassa mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsi.
segs.e: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.

segs.p: Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca satthugāravo hoti satthugāravatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant personally respects the Teacher …

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na satthugāravā te ca satthugāravatāya samādapeti.
Ye caññe bhikkhū satthugāravā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Attanā ca dhammagāravo hoti …
segs.e: They personally respect the teaching …

segs.p: saṅghagāravo hoti …
segs.e: They personally respect the Saṅgha …

segs.p: sikkhāgāravo hoti …
segs.e: They personally respect the training …

segs.p: suvaco hoti …
segs.e: They are personally easy to admonish …

segs.p: kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇamittatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: They personally have good friends, and praise such friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na kalyāṇamittā te ca kalyāṇamittatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack good friends to develop good friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū kalyāṇamittā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who have good friends at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Imassa kho, sāriputta, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
segs.e: This is how to see the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.70
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.70

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Samādhisutta
segs.e: Immersion

segs.p: “‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na santena samādhinā na paṇītena na paṭippassaddhiladdhena na ekodibhāvādhigatena anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhavissati—ekopi hutvā bahudhā bhavissati, bahudhāpi hutvā eko bhavissati …pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vattessatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible that a mendicant without immersion that is peaceful, refined, tranquil, and unified will wield the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. They control the body as far as the realm of divinity.

segs.p: ‘Dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇissati—dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike cā’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s impossible that with clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they’ll hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

segs.p: ‘Parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānissati—
segs.e: It’s impossible that they’ll understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind,

segs.p: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānissati …pe…
segs.e: understanding mind with greed as ‘mind with greed’ …

segs.p: vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ cittanti pajānissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: and freed mind as ‘freed mind’.

segs.p: ‘Anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarissati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ, dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s impossible that they’ll recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: ‘Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passissati …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s impossible that with clairvoyance that is purified and surpasses the human, they’ll understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: ‘Āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s impossible that they’ll realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: ‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santena samādhinā paṇītena paṭippassaddhiladdhena ekodibhāvādhigatena anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhavissati …pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vattessatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: But it’s quite possible that a mendicant who has immersion that is peaceful, refined, tranquil, and unified will wield the many kinds of psychic power …

segs.p: ‘Dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇissati—dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike cā’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s possible that with clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they’ll hear both kinds of sounds …

segs.p: ‘Parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānissati—
segs.e: It’s possible that they’ll understand the minds of other beings …

segs.p: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānissati …pe…
vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ cittanti pajānissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
‘Anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarissati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ, dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s possible that they’ll recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: ‘Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passissati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s possible that with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they’ll understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: ‘Āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: It’s possible that they’ll realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.71
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.71

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Sakkhibhabbasutta
segs.e: Capable of Realizing

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṁ pāpuṇituṁ sati sati āyatane.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities is incapable of realizing anything that can be realized, since each and every one is within range.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘ime hānabhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ‘ime ṭhitibhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ‘ime visesabhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ‘ime nibbedhabhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, asakkaccakārī ca hoti, asappāyakārī ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t truly understand which qualities make things worse, which keep things steady, which lead to distinction, and which lead to penetration. And they don’t practice carefully or do what’s suitable.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṁ pāpuṇituṁ sati sati āyatane.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is incapable of realizing anything that can be realized, since each and every one is within range.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṁ pāpuṇituṁ sati sati āyatane.
segs.e: A mendicant with six qualities is capable of realizing anything that can be realized, since each and every one is within range.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘ime hānabhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ime ṭhitibhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ime visesabhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ime nibbedhabhāgiyā dhammā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, sakkaccakārī ca hoti, sappāyakārī ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands which qualities make things worse, which keep things steady, which lead to distinction, and which lead to penetration. And they practice carefully and do what’s suitable.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṁ pāpuṇituṁ sati sati āyatane”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is capable of realizing anything that can be realized, since each and every one is within range.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.72
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.72

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Balasutta
segs.e: Strength

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo samādhismiṁ balataṁ pāpuṇituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has six qualities can’t attain strength in immersion.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na samādhissa samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhissa ṭhitikusalo hoti, na samādhissa vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, asakkaccakārī ca hoti, asātaccakārī ca, asappāyakārī ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is not skilled in entering immersion, skilled in remaining in immersion, or skilled in emerging from immersion. And they don’t practice carefully and persistently, and they don’t do what’s suitable.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo samādhismiṁ balataṁ pāpuṇituṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these six qualities can’t attain strength in immersion.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo samādhismiṁ balataṁ pāpuṇituṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who has six qualities can attain strength in immersion.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samādhissa samāpattikusalo hoti, samādhissa ṭhitikusalo hoti, samādhissa vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, sakkaccakārī ca hoti, sātaccakārī ca, sappāyakārī ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is skilled in entering immersion, skilled in remaining in immersion, and skilled in emerging from immersion. And they practice carefully and persistently, and do what’s suitable.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo samādhismiṁ balataṁ pāpuṇitun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these six qualities can attain strength in immersion.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.73
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.73

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Paṭhamatajjhānasutta
segs.e: First Absorption (1st)

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up these six qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kāmacchandaṁ, byāpādaṁ, thinamiddhaṁ, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ, vicikicchaṁ.
segs.e: Desire for sensual pleasures, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

segs.p: Kāmesu kho panassa ādīnavo na yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭho hoti.
segs.e: And the drawbacks of sensual pleasures have not been truly seen clearly with right wisdom.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: But after giving up these six qualities you can enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kāmacchandaṁ, byāpādaṁ, thinamiddhaṁ, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ, vicikicchaṁ,
segs.e: Desire for sensual pleasures, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

segs.p: kāmesu kho panassa ādīnavo na yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭho hoti.
segs.e: And the drawbacks of sensual pleasures have been truly seen clearly with right wisdom.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharitun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six qualities you can enter and remain in the first absorption.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.74
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.74

segs.p: 7. Devatāvagga
segs.e: 7. A God

segs.p: Dutiyatajjhānasutta
segs.e: First Absorption (2nd)

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up these six qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kāmavitakkaṁ, byāpādavitakkaṁ, vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ, kāmasaññaṁ, byāpādasaññaṁ, vihiṁsāsaññaṁ—
segs.e: Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts; and sensual, malicious, and cruel perceptions.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: But after giving up these six qualities you can enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kāmavitakkaṁ, byāpādavitakkaṁ, vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ, kāmasaññaṁ, byāpādasaññaṁ, vihiṁsāsaññaṁ—
segs.e: Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts; and sensual, malicious, and cruel perceptions.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharitun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six qualities you can enter and remain in the first absorption.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.

Anāgāmi arahaṁ mittā,

Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.75
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.75

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Dukkhasutta
segs.e: Suffering

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has six qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kāmavitakkena, byāpādavitakkena, vihiṁsāvitakkena, kāmasaññāya, byāpādasaññāya, vihiṁsāsaññāya—
segs.e: Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts; and sensual, malicious, and cruel perceptions.

segs.p: imehi, kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these six qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: When a mendicant has six qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, or fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Nekkhammavitakkena, abyāpādavitakkena, avihiṁsāvitakkena, nekkhammasaññāya, abyāpādasaññāya, avihiṁsāsaññāya—
segs.e: Thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness. And perceptions of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.

segs.p: imehi, kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these six qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, or fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.76
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.76

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Arahattasutta
segs.e: Perfection

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up six things you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Mānaṁ, omānaṁ, atimānaṁ, adhimānaṁ, thambhaṁ, atinipātaṁ.
segs.e: Conceit, inferiority complex, superiority complex, overestimation, obstinacy, and groveling.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six qualities you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up six things you can realize perfection.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Mānaṁ, omānaṁ, atimānaṁ, adhimānaṁ, thambhaṁ, atinipātaṁ.
segs.e: Conceit, inferiority complex, superiority complex, overestimation, obstinacy, and groveling.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six things you can realize perfection.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.77
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.77

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Uttarimanussadhammasutta
segs.e: Superhuman States

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo uttari manussadhammaṁ alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up six qualities you can’t realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Muṭṭhassaccaṁ, asampajaññaṁ, indriyesu aguttadvārataṁ, bhojane amattaññutaṁ, kuhanaṁ, lapanaṁ.
segs.e: Lack of mindfulness and situational awareness, not guarding the sense doors, eating too much, fawning, and flattery.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo uttari manussadhammaṁ alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six qualities you can’t realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo uttari manussadhammaṁ alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: But after giving up six qualities you can realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Muṭṭhassaccaṁ, asampajaññaṁ, indriyesu aguttadvārataṁ, bhojane amattaññutaṁ, kuhanaṁ, lapanaṁ.
segs.e: Lack of mindfulness and situational awareness, not guarding the sense doors, eating too much, fawning, and flattery.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo uttari manussadhammaṁ alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six qualities you can realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.78
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.78

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Sukhasomanassasutta
segs.e: Joy and Happiness

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhasomanassabahulo viharati, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has six things they’re full of joy and happiness in this very life, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammārāmo hoti, bhāvanārāmo hoti, pahānārāmo hoti, pavivekārāmo hoti, abyāpajjhārāmo hoti, nippapañcārāmo hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant enjoys the teaching, meditation, giving up, seclusion, kindness, and non-proliferation.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu diṭṭheva dhamme sukhasomanassabahulo viharati, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāyā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these six things they’re full of joy and happiness in this very life, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.79
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.79

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Adhigamasutta
segs.e: Achievement

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has six qualities is unable to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na āyakusalo ca hoti, na apāyakusalo ca hoti, na upāyakusalo ca hoti, anadhigatānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ adhigamāya na chandaṁ janeti, adhigate kusale dhamme na ārakkhati, sātaccakiriyāya na sampādeti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is not skilled in progress, skilled in regress, or skilled in means. They don’t generate enthusiasm to achieve skillful qualities not yet achieved. They don’t protect skillful qualities they have achieved. And they don’t try to persist in the task.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these six qualities is unable to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who has six qualities is able to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āyakusalo ca hoti, apāyakusalo ca hoti, upāyakusalo ca hoti, anadhigatānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ adhigamāya chandaṁ janeti, adhigate kusale dhamme ārakkhati, sātaccakiriyāya sampādeti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is skilled in progress, skilled in regress, and skilled in means. They generate enthusiasm to achieve skillful qualities not yet achieved. They protect skillful qualities they have achieved. And they try to persist in the task.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these six qualities is able to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.80
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.80

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Mahantattasutta
segs.e: Greatness

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva mahantattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti dhammesu.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities soon acquires great and abundant good qualities.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ālokabahulo ca hoti yogabahulo ca vedabahulo ca asantuṭṭhibahulo ca anikkhittadhuro ca kusalesu dhammesu uttari ca patāreti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is full of light, full of practice, full of inspiration, and full of eagerness. They don’t slack off when it comes to developing skillful qualities. They reach further.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva mahantattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti dhammesū”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these six qualities soon acquires great and abundant good qualities.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.81
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.81

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Paṭhamanirayasutta
segs.e: Hell (1st)

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with six qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pāpiccho ca, micchādiṭṭhi ca.
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie. And they have corrupt wishes and wrong view.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with six qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, appiccho ca, sammādiṭṭhi ca.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, or lie. And they have few desires and right view.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.82
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.82

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Dutiyanirayasutta
segs.e: Hell (2nd)

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with six qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, luddho ca, pagabbho ca.
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie. And they’re greedy and rude.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with six qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, aluddho ca, appagabbho ca.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, or lie. And they’re not greedy or rude.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.83
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.83

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Aggadhammasutta
segs.e: The Best Thing

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo aggaṁ dhammaṁ arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities can’t realize the best thing, perfection.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto hoti, duppañño hoti, kāye ca jīvite ca sāpekkho hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, lazy, and witless. And they’re concerned with their body and their life.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo aggaṁ dhammaṁ arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities can’t realize the best thing, perfection.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo aggaṁ dhammaṁ arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with six qualities can realize the best thing, perfection.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho hoti, hirīmā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, paññavā hoti, kāye ca jīvite ca anapekkho hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, energetic, and wise. And they have no concern for their body and their life.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo aggaṁ dhammaṁ arahattaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities can realize the best thing, perfection.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.84
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.84

segs.p: 8. Arahattavagga
segs.e: 8. Perfection

segs.p: Rattidivasasutta
segs.e: Day and Night

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities can expect decline, not growth, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahiccho hoti, vighātavā, asantuṭṭho, itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, assaddho hoti, dussīlo hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, duppañño hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has many desires—they’re frustrated and not content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they’re faithless, unethical, unmindful, and witless.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities can expect decline, not growth, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni.
segs.e: A mendicant with six qualities can expect growth, not decline, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na mahiccho hoti, avighātavā, santuṭṭho, itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, saddho hoti, sīlavā hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, satimā hoti, paññavā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t have many desires—they’re not frustrated but content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they’re faithful, ethical, mindful, and wise.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, kusalesu dhammesu no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities can expect growth, not decline, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Arahattavaggo aṭṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Dukkhaṁ arahattaṁ uttari ca,
Sukhaṁ adhigamena ca;
Mahantattaṁ dvayaṁ niraye,
Aggadhammañca rattiyoti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.85
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.85

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Sītibhāvasutta
segs.e: Coolness

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo anuttaraṁ sītibhāvaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities can’t realize supreme coolness.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ niggahetabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ na niggaṇhāti, yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ paggahetabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ na paggaṇhāti, yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ sampahaṁsitabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ na sampahaṁseti, yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ ajjhupekkhitabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ na ajjhupekkhati, hīnādhimuttiko ca hoti, sakkāyābhirato ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t keep their mind in check when they should. They don’t exert their mind when they should. They don’t encourage the mind when they should. They don’t watch over the mind with equanimity when they should. They have inferior convictions. They delight in substantial reality.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo anuttaraṁ sītibhāvaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities can’t realize supreme coolness.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anuttaraṁ sītibhāvaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with six qualities can realize supreme coolness.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ niggahetabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ niggaṇhāti, yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ paggahetabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ paggaṇhāti, yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ sampahaṁsitabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ sampahaṁseti, yasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ ajjhupekkhitabbaṁ tasmiṁ samaye cittaṁ ajjhupekkhati, paṇītādhimuttiko ca hoti nibbānābhirato ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant keeps their mind in check when they should. They exert their mind when they should. They encourage the mind when they should. They watch over the mind with equanimity when they should. They have excellent convictions. They delight in extinguishment.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anuttaraṁ sītibhāvaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities can realize supreme coolness.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.86
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.86

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Āvaraṇasutta
segs.e: Obstacles

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with six qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kammāvaraṇatāya samannāgato hoti, kilesāvaraṇatāya samannāgato hoti, vipākāvaraṇatāya samannāgato hoti, assaddho ca hoti, acchandiko ca, duppañño ca.
segs.e: They’re obstructed by deeds, defilements, or results. And they’re faithless, unenthusiastic, and witless.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with six qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Na kammāvaraṇatāya samannāgato hoti, na kilesāvaraṇatāya samannāgato hoti, na vipākāvaraṇatāya samannāgato hoti, saddho ca hoti, chandiko ca, paññavā ca.
segs.e: They’re not obstructed by deeds, defilements, or results. And they’re faithful, enthusiastic, and wise.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattan”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.87
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.87

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Voropitasutta
segs.e: A Murderer

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with six qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Mātā jīvitā voropitā hoti, pitā jīvitā voropito hoti, arahaṁ jīvitā voropito hoti, tathāgatassa duṭṭhena cittena lohitaṁ uppāditaṁ hoti, saṅgho bhinno hoti, duppañño hoti jaḷo eḷamūgo.
segs.e: They murder their mother or father or a perfected one. They maliciously shed the blood of a Realized One. They cause a schism in the Saṅgha. They’re witless, dull, and idiotic.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with six qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Na mātā jīvitā voropitā hoti, na pitā jīvitā voropito hoti, na arahaṁ jīvitā voropito hoti, na tathāgatassa duṭṭhena cittena lohitaṁ uppāditaṁ hoti, na saṅgho bhinno hoti, paññavā hoti ajaḷo aneḷamūgo.
segs.e: They don’t murder their mother or father or a perfected one. They don’t maliciously shed the blood of a Realized One. They don’t cause a schism in the Saṅgha. They’re wise, bright, and clever.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattan”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.88
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.88

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Sussūsatisutta
segs.e: Wanting to Listen

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with six qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne na sussūsati, na sotaṁ odahati, na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhāpeti, anatthaṁ gaṇhāti, atthaṁ riñcati, ananulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: When the teaching and practice proclaimed by the Realized One is being taught they don’t want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand. They learn the incorrect meaning and neglect the correct meaning. They accept views that contradict the teaching.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with six qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne sussūsati, sotaṁ odahati, aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhāpeti, atthaṁ gaṇhāti, anatthaṁ riñcati, anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: When the teaching and practice proclaimed by the Realized One is being taught they want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand. They learn the correct meaning and neglect the incorrect meaning. They accept views that conform with the teaching.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattan”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these six qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.”

segs.p: Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.89
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.89

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Appahāyasutta
segs.e: Not Giving Up

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo diṭṭhisampadaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up six things you can’t become accomplished in view.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṁ, vicikicchaṁ, sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ rāgaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ dosaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ mohaṁ.
segs.e: Substantialist view, doubt, misapprehension of precepts and observances, and forms of greed, hate, and delusion that lead to rebirth in places of loss.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo diṭṭhisampadaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six things you can’t become accomplished in view.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo diṭṭhisampadaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up six things you can become accomplished in view.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṁ, vicikicchaṁ, sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ rāgaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ dosaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ mohaṁ.
segs.e: Substantialist view, doubt, misapprehension of precepts and observances, and forms of greed, hate, and delusion that lead to rebirth in places of loss.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo diṭṭhisampadaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six things you can become accomplished in view.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.90
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.90

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Pahīnasutta
segs.e: Given Up

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an individual accomplished in view has given up these six things.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso, apāyagamanīyo rāgo, apāyagamanīyo doso, apāyagamanīyo moho.
segs.e: Substantialist view, doubt, misapprehension of precepts and observances, and forms of greed, hate, and delusion that lead to rebirth in places of loss.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhammā diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā”ti.
segs.e: An individual accomplished in view has given up these six things.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.91
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.91

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Abhabbasutta
segs.e: Can’t Give Rise

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo uppādetuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an individual accomplished in view can’t give rise to six things.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṁ, vicikicchaṁ, sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ rāgaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ dosaṁ, apāyagamanīyaṁ mohaṁ.
segs.e: Substantialist view, doubt, misapprehension of precepts and observances, and forms of greed, hate, and delusion that lead to rebirth in places of loss.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo uppādetun”ti.
segs.e: An individual accomplished in view can’t give rise to these six things.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.92
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.92

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Paṭhamaabhabbaṭṭhānasutta
segs.e: Things That Can’t Be Done (1st)

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, abhabbaṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six things can’t be done.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo satthari agāravo viharituṁ appatisso, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo dhamme agāravo viharituṁ appatisso, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo saṅghe agāravo viharituṁ appatisso, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sikkhāya agāravo viharituṁ appatisso, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo anāgamanīyaṁ vatthuṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo aṭṭhamaṁ bhavaṁ nibbattetuṁ.
segs.e: An individual accomplished in view can’t live disrespectful and irreverent toward the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, or the training. They can’t establish their belief on unreliable grounds. And they can’t generate an eighth rebirth.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha abhabbaṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six things that can’t be done.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.93
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.93

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Dutiyaabhabbaṭṭhānasutta
segs.e: Things That Can’t Be Done (2nd)

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, abhabbaṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six things can’t be done.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṁ niccato upagantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṁ sukhato upagantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci dhammaṁ attato upagantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo ānantariyaṁ kammaṁ kātuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kotūhalamaṅgalena suddhiṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo ito bahiddhā dakkhiṇeyyaṁ gavesituṁ.
segs.e: An individual accomplished in view can’t take conditions to be permanent. They cannot take conditions to be happiness. They cannot take anything to be the self. They can’t do deeds with fixed result in the next life. They can’t fall back on purification through boisterous, superstitious rites. They can’t seek outside of the Buddhist community for those worthy of religious donations.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha abhabbaṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six things that can’t be done.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.94
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.94

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Tatiyaabhabbaṭṭhānasutta
segs.e: Things That Can’t Be Done (3rd)

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, abhabbaṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six things can’t be done.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo mātaraṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo pitaraṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo arahantaṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo tathāgatassa duṭṭhena cittena lohitaṁ uppādetuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo saṅghaṁ bhindituṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo aññaṁ satthāraṁ uddisituṁ.
segs.e: An individual accomplished in view can’t murder their mother or father or a perfected one. They can’t maliciously shed the blood of the Realized One. They can’t cause a schism in the Saṅgha. They can’t dedicate themselves to another teacher.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha abhabbaṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six things that can’t be done.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.95
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.95

segs.p: 9. Sītivagga
segs.e: 9. Coolness

segs.p: Catutthaabhabbaṭṭhānasutta
segs.e: Things That Can’t Be Done (4th)

segs.p: “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, abhabbaṭṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these six things can’t be done.

segs.p: Katamāni cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sayaṅkataṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo paraṅkataṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca sukhadukkhaṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo asayaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paccāgantuṁ, abhabbo diṭṭhisampanno puggalo asayaṅkārañca aparaṅkārañca adhiccasamuppannaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ paccāgantuṁ.
segs.e: An individual accomplished in view can’t fall back on the idea that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, or that they’re made by another, or that they’re made by both. Nor can they fall back on the idea that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself, by another, or by both.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hissa, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa hetu ca sudiṭṭho hetusamuppannā ca dhammā.
segs.e: It is because an individual accomplished in view has clearly seen causes and the phenomena that arise from causes.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha abhabbaṭṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the six things that can’t be done.”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Sītivaggo navamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Sītibhāvaṁ āvaraṇaṁ,
voropitā sussūsati;
Appahāya pahīnābhabbo,
taṭṭhānā caturopi cāti.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.96
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.96

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Pātubhāvasutta
segs.e: Appearance

segs.p: “Channaṁ, bhikkhave, pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the appearance of six things is rare in the world.

segs.p: Katamesaṁ channaṁ?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desetā puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ, ariyāyatane paccājāti dullabhā lokasmiṁ, indriyānaṁ avekallatā dullabhā lokasmiṁ, ajaḷatā aneḷamūgatā dullabhā lokasmiṁ, kusale dhamme chando dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: A Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha. A teacher of the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One. Rebirth in a civilized region. Unimpaired sense faculties. Being bright and clever. Enthusiasm for skillful qualities.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, channaṁ pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: The appearance of these six things is rare in the world.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.97
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.97

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Ānisaṁsasutta
segs.e: Benefit

segs.p: “Chayime, bhikkhave, ānisaṁsā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these are the six benefits of realizing the fruit of stream-entry.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Saddhammaniyato hoti, aparihānadhammo hoti, pariyantakatassa dukkhaṁ hoti, asādhāraṇena ñāṇena samannāgato hoti, hetu cassa sudiṭṭho, hetusamuppannā ca dhammā.
segs.e: You’re bound for the true teaching. You’re not liable to decline. You suffer only for a limited period. You have distinct knowledge. You’ve clearly seen causes and the phenomena that arise from causes.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha ānisaṁsā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the six benefits of realizing the fruit of stream-entry.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.98
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.98

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Aniccasutta
segs.e: Impermanence

segs.p: “‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kañci saṅkhāraṁ niccato samanupassanto anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato bhavissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible for a mendicant who regards any condition as permanent to accept views that conform with the teaching.

segs.p: ‘Anulomikāya khantiyā asamannāgato sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without accepting views that conform with the teaching, it’s impossible to step into the sure path.

segs.p: ‘Sammattaniyāmaṁ anokkamamāno sotāpattiphalaṁ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṁ vā anāgāmiphalaṁ vā arahattaṁ vā sacchikarissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Without stepping into the sure path, it’s impossible to realize the fruit of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, or perfection.

segs.p: ‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbasaṅkhāre aniccato samanupassanto anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato bhavissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s quite possible for a mendicant who regards all conditions as impermanent to accept views that conform with the teaching.

segs.p: ‘Anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: Having accepted views that conform with the teaching, it’s possible to step into the sure path.

segs.p: ‘Sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamamāno sotāpattiphalaṁ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṁ vā anāgāmiphalaṁ vā arahattaṁ vā sacchikarissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: Having stepped into the sure path, it’s possible to realize the fruit of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, or perfection.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.99
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.99

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Dukkhasutta
segs.e: Suffering

segs.p: “So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kañci saṅkhāraṁ sukhato samanupassanto …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible for a mendicant who regards any condition as pleasurable to accept views that agree with the teaching. …

segs.p: sabbasaṅkhāre dukkhato samanupassanto …pe…
segs.e: It’s quite possible for a mendicant who regards all conditions as suffering to accept views that agree with the teaching. …”

segs.p: ṭhānametaṁ vijjati”.
Catutthaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.100
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.100

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Anattasutta
segs.e: Not-Self

segs.p: “So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kañci dhammaṁ attato samanupassanto …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible for a mendicant who regards any thing as self to accept views that agree with the teaching. …

segs.p: sabbadhamme anattato samanupassanto …pe…
segs.e: It’s quite possible for a mendicant who regards all things as not-self to accept views that agree with the teaching. …”

segs.p: ṭhānametaṁ vijjati”.
Pañcamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.101
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.101

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Nibbānasutta
segs.e: Extinguished

segs.p: “‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nibbānaṁ dukkhato samanupassanto anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato bhavissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible for a mendicant who regards extinguishment as suffering to accept views that conform with the teaching. …

segs.p: ‘Anulomikāya khantiyā asamannāgato sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
‘Sammattaniyāmaṁ anokkamamāno sotāpattiphalaṁ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṁ vā anāgāmiphalaṁ vā arahattaṁ vā sacchikarissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
‘So vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nibbānaṁ sukhato samanupassanto anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato bhavissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It’s quite possible for a mendicant who regards extinguishment as pleasurable to accept views that conform with the teaching. …”

segs.p: ‘Anulomikāya khantiyā samannāgato sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
‘Sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamamāno sotāpattiphalaṁ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṁ vā anāgāmiphalaṁ vā arahattaṁ vā sacchikarissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
Chaṭṭhaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.102
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.102

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Anavatthitasutta
segs.e: Transience

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, ānisaṁse sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā sabbasaṅkhāresu anodhiṁ karitvā aniccasaññaṁ upaṭṭhāpetuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, seeing six benefits is quite enough to establish the perception of impermanence in all conditions without qualification.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: ‘Sabbasaṅkhārā ca me anavatthitā khāyissanti, sabbaloke ca me mano nābhiramissati, sabbalokā ca me mano vuṭṭhahissati, nibbānapoṇañca me mānasaṁ bhavissati, saṁyojanā ca me pahānaṁ gacchissanti, paramena ca sāmaññena samannāgato bhavissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘All conditions will appear to me as transient.’ ‘My mind will not delight anywhere in the world.’ ‘My mind will rise above the whole world.’ ‘My heart will incline to extinguishment.’ ‘My fetters will be given up.’ ‘I will achieve the ultimate goal of the ascetic life.’

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha ānisaṁse sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā sabbasaṅkhāresu anodhiṁ karitvā aniccasaññaṁ upaṭṭhāpetun”ti.
segs.e: Seeing these six benefits is quite enough to establish the perception of impermanence in all conditions without qualification.”

segs.p: Sattamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.103
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.103

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Ukkhittāsikasutta
segs.e: With a Drawn Sword

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, ānisaṁse sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā sabbasaṅkhāresu anodhiṁ karitvā dukkhasaññaṁ upaṭṭhāpetuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, seeing six benefits is quite enough to establish the perception of suffering in all conditions without qualification.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: ‘Sabbasaṅkhāresu ca me nibbidasaññā paccupaṭṭhitā bhavissati, seyyathāpi ukkhittāsike vadhake.
segs.e: ‘Perception of disillusionment will be established in me for all conditions, like a killer with a drawn sword.’

segs.p: Sabbalokā ca me mano vuṭṭhahissati, nibbāne ca santadassāvī bhavissāmi, anusayā ca me samugghātaṁ gacchissanti, kiccakārī ca bhavissāmi, satthā ca me pariciṇṇo bhavissati mettāvatāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘My mind will rise above the whole world.’ ‘I will see extinguishment as peaceful.’ ‘My underlying tendencies will be uprooted.’ ‘I will fulfill my duty.’ ‘I will have served my Teacher with love.’

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha ānisaṁse sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā sabbasaṅkhāresu anodhiṁ karitvā dukkhasaññaṁ upaṭṭhāpetun”ti.
segs.e: Seeing these six benefits is quite enough to establish the perception of suffering in all conditions without qualification.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.104
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.104

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Atammayasutta
segs.e: Not Determined by Anything

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, ānisaṁse sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā sabbadhammesu anodhiṁ karitvā anattasaññaṁ upaṭṭhāpetuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, seeing six benefits is quite enough to establish the perception of not-self in all things without qualification.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Sabbaloke ca atammayo bhavissāmi, ahaṅkārā ca me uparujjhissanti, mamaṅkārā ca me uparujjhissanti, asādhāraṇena ca ñāṇena samannāgato bhavissāmi, hetu ca me sudiṭṭho bhavissati, hetusamuppannā ca dhammā.
segs.e: ‘I will not be determined by anything in the world.’ ‘My I-making will stop.’ ‘My mine-making will stop.’ ‘I will have distinct knowledge.’ ‘I will clearly see causes and the phenomena that arise from causes.’

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha ānisaṁse sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā sabbadhammesu anodhiṁ karitvā anattasaññaṁ upaṭṭhāpetun”ti.
segs.e: Seeing these six benefits is quite enough to establish the perception of not-self in all things without qualification.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.105
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.105

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Bhavasutta
segs.e: States of Existence

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, bhavā pahātabbā, tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should give up these three states of existence. And you should train in three trainings.

segs.p: Katame tayo bhavā pahātabbā?
segs.e: What are the three states of existence you should give up?

segs.p: Kāmabhavo, rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo—
segs.e: Existence in the sensual realm, the realm of luminous form, and the formless realm.

segs.p: ime tayo bhavā pahātabbā.
segs.e: These are the three states of existence you should give up.

segs.p: Katamāsu tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhitabbaṁ?
segs.e: What are the three trainings you should train in?

segs.p: Adhisīlasikkhāya, adhicittasikkhāya, adhipaññāsikkhāya—
segs.e: The training in the higher ethics, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom.

segs.p: imāsu tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: These are the three trainings you should train in.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ime tayo bhavā pahīnā honti, imāsu ca tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhitasikkho hoti—
segs.e: When a mendicant has given up these three states of existence and has trained in these three trainings

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā”ti.
segs.e: they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.106
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.106

segs.p: 10. Ānisaṁsavagga
segs.e: 10. Benefit

segs.p: Taṇhāsutta
segs.e: Craving

segs.p: “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, taṇhā pahātabbā, tayo ca mānā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should give up these three cravings and three conceits.

segs.p: Katamā tisso taṇhā pahātabbā?
segs.e: What three cravings should you give up?

segs.p: Kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā—
segs.e: Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence.

segs.p: imā tisso taṇhā pahātabbā.
segs.e: These are the three cravings you should give up.

segs.p: Katame tayo mānā pahātabbā?
segs.e: What three conceits should you give up?

segs.p: Māno, omāno, atimāno—
segs.e: Conceit, inferiority complex, and superiority complex.

segs.p: ime tayo mānā pahātabbā.
segs.e: These are the three conceits you should give up.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno imā tisso taṇhā pahīnā honti, ime ca tayo mānā;
segs.e: When a mendicant has given up these three cravings and these three conceits

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā”ti.
segs.e: they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.
Ānisaṁsavaggo dasamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Pātubhāvo ānisaṁso,
aniccadukkhaanattato;
Nibbānaṁ anavatthi,
ukkhittāsi atammayo;
Bhavā taṇhāyekā dasāti.
Dutiyo paṇṇāsako samatto.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.107
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.107

segs.p: 11. Tikavagga
segs.e: 11. Triads

segs.p: Rāgasutta
segs.e: Greed

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Rāgo, doso, moho.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Rāgassa pahānāya asubhā bhāvetabbā, dosassa pahānāya mettā bhāvetabbā, mohassa pahānāya paññā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop the perception of ugliness to give up greed, love to give up hate, and wisdom to give up delusion.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.108
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.108

segs.p: 11. Tikavagga
segs.e: 11. Triads

segs.p: Duccaritasutta
segs.e: Bad Conduct

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāyaduccaritaṁ, vacīduccaritaṁ, manoduccaritaṁ.
segs.e: Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāyaduccaritassa pahānāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāvetabbaṁ, vacīduccaritassa pahānāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāvetabbaṁ, manoduccaritassa pahānāya manosucaritaṁ bhāvetabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should develop good bodily conduct to give up bad bodily conduct, good verbal conduct to give up bad verbal conduct, and good mental conduct to give up bad mental conduct.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.109
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.109

segs.p: 11. Tikavagga
segs.e: 11. Triads

segs.p: Vitakkasutta
segs.e: Thoughts

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṁsāvitakko.
segs.e: Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāmavitakkassa pahānāya nekkhammavitakko bhāvetabbo, byāpādavitakkassa pahānāya abyāpādavitakko bhāvetabbo, vihiṁsāvitakkassa pahānāya avihiṁsāvitakko bhāvetabbo.
segs.e: You should develop thoughts of renunciation to give up sensual thoughts, thoughts of good will to give up malicious thoughts, and thoughts of harmlessness to give up cruel thoughts.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.110
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.110

segs.e: 11. Triads

segs.p: Saññāsutta
segs.e: Perceptions

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāmasaññā, byāpādasaññā, vihiṁsāsaññā.
segs.e: Sensual, malicious, and cruel perceptions.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāmasaññāya pahānāya nekkhammasaññā bhāvetabbā, byāpādasaññāya pahānāya abyāpādasaññā bhāvetabbā, vihiṁsāsaññāya pahānāya avihiṁsāsaññā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop perceptions of renunciation to give up sensual perceptions, perceptions of good will to give up malicious perceptions, and perceptions of harmlessness to give up cruel perceptions.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.111
segs.e: Numbered Discourses 6.111

segs.p: 11. Tikavagga
segs.e: 11. Triads

segs.p: Dhātusutta
segs.e: Elements

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāmadhātu, byāpādadhātu, vihiṁsādhātu.
segs.e: The elements of sensuality, malice, and cruelty.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Kāmadhātuyā pahānāya nekkhammadhātu bhāvetabbā, byāpādadhātuyā pahānāya abyāpādadhātu bhāvetabbā, vihiṁsādhātuyā pahānāya avihiṁsādhātu bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop the element of renunciation to give up the element of sensuality, the element of good will to give up the element of malice, and the element of harmlessness to give up the element of cruelty.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Assādasutta
segs.e: Gratification

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Assādadiṭṭhi, attānudiṭṭhi, micchādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: The view that things are gratifying, the theory of self, and wrong view.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Assādadiṭṭhiyā pahānāya aniccasaññā bhāvetabbā, attānudiṭṭhiyā pahānāya anattasaññā bhāvetabbā, micchādiṭṭhiyā pahānāya sammādiṭṭhi bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop the perception of impermanence to give up the view that things are gratifying; the perception of not-self to give up the theory of self; and right view to give up wrong view.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Aratisutta
segs.e: Discontent

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Arati, vihiṁsā, adhammacariyā.
segs.e: Discontent, cruelty, and unprincipled conduct.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Aratiyā pahānāya muditā bhāvetabbā, vihiṁsāya pahānāya avihiṁsā bhāvetabbā, adhammacariyāya pahānāya dhammacariyā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop rejoicing to give up discontent, harmlessness to give up cruelty, and principled conduct to give up unprincipled conduct.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Santuṭṭhitāsutta
segs.e: Contentment

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Asantuṭṭhitā, asampajaññaṁ, mahicchatā.
segs.e: Lack of contentment, lack of situational awareness, and having many wishes.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Asantuṭṭhitāya pahānāya santuṭṭhitā bhāvetabbā, asampajaññassa pahānāya sampajaññaṁ bhāvetabbaṁ, mahicchatāya pahānāya appicchatā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop contentment to give up lack of contentment, situational awareness to give up lack of situational awareness, and having few wishes to give up having many wishes.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Dovacassatāsutta
segs.e: Hard to Admonish

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Dovacassatā, pāpamittatā, cetaso vikkhepo.
segs.e: Being hard to admonish, bad friendship, and a scattered mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Dovacassatāya pahānāya sovacassatā bhāvetabbā, pāpamittatāya pahānāya kalyāṇamittatā bhāvetabbā, cetaso vikkhepassa pahānāya ānāpānassati bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: You should develop being easy to admonish to give up being hard to admonish, good friendship to give up bad friendship, and mindfulness of breathing to give up a scattered mind.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”
