segs.p: Uddhaccasutta
segs.e: Restlessness

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Uddhaccaṁ, asaṁvaro, pamādo.
segs.e: Restlessness, lack of restraint, and negligence.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā.
segs.e: These are the three things.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: To give up these three things you should develop three things.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Uddhaccassa pahānāya samatho bhāvetabbo, asaṁvarassa pahānāya saṁvaro bhāvetabbo, pamādassa pahānāya appamādo bhāvetabbo.
segs.e: You should develop serenity to give up restlessness, restraint to give up lack of restraint, and diligence to give up negligence.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya ime tayo dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three things you should develop to give up those three things.”

segs.p: Kāyānupassīsutta
segs.e: Observing the Body

segs.p: “Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo kāye kāyānupassī viharituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up these six qualities you can’t meditate observing an aspect of the body.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kammārāmataṁ, bhassārāmataṁ, niddārāmataṁ, saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ, indriyesu aguttadvārataṁ, bhojane amattaññutaṁ.
segs.e: Relishing work, talk, sleep, and company, not guarding the sense doors, and eating too much.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme appahāya abhabbo kāye kāyānupassī viharituṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these six qualities you can’t meditate observing an aspect of the body.

segs.p: Cha, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo kāye kāyānupassī viharituṁ.
segs.e: But after giving up these six qualities you can meditate observing an aspect of the body.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Kammārāmataṁ, bhassārāmataṁ, niddārāmataṁ, saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ, indriyesu aguttadvārataṁ, bhojane amattaññutaṁ.
segs.e: Relishing work, talk, sleep, and company, not guarding the sense doors, and eating too much.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha dhamme pahāya bhabbo kāye kāyānupassī viharitun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these six qualities you can meditate observing an aspect of the body.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Tapussasutta
segs.e: About Tapussa

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato tapusso gahapati tathāgate niṭṭhaṅgato amataddaso amataṁ sacchikatvā iriyati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, having six qualities the householder Tapussa is certain about the Realized One, sees freedom from death  and lives having realized freedom from death.

segs.p: Katamehi chahi?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Buddhe aveccappasādena, dhamme aveccappasādena, saṅghe aveccappasādena, ariyena sīlena, ariyena ñāṇena, ariyāya vimuttiyā.
segs.e: Experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and noble ethics, knowledge, and freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato tapusso gahapati tathāgate niṭṭhaṅgato amataddaso amataṁ sacchikatvā iriyatī”ti.
segs.e: Having these six qualities the householder Tapussa is certain about the Realized One, sees freedom from death and lives having realized freedom from death.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.

segs.e: 13. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (1st)

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya cha dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “For insight into greed, six things should be developed.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ, anussatānuttariyaṁ.
segs.e: The unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime cha dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these six things should be developed.”

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya cha dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “For insight into greed, six things should be developed.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Buddhānussati, dhammānussati, saṅghānussati, sīlānussati, cāgānussati, devatānussati.
segs.e: The recollection of the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, ethics, generosity, and the deities.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime cha dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these six things should be developed.”

segs.e: 13. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (3rd)

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya cha dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “For insight into greed, six things should be developed.

segs.p: Katame cha?
segs.e: What six?

segs.p: Aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā.
segs.e: The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime cha dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these six things should be developed.”
